justification_text: D1 (randomization process): low. Permuted blocks of random size, stratified by center and Disease Risk Index (low/int/high or very high). Allocation concealment via NHLBI-appointed processes. Baseline characteristics well balanced (Table 1). D2 (deviations from intended interventions): low. 11/431 (2.6%) did not receive intended conditioning; treatment adherence detailed in Table S5. ITT analysis pre-specified. D3 (missing outcome data): low. Only 20/431 (4.6%) had <12 mo follow-up; primary endpoint assessable for all. D4 (measurement of outcome): some concerns. Open-label (no placebo or blinding feasible for GVHD prophylaxis regimens); GVHD assessors not blinded. GVHD grading (Mount Sinai/MAGIC) and NIH 2014 criteria are standardized but outcome assessors not formally blinded. D5 (selection of reported result): low. Protocol available; primary endpoint pre-specified; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03959241 registered. Overall: some_concerns due to lack of blinded outcome assessment.

CIBMTR registry analysis with large sample (n=2765) and pre-specified multivariable adjustment. D1 (confounding): moderate — unmeasured confounders include center-specific prophylaxis/surveillance protocols, letermovir use (era spans 2012-2017 pre/post FDA approval Nov 2017), antifungal/antibacterial prophylaxis; reasons for haplo donor selection or PTCy in sibling transplant not captured. D2 (selection of participants): moderate — study restricted to centers reporting both HaploCy and SibCNI patients, reducing center bias but not eliminating it. D3 (classification of interventions): low — GVHD prophylaxis intervention well-defined and recorded prospectively on CIBMTR forms. D4 (deviations): low — observational; no protocol-driven intervention. D5 (missing data): moderate — substantial missing immune reconstitution data (78%), CD3+ cell dose missing in ~45%, no data on prophylaxis or preemptive thresholds. D6 (measurement of outcome): moderate — no data on viral load thresholds, diagnostic methodology, or treatment of CMV; ascertainment depends on center-reported infection forms. D7 (selection of reported result): low — pre-specified analyses with composite variables and full multivariable results reported.

Retrospective single-center cohort, BRAIN database supplemented by chart review. D1 (confounding): MODERATE - 4 prophylaxis groups differed in age, KPS, disease, graft source, sex matching; multivariable Cox/Fine-Gray adjustment performed for survival outcomes but not for infection density. D2 (selection): MODERATE - consecutive eligible patients but exclusions for clinical trial regimens and rituximab. D3 (classification of interventions): LOW - GVHD prophylaxis regimen clearly documented. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): MODERATE - immune suppression duration differed by regimen, exact stop dates not captured (acknowledged limitation). D5 (missing data): LOW for infections (all patients); MODERATE for immune reconstitution (~50% had FCM data) - but immune reconstitution not used here. D6 (measurement of outcomes): LOW - standardized CMV PCR threshold and weekly screening through D+100; uniform infection ascertainment. D7 (selection of reported result): MODERATE - infection density a pre-specified primary endpoint; multiple time-window analyses reported but pre-specified per methods.

Retrospective single-center study with non-random group allocation by donor type and GvHD prophylaxis era. D1 (confounding): serious — substantial confounding by donor type (haplo/MM vs MRD vs MUD), conditioning intensity differences (e.g., MAC: 7% PTCY vs 20% MRD vs 17% MUD vs 26% MM), Karnofsky differences (p<0.05), and especially temporal/era confounding because centre practice switched from ATLG to PTCY in MM grafts over 2015-2022 — meaning PTCY patients more likely received letermovir (approved 2017) than earlier MM/ATLG patients. D2 (selection): serious — inclusion based on retrospective database with non-randomized allocation. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — GvHD prophylaxis well-defined and homogeneous within groups (ATLG-Grafalon 30 mg/kg fixed, PTCY 50 mg/kg D+3,4 fixed). D4 (deviations from intended interventions): moderate — no clear deviations described. D5 (missing data): low — single-center database appears complete; outcomes systematically extracted. D6 (measurement of outcomes): low — outcomes objective (BSI by culture, CMV by PCR threshold, GVHD per standardized criteria, OS). D7 (reporting): low — all pre-specified groups and outcomes reported with full tables. Overall: serious risk of confounding given era effects on letermovir use and antifungal practice; reasonable internal consistency otherwise.

Non-randomized prospective trial with historical control (2010-2013 ATG) compared to prospective PTCy cohort (2013-2015). D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - historical control with secular trends, potential improvements in supportive care over 2010-2015 period; multivariate adjustment performed but residual confounding likely. D2 (selection): moderate - 86/200 trial patients selected based on diagnosis/graft source; consecutive historical controls reasonably selected. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate - intervention well-defined per arm. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low - protocols specified. D5 (missing data): moderate - infectious complication denominators inconsistent; follow-up shorter in PTCy (12 vs 17 mo median). D6 (measurement of outcomes): low - standardized criteria (NIH, Consensus Conference, EORTC/MSG). D7 (reported result selection): moderate - multiple comparisons not adjusted (acknowledged in paper). Overall: SERIOUS risk of bias due to historical control design and uneven follow-up.

Retrospective CIBMTR registry analysis. D1 (confounding): moderate -- key confounders included in multivariable models but antifungal prophylaxis and corticosteroid exposure not captured. D2 (selection): moderate -- restricted to centers reporting both HaploCy and SibCNI, but choice of donor type and GVHD prophylaxis is at center discretion (treatment-confounded selection). D3 (classification of interventions): serious -- FI diagnoses reported by site, NOT standardized by EORTC/MSG criteria; >50% of yeast FI from non-sterile sites; no central adjudication. Risk of misclassification differential across cohorts due to varying surveillance practices. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): moderate -- antifungal prophylaxis data missing for the entire study period (pre-2017 CIBMTR did not capture). D6 (outcome measurement): low for the registry data. D7 (selective reporting): low. Overall: serious due to non-standardized FI ascertainment and missing key confounders.

Single-center retrospective cohort with substantial confounding by indication: PTCy was selectively used for alternative donor sources (haplo, MMUD) and increasingly in later era (2018-2021, 65% PTCy vs 25% non-PTCy), while non-PTCy arm was predominantly MSD (56.1%) and earlier era (74.6% from 2014-2017). Donor type and era differ markedly between arms (D1: moderate-serious confounding). Selection into PTCy was protocol-driven by donor type, not patient characteristics (D2: serious selection bias — institutional shift means PTCy and non-PTCy reflect different transplant strategies, not contemporaneous comparison). BSI ascertainment was via clinical chart review with explicit verbatim definition and uniform microbiology lab — low concern for measurement bias (D4-D5). Multivariable models adjust for donor type, conditioning, era, age, KPS but residual confounding by indication remains. Authors acknowledge retrospective design and lack of ATG as limitations.

Retrospective CIBMTR registry analysis with potential selection bias (patients selected for certain donor/GVHD prophylaxis approaches based on clinical judgment and donor availability). Multivariable adjustment for known confounders (DRI, HCT-CI, age, race/ethnicity, CMV serostatus, year of HCT) but residual confounding likely (D1, D2). Donor selection bias acknowledged by authors. Standard CIBMTR data collection used for outcomes (D3-D5 low). Reporting complete (D6-D7 low).

Single-arm retrospective national registry analysis (ABMTRR) with no comparator arm; confounding cannot be assessed against an internal control (D1 serious). Selection into the cohort is defined by registry inclusion criteria with all eligible patients included, limiting selection bias (D2 low). Disease risk index not assigned for 20.5% of patients and HLA matching 'not available' for 36.3% (D3 moderate). Intervention is uniform (PTCy + PB + haplo) per protocol (D4 low). Some outcome ascertainment depends on center-level reporting with limited central adjudication, especially cGVHD grading by centers (D5/D6 moderate). Selective reporting risk low; primary endpoints clearly pre-specified (D7 low). Overall serious risk of bias due to single-arm design and missing covariates. Study is protocol-excluded from quantitative synthesis but retained for PRISMA tracking.

Post-hoc subgroup analysis of BMT CTN 1703 RCT (parent trial: low RoB). D1 (randomization) - low, inherited from parent RCT 1:1 stratified randomization. D2 (deviations from intended interventions) - low, ITT analysis for primary endpoint, transplanted population for secondary. D3 (missing outcome data) - low. D4 (measurement of outcome) - low, standardized BMT CTN ascertainment. D5 (selection of reported result) - some_concerns: this is an unprespecified post-hoc age subgroup with small N (n=96, PTCy n=43 vs Tac/MTX n=53), wide CIs, and multiple secondary endpoints reported; subgroup not pre-powered and selective reporting risk elevated. Overall: some_concerns.
Single-arm descriptive paper with no non-PTCy comparator; protocol-excluded from primary analysis. RoB not formally assessed.

Retrospective single-center cohort, consecutive patients (good for selection), but baseline confounding present (older patients had more RIC, more myeloid disease, older donors). Study tracked for PRISMA but excluded from primary analysis (single_arm_descriptive_excluded: no PTCy-vs-comparator contrast; age subgroup analysis only).

Large CIBMTR registry comparison of haplo/PTCy vs MSD/CNI in cHL. Confounding (d1): moderate — important baseline differences (graft source 70% BM vs 4% BM, 14% ATG/alemtuzumab in MSD, prior auto-HCT 84% vs 73%, conditioning intensity, race) addressed via multivariate Cox/logistic regression but residual confounding likely (immune reconstitution kinetics, salvage regimens, checkpoint inhibitor exposure not captured). Selection (d2): moderate — eligibility consecutive registry reporting but ex vivo TCD excluded; overlap with Kanate 2016/Ghosh 2016 noted. Classification (d3): low — registry definitions standardized. Deviations (d4): low — observational. Missing data (d5): moderate — some baseline missingness (HCT-CI, race), some outcomes with missing assessments. Outcome measurement (d6): low — standard CIBMTR endpoints with cumulative incidence and competing risks. Reporting (d7): low — all pre-specified outcomes reported.

D1 (confounding): serious — retrospective non-randomized comparison of FMTBI (2023+) vs FB historical control (2017-2022) with substantial temporal confounding (evolving practice, supportive care, MRD monitoring availability changed mid-cohort). FMTBI group also significantly older (median 59 vs 48 yr) and had longer time to HCT. D2 (selection): moderate — consecutive patients but FMTBI all from 2023 onward, FB from 2017-2022, no overlap in time. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — regimen labels are clear but ATG dose also differs (4.5 vs 6.0 mg/kg), confounding PTCy effect. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): moderate — MRD monitoring was unavailable for many earlier-era Ph-negative ALL patients. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — clinical outcomes objective but no blinding, GVHD grading system not specified. D7 (selection of reported result): moderate — focus on favorable DFS/relapse endpoints; infection outcomes not reported in detail. Overall: serious risk of bias dominated by temporal confounding and small sample.

Single-center retrospective comparison of ATG+PTCy vs heterogeneous mixed comparator (alemtuzumab+CsA, MMF+CsA, MTX+CsA, ATG+MTX+CsA, ATG alone). D1 (confounding): serious — strong confounding by conditioning intensity (100% RIC in ATG+PTCy vs 37% RIC in comparator), donor type, and treatment era; multivariable adjustment partial. D2 (selection): serious — non-randomized allocation by treating physician/protocol over time; ATG+PTCy likely later in study period. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate — well-defined regimens but heterogeneous comparator pools 5 different regimens. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): low. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate — investigator-defined GvHD grading, no central review noted. D7 (reporting): low. Overall judgement: serious due to D1 and D2.

Prospective phase II single-arm trial with matched historical/contemporaneous cohort comparison. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - matched cohort drawn from institutional database with limited matching variables (age, diagnosis, disease status, donor, graft, ATG); residual confounding likely (notably graft source mismatch - more PB in Tac/MTX controls; mixed RIC regimens Bu/Flu vs Flu/Mel; protocol amendment removing ATG mid-trial creating intra-arm heterogeneity). D2 (selection): MODERATE - 12/49 PTCy patients could not be matched (mostly post-amendment no-ATG MUD patients); only 37 matched analyzed, raising selection concern. D3 (classification of interventions): MODERATE - clear PTCy regimen but mixed ATG use within PTCy arm. D4 (deviations): LOW - prospective protocol followed, deviations documented. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - some incomplete reporting for arm characteristics. D6 (outcome measurement): LOW - standard MAGIC/Consensus/NIH grading, histologic confirmation, weekly CMV monitoring. D7 (selection of reported result): LOW - registered trial (NCT00800839) with pre-specified primary endpoint. Overall: SERIOUS due to confounding and selection in the comparative analysis.

Single-arm retrospective descriptive series (N=16) with no comparator arm; no PTCy contrast possible. Confounding domain serious due to absence of comparator and selection by clinician choice. Outcome measurement uses standard criteria (Modified Glucksberg, NIH 2014). Very small sample size and short follow-up limit inference. Single-arm descriptive paper excluded from primary analysis per protocol; tracked for PRISMA.

ROBINS-I: D1 (confounding) SERIOUS - registry-based retrospective comparison with marked baseline imbalances (year of HSCT, donor age, HCT-CI, stem cell source, MAC use, age distribution, CMV status all significantly different); multivariate models adjust for many but residual confounding likely (no center effects fully controlled; ATG dose/preparation - ATG vs ATLG - not distinguished). D2 (selection) MODERATE - eligibility defined by donor/prophylaxis choice which may be center-driven. D3 (intervention classification) LOW - donor and prophylaxis well-defined. D4 (deviations) LOW - registry, prophylaxis adherence not analyzed. D5 (missing data) MODERATE - notable missingness for donor age (44.2% in MUD arm), HCT-CI (33% MUD), and other covariates handled as separate category. D6 (measurement) LOW - standard registry definitions (EBMT). D7 (selective reporting) MODERATE - infection outcomes (CMV, IFI, BSI) not reported; analysis focuses on survival/GVHD endpoints. Overall: SERIOUS due to substantial confounding inherent to non-randomized cross-era cohort comparison and inability to disentangle PT-CY effect from ATG vs no-ATG in MUD arm.

Single-center retrospective cohort with regimen assignment by physician discretion. Significant baseline imbalances in age (P=.009), transplant type (P=.007), MRD status (P<.001), stem cell source (P<.001) and CD34/CD3 doses across the three arms. Confounding by indication likely (D1 serious). Selection issues moderate. Outcome measurement for severe cGVHD relies on investigator definition (systemic therapy initiated) rather than formal NIH 2014 grading. Small PTCy-alone arm (n=9). Limited adjustment (bivariate only).

Retrospective two-center study; treatment assignment (ATG vs PTCy) was largely determined by treating center (location A vs B). D1 (confounding): moderate—treatment confounded with center; baseline characteristics balanced but supportive care differences may persist (antibacterial prophylaxis in PTCy arm at center B for aGvHD). D2 (selection): moderate—consecutive patients but center-based allocation may introduce selection bias. D3 (intervention classification): low—protocols clearly documented. D4 (deviations): low—standardized GvHD diagnosis joint protocol. D5 (missing data): low—data from prospectively collected registries and medical records, minimum 12-month follow-up. D6 (outcome measurement): low—joint protocol across centers for diagnosing/staging GvHD. D7 (reporting): low—pre-specified primary endpoint, multivariate analyses reported.

Retrospective multicenter cohort comparing PTCy (3 centers, 2013-2018) to historical ATG-MTX-CsA controls (2 centers, 2010-2018). D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - calendar-period confounding (ATG cohort earlier; PTCy cohort partially overlapping), different centers used different regimens, three different PTCy backbones (CsA/MMF vs Tac/MMF vs Siro/MMF), two ATG doses (6 vs 2.5 mg/kg), MV adjusted for center but limited power. D2 (selection): MODERATE - consecutive patients reduces selection bias; minimum 6 mo follow-up requirement could exclude very early deaths. D3 (intervention classification): MODERATE - prophylaxis regimens well-documented but heterogeneous. D4 (deviations): LOW - GVHD prophylaxis is structured protocol. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - some retrospective data gaps; EBV only screened in ATG group introducing surveillance bias for that outcome. D6 (measurement of outcome): MODERATE - GVHD scored by clinical criteria (Glucksberg/NIH) but multicenter potential for grading variability; only 1 center used both regimens. D7 (selection of reported result): LOW - planned endpoints and CONSORT-like reporting. Overall: SERIOUS.

Retrospective multicenter cohort from GETH-TC database. D1 (confounding): serious; substantial imbalance between haplo and MSD/MUD groups in DRI (high/very high 67% vs 32%, p<.001), active disease at HSCT (20% vs 5%, p=.001), prior auto-HSCT (11% vs 2%, p=.010), and female-donor/male-recipient sex disparity. Multivariate adjustment for some confounders but residual confounding likely. D2 (selection): moderate; haplo arm drawn from 20 centers while MSD/MUD from only 3 centers using PTCy as standard, introducing center effect (acknowledged by authors). D3 (intervention classification): moderate; heterogeneous PTCy timing and adjunct IS in MSD/MUD (PTCy+3+4/CNI/MMF, PTCy+3+5/CNI no MMF, PTCy+3+4/Sir/MMF). D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low; participating centers asked to replace missing data. D6 (outcome measurement): low; standard MAGIC and NIH criteria. D7 (selective reporting): low; pre-specified primary endpoints and standard outcome panel. Overall: serious risk of bias due to confounding and selection.

Retrospective single-center cohort with non-randomized donor allocation (HAPLO assigned by URD unavailability). D1 (confounding): serious — major imbalance in conditioning regimens (Flu/Cy/TBI for HAPLO vs heterogeneous regimens for URD, most containing ATG) and GVHD prophylaxis (PTCy+Tac+MMF vs ATG+Tac+MTX/MMF). Disease risk balanced but no adjusted analysis. D2 (selection of participants): moderate — consecutive HAPLO patients with URD matched immediately before/after; 1 URD could serve as control for >1 HAPLO. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — conditioning and GVHD prophylaxis regimens well-defined but heterogeneous in URD arm. D4 (deviations): low — protocol-driven supportive care identical between arms. D5 (missing data): low — all 113 patients analyzed. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — clinical aGVHD/cGVHD assessment without blinding; infection surveillance protocols identical and prospective. D7 (selective reporting): low — standard outcomes reported. Overall: serious due to unbalanced confounding from conditioning/ATG differences.

Single-center retrospective cohort. D1 (confounding): moderate - significant baseline differences between PTCy and MTX arms (more haplo/MMUD, more high DRI, less MAC in PTCy); no propensity matching. D2 (selection): moderate - PTCy use determined by donor type and clinical factors. D3 (exposure classification): low. D4 (deviations from intended): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - some chimerism timepoints missing. D6 (measurement): moderate - chimerism measurement standardized. D7 (reporting): low. Study focus is chimerism kinetics, not infection/GVHD outcomes which are not reported.

Single-center retrospective study without prespecified protocol. D1 (confounding): serious — donor selection driven by availability and clinical factors; only partial adjustment via multivariate Cox/Fine-Gray; key confounders (CMV serostatus, disease risk index, conditioning intensity) not adjusted for. D2 (selection): moderate — consecutive ALL/AML patients but censoring at 3 years and arm-specific follow-up differences (haplo 18.2 mo vs MUD 60 mo) raises immortal-time concerns. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — donor type clearly defined. D4 (deviations): moderate — protocol changes over decade (haplo PTCy added in cohort). D5 (missing data): serious — exact time of GvHD onset not recorded for many patients, precluding CI calculation; CMV/BSI/IFI not reported. D6 (measurement): moderate — outcomes mostly objective. D7 (reporting): moderate — outcomes pre-specified in methods; small comparator arms (MMRD n=18) yield unstable estimates.

Retrospective single-center cohort comparing ATG/PTCy (2010-2020) vs historical ATG-only control (2008-2015) at Tehran HORCSCT. D1 (confounding) serious: era effect — comparator enrolled 5+ years earlier; supportive care, donor selection criteria, MRD methods evolved during the period; significant baseline imbalances in donor age, recipient CMV serostatus, and donor-recipient sex matching. D2 (selection) moderate: consecutive patients but allocation determined by treatment era. D3 (classification) moderate: GVHD prophylaxis allocation determined by era; potential misclassification by historical record review. D4 (deviations) low: protocol-defined regimens. D5 (missing data) moderate: incomplete MRD/cytogenetic info acknowledged by authors; immune reconstitution data absent. D6/D7 (outcome measurement, reporting) low: standardized Glucksberg/NIH criteria; outcomes pre-specified. Overall serious due to era confounding and baseline imbalances.

Retrospective single-center cohort comparing two consecutive era-stratified prophylaxis regimens (ATG/PTCy 2010-2020 vs ATG-only 2008-2015). D1 (confounding): moderate - era effect inherent given non-contemporaneous arms; donor age, recipient CMV status, sex matching differed significantly between arms; multivariable analysis was performed but unmeasured confounders (era-related supportive care improvements, learning curve) remain. D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive inclusion described but assignment to era-based group means selection partly determined by calendar time. D3 (classification): moderate - intervention well-defined but distinct from intended PTCy-vs-non-PTCy comparison of interest. D4 (deviations): low - standardized prophylaxis regimens. D5 (missing data): moderate - some patients lacked FLT3/NPM1 data; outcomes complete. D6 (measurement): low - GvHD per Glucksberg/NIH criteria, CMV via twice-weekly PCR. D7 (reporting): low - comprehensive outcomes table. Overall: moderate risk of bias driven by era effect and residual confounding.

EBMT ALWP retrospective registry study comparing UD 9/10 PTCy vs dCBT in AML CR1. D1 (confounding): moderate—significant imbalances at baseline (year of HCT 2019 vs 2016, conditioning intensity MAC 51% vs 21%, KPS, CMV serostatus, donor sex) addressed by multivariate Cox with frailty for center; PTCy dose/schedule not captured. D2 (selection): moderate—centers contributing UD9/10 PTCy may differ from those doing dCBT, no propensity score. D3 (classification of intervention): low—donor type and PTCy use clearly defined per inclusion criteria. D4 (deviations): low—observational, intent-to-treat-like at registry level. D5 (missing data): low—main outcomes complete; MRD, FLT3/NPM1 substantially missing but adjusted for. D6 (measurement): moderate—infection deaths from registry forms, no central adjudication. D7 (selective reporting): low—all pre-planned outcomes reported. Overall moderate risk of bias.

D1 (confounding): moderate. Single-center retrospective cohort with consistent donor allocation algorithm (MRD > 8/8 MUD > HID) which introduces selection - patients without MRD/MUD donors were channeled to HID, generating confounding by availability/timeline/disease urgency. Multivariable Cox adjusts for patient age, gender, race, diagnosis, conditioning intensity, cell source, CMV, HCT-CI, CIBMTR risk, DRI, HLA matching, donor age, year of transplant - reasonable set but limited by N. Imbalances: HID more BM grafts (52% vs 0/21%), less MAC (6% vs 30-32%), more non-white. D2 (deviations): moderate. GVHD prophylaxis differs by donor type per protocol (HID gets PTCy+Tac+MMF; MRD/MUD get Tac+MTX); 9/10 MUD subset gets ATG. These reflect intended interventions but co-vary with the exposure of interest. Also HID got fluoroquinolone for BK prophylaxis through D+100 - confounds infection outcomes. D3 (missing data): low. Prospectively documented database; few losses described; follow-up median 27 months. D4 (outcome measurement): moderate. Outcome assessor (single dedicated practitioner) not blinded to donor type; GVHD grading prospective and standardized (modified Keystone for aGVHD, NIH consensus for cGVHD). D5 (selection of reported results): low. Standard outcome set; multivariable analysis tables shown. D6 (deviations specific to ROBINS-I; treated as covered by D2): low. D7 (selection of participants - all consecutive patients in eligible window): low. Overall: moderate.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis comparing Haplo vs MSD for R/R-AML, 2007-2015. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - large baseline imbalances (Haplo more recent year, longer interval from diagnosis, more BM, more poor PS, more refractory disease in MSD); multivariable Cox adjustment performed but residual confounding likely (no DRI/molecular markers, no center-level case-mix). D2 (selection): MODERATE - selection into Haplo vs MSD non-random and driven by donor availability/era. D3 (classification of interventions): MODERATE - GVHD prophylaxis heterogeneous; Haplo includes PTCy (71%), ATG-only (24%), and both (4%). D4 (deviations from intervention): LOW - registry capture. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - cytogenetics 38-64% NA/failed; no DRI; no DLI/sequential data. D6 (measurement of outcomes): MODERATE - registry-based outcome reporting; no infection-type detail; no immune reconstitution. D7 (selection of reported result): LOW - pre-specified primary OS endpoint. Overall SERIOUS due to confounding and prophylaxis heterogeneity in Haplo arm.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis with propensity-score matched-pair design (1:2 PTCy:ATG). D1 (confounding): moderate - PSM applied for disease status, conditioning, age, graft source, secondary AML, CMV, F-donor/M-recipient but unbalanced immunosuppressive backbones and ATG heterogeneity (thymoglobulin vs Grafalon, doses ranging 2.5-60 mg/kg) leave residual confounding. D2 (selection): moderate - 9/93 PTCy excluded due to missing match/data. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - mixed ATG brands and doses; PTCy schedule not specified. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - infection complications not captured (acknowledged by authors); HRs not provided. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - registry-reported GVHD without central adjudication. D7 (reporting): low. Overall: moderate per ROBINS-I.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis comparing PTCy (n=197) vs ATG (n=1913) in HLA-identical sibling AML CR1. D1 confounding serious: groups significantly differ in age, year of transplant, conditioning intensity, stem cell source, time from diagnosis, and number of additional immunosuppressive agents; multivariate Cox adjusts for measured confounders and propensity score matching performed but residual confounding likely (e.g., center effect, ATG brand/dose data missing, no info on physician choice rationale). D2 selection moderate: prevalent cases excluded by design (first allo-HSCT only). D3 classification moderate: GVHD prophylaxis self-reported by centers; ATG brand inferred from dose threshold (>=16mg/kg = Grafalon) rather than directly reported. D4 deviations from intended interventions low. D5 missing data moderate: cytogenetic risk NA/Failed in 33% (ATG) and 37% (PTCY); ATG dose unavailable for many patients. D6 outcome measurement moderate: standardized EBMT MED-A reporting with selective audit; clinical-only GVHD ascertainment. D7 selective reporting low: prespecified primary endpoint (GVHD CI) reported.

Retrospective EBMT registry comparison with sizeable imbalance in arm sizes (374 vs 67). D1 (confounding): serious - allocation to ATG+PTCy reflects center policy not patient characteristics; criteria guiding allocation acknowledged as missing by authors. D2 (selection): moderate - inclusion limited to specific GVHD prophylaxis subgroups. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate - ATG dose heterogeneous (2.5-10 mg/kg) and ATG agent (rabbit vs ATLG) not specified; PTCy schedule per center policy. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - infection mortality grouped (35% in both), no detailed infection data, immune reconstitution missing. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - registry data, MAC/RIC and cytogenetics classification per center reporting. D7 (selective reporting): low. Overall: serious risk of bias.

Large EBMT ALWP registry retrospective comparison of PTCy vs ATG vs PTCy+ATG in adult AML haplo-SCT (n=3649). Confounding (D1) serious: substantial era imbalance (ATG median 2015 vs PTCy/comb 2018), differences in conditioning intensity, BM vs PB usage, NPM1/cytogenetic risk; MVA adjustment present but ATG vs PTCy time-period effect not directly modelable. Selection (D2) moderate: registry coverage adequate but some patients excluded; ex vivo manipulation and alemtuzumab excluded. Classification of interventions (D3) moderate: ATG type and dose not routinely captured in registry (Table S2 partial). Deviations (D4) low: GVHD prophylaxis defined at outset. Missing data (D5) moderate: substantial missingness in MRD (52%), cytogenetics (18%), HCT-CI (22%), NPM1 (51%); no infection ascertainment data. Outcome measurement (D6 NA for ROBINS-I dimension 6; using D6=low) and selection of reported result (D7=low): pre-specified MVA endpoints reported. Overall judgement: serious due to confounding by era and treatment-allocation differences inherent to registry comparison.

Retrospective two-center comparison with center-defined allocation to prophylaxis (entire allocation by transplant center), inducing major confounding by center and era. Baseline imbalances acknowledged: ATG arm older, higher DRI intermediate, more TBI, more RIC. No multivariable propensity score matching attempted; Cox MVA performed but limited variables. Selection by indication (donor center) is structural. Outcomes ascertainment standard transplant follow-up. Some flexibility in stratification timing. Seattle criteria used (predates NIH 2014). Overall serious risk of bias per ROBINS-I.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing PTCy (08/2015-12/2019) vs ATG historical control (01/2012-07/2015). D1 (confounding): serious — substantial era differences (8-year span across two non-contemporaneous periods), small N=28 per arm limits adjustment; multivariate analysis adjusted for only 2 covariates per outcome due to event limits, leaving residual confounding (e.g., supportive care evolution, CMV monitoring practices, letermovir era). D2 (selection): moderate — patients selected by treatment era; no formal eligibility criteria reported. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — PTCy and ATG arms well-defined but ATG doses varied 7.5-15 mg/kg (substantial heterogeneity in immunosuppression intensity). D4 (deviations): low — both arms followed standard protocols. D5 (missing data): moderate — many baseline variables not separately tabulated by arm; CMV serostatus not reported; full follow-up duration per arm not reported. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — outcomes (GVHD, NRM, relapse) ascertained clinically without blinded adjudication; era-dependent ascertainment of CMV. D7 (reported result): low — primary endpoints pre-specified. Overall: serious risk of bias due to non-contemporaneous historical control, small sample size, and limited adjustment for confounders.

Retrospective single-center cohort comparing PTCy (2014-2023, n=41) vs non-Cy (2010-2018, n=20) in adults >=70. D1 (confounding): serious - era effect heavily confounded with treatment (non-Cy concentrated in 2010-2012; PTCy in 2017-2023) plus markedly different donor mix (100% MUD non-Cy vs 64% MUD + 29% haplo + 7% MMUD in PTCy) and different conditioning regimens (Flu/Bu universally non-Cy vs ThioFluMel/FluCyTBI for PTCy); no multivariable adjustment. D2 (selection): serious - no consecutive-eligibility statement; non-randomized assignment of prophylaxis driven by donor and era. D3 (classification): moderate - GvHD prophylaxis well documented. D4 (deviations): moderate. D5 (missing data): moderate - follow-up duration not reported. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - retrospective EMR ascertainment, no central adjudication. D7 (selective reporting): low. Overall: serious due to severe confounding by era and donor type.

Retrospective single-center comparative cohort. D1 (confounding) moderate: comparators received ATG-based prophylaxis with different conditioning (RIC for MRD/UD vs predominantly NMAC for haplo, P<0.0001); CMV serostatus differed between UD and haplo (P=0.01); no propensity matching or multivariable adjustment for outcome comparisons. D2 (selection) moderate: haplo was last-choice donor (per French standards), introducing selection bias. D3 (intervention classification) low: clear protocol-defined prophylaxis. D4 (deviations) low. D5 (missing data) moderate: HCT-CI missing for some patients (44/47 MRD, 58/63 UD). D6 (outcome measurement) low: standard GVHD criteria used uniformly. D7 (selective reporting) low.

BMT CTN 1203 phase 2 trial randomized between 3 experimental arms (TAC/MMF/PTCy, TAC/MTX/BOR, TAC/MTX/MVC) 1:1:1, BUT the TAC/MTX control arm was a non-randomized contemporary CIBMTR-collected cohort from non-participating centers. D1 (randomization process): HIGH for the PTCy-vs-control comparison since control patients were NOT randomized; allocation across treatment-vs-control was determined by center selection. Significant baseline imbalance (HCT-CI >3: 62% controls vs 38-42% trial arms; conditioning regimen distribution differs). D2 (deviations from intended interventions): some concerns - modified ITT analysis included only patients who were transplanted, open-label trial. D3 (missing outcome data): low - outcome ascertainment used adjudication review committee blinded to treatment. D4 (measurement of outcome): low - standardized GVHD grading (Keystone Consensus, NIH Consensus), blinded adjudication. D5 (selection of reported result): some concerns - 90% CIs used (not 95%), composite primary endpoint pre-specified. Overall judgement: HIGH risk of bias due to non-randomized comparison to the contemporary control cohort.

Single-center retrospective comparison of PTCY vs HD-ATG vs LD-ATG in MMUD. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - Substantial era confounding: PTCY group transplanted predominantly 2019-2024 (92.7%) while HD-ATG was 63.4% pre-2015 and LD-ATG 2011-2019; median follow-up 19.4 vs 91.4 vs 73.0 months (P<0.01); supportive care evolved substantially (letermovir, ruxolitinib); authors explicitly acknowledge this confounding. D2 (selection): MODERATE - Eligibility identical (MMUD with single allele mismatch) but treatment assignment driven by transplant era rather than randomization. D3 (intervention classification): LOW - PTCY/ATG dosing clearly defined. D4 (deviations): LOW - Standardized protocols per JACIE. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - Outcomes reported across cohort; not all groups had immune reconstitution data (n=106/155). D6 (measurement): LOW - Standardized outcome definitions (Mount Sinai, NIH 2014). D7 (selective reporting): LOW - All prespecified primary and secondary endpoints reported. Multivariate Cox confirmed PTCY benefit after adjustment for age, conditioning intensity, DRI, HCT-CI, but era/letermovir/ruxolitinib not modeled.

Retrospective EBMT ALWP registry analysis. D1 (confounding): serious — substantial baseline imbalances across donor types (year of tx, MAC use, CMV serostatus, sequential conditioning, in vivo TCD). Authors attempted propensity score weighting to address; results consistent. D2 (selection): moderate — center-level allocation to Haplo vs UD with unclear criteria; selection process not fully described. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate — definitions of MAC/RIC/sequential per EBMT criteria; donor type clearly classified. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate — cytogenetics unknown in 73/199 Haplo, 718/1111 UD 10/10, 222/383 UD 9/10; blast counts at HSCT missing for many. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — center-reported aGVHD/cGVHD grading subject to variability. D7 (selective reporting): low — pre-specified outcomes reported. Overall: serious due to confounding and missing covariate data despite PS adjustment.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective cohort. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS — significant baseline imbalance: PTCy patients younger (median 46 vs 56 yrs, p<0.001), more recent transplants (2016 vs 2014, p<0.001), higher KPS, higher CMV+ recipient. Propensity score matching attempted but residual confounding likely (no info on what guided GVHD prophylaxis choice, center effect). D2 (selection): MODERATE — registry inclusion may miss centers/patients not reporting. D3 (classification of interventions): MODERATE — ATG brand limited to Thymoglobulin 5 mg/kg total but additional immunosuppressive drug schedules varied (55% vs 85% used 2-3 additional agents), heterogeneous PTCy schedules. D4 (deviations): LOW — registry observational data, not intervention-trial. D5 (missing data): LOW — primary outcomes available for nearly all patients; some baseline covariates missing (KPS 111+1, CMV 23+3). D6 (measurement of outcomes): MODERATE — GVHD assessed clinically per modified Glucksberg/Seattle criteria; outcome assessors not blinded. D7 (selection of reported result): LOW — pre-specified endpoints reported consistently. Overall SERIOUS due to D1 confounding with substantial baseline imbalance and residual confounding from unmeasured factors (infections, ATG dose data, post-transplant strategies, center effect).

Phase 2 RCT with central randomization (1:1) — D1 (randomization) low. Open-label design — investigators and patients aware of treatment allocation, leading to D2 (deviations from intended interventions) concerns; 8 ATG patients did not undergo HSCT (6 pre-transplant relapses, 2 donor unavailability) leading to imbalanced numbers (44 PTCy vs 37 ATG analyzed) — analyzed cohort drops 8 ATG patients from randomization; though full analysis set defined as patients undergoing HSCT. D3 (missing outcome data) low - GRFS, OS, DFS reported for all transplanted patients. D4 (measurement of outcome) low - composite GRFS endpoint with objective relapse/death components and standardized aGVHD/cGVHD grading (Glucksberg, NIH). D5 (selection of reported result) low - prespecified primary endpoint, registered NCT02876679. Overall: some_concerns due to open-label design and asymmetric attrition pre-HSCT.

RCT, randomized 1:2 with biased-coin minimization stratified by hospital and donor type (d1=low). Open-label trial as expected for distinct GVHD prophylaxis regimens; deviations from intended interventions were not described in detail but ITT used (d2=low). Modified ITT applied with 9 patients withdrawn for ineligibility based on data available before randomization; otherwise minimal missing outcome data given centralized HOVON Data Center (d3=low). GVHD assessment with standardized Glucksberg/Seattle criteria, central data management (d4=low). Some concerns in d5 (selection of reported result): protocol amendment changed the trial from a 2-arm time-restricted IS comparison to a 3-arm including PT-Cy; the original primary endpoint (PG180) was retained but unsuited for PT-Cy comparison per authors' own discussion. Many key endpoints (GVHD, NRM, OS, GRFS) were exploratory secondary analyses without multiplicity correction. Overall: some concerns.

ROBINS-I assessment: D1 (confounding) serious - retrospective single-center cohort, arm assignment by treating physician/era, large baseline imbalances between arms (age 6 vs 3.6 yrs; sex 44% vs 66% male; donor type 8% vs 38% haplo; conditioning 20% vs 52% MAC; first vs repeat HSCT 87% vs 69%); no multivariable adjustment performed. D2 (selection of participants) serious - arms drawn from different eras (2005-2018) without matching, with calendar-time confounding likely (PtCy adopted later in cohort). D3 (classification of interventions) moderate - clear prophylaxis definitions but other concurrent IS unspecified. D4 (deviations) moderate - no protocol; standard care varied over 13-year period. D5 (missing data) moderate - small PTCy arm (n=29); 21 repeat transplants overlapping with first transplant counts. D6 (outcome measurement) serious - GVHD ascertainment retrospective, grading system not specified, no central adjudication. D7 (selective reporting) moderate - no protocol/registration listed; key outcomes (NRM, cGVHD, infection) not reported. Overall serious risk of bias.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing 3 nonrandomized groups (PTCy MMUD vs ATG MMUD vs PTCy haploidentical). D1 (confounding): serious — substantial differences in graft source (BM 91% vs PBSC 73%/89%), CNI agent (sirolimus preferred in PTCy MMUD), letermovir use (45% vs 11% vs 16%), and antifungal/PJP prophylaxis across arms; multivariate models partially address confounding (adjusted for letermovir) but residual confounding likely. D2 (selection): moderate — historical controls (2015-2018) vs contemporary PTCy MMUD (2017-2019), introduces era effects acknowledged by authors. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate — interventions clearly defined but mixed CNI/sirolimus in PTCy groups blurs prophylaxis category. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low — standard prophylaxis protocols. D5 (missing data): low — comprehensive outcome reporting. D6 (measurement of outcome): moderate — CMV detection by standardized PCR is robust but transplant era change in pre-emptive threshold; GVHD/IRM ascertainment subjective for retrospective design. D7 (selection of reported result): low — primary outcomes appear pre-specified. Small sample size (22 PTCy MMUD) limits power.

Retrospective single-center cohort with non-contemporaneous comparator (ATG-PTCy 2016-2020 vs ATG-only 2014-2018) introduces confounding by era (D1 serious). Selection bias: '1-to-1 matched' historical control selected from institutional database without described matching algorithm (D2 serious). Interventions are not just GVHD prophylaxis - conditioning regimen also differs (Flu added to ATG-PTCy, different ATG dose 7.5 vs 10 mg/kg, graft source PBSC-only vs BM+PBSC) - this confounds the PTCy effect (D3 moderate). Outcome data complete in all 80 patients (D4 low). Outcomes (GVHD by IBMTR criteria, cGVHD by NIH 2014, OS, RFS, CIR) measured per established criteria (D5 low). No protocol available; some selective reporting concerns (e.g., infection subtypes not consistently reported) (D6 moderate). Reporting adequate in main paper (D7 low). Preprint status (Research Square) — not peer-reviewed.

Single-center retrospective cohort, 2015-2019. D1 (confounding): moderate - 4 non-randomized GVHD prophylaxis groups assigned by donor type/era; multivariable adjustment for DRI, donor, neutropenia, relapse but not all confounders (mucositis, TPN, microbiome). D2 (selection): low - consecutive recipients. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate - PTCy-ATG-CsA bundled with ATG, hard to isolate PTCy effect. D4 (deviations): low - protocolized supportive care. D5 (missing data): moderate - some baseline characteristics not stratified by arm. D6 (measurement of outcome): moderate - clinical BSI ascertainment, no central adjudication noted, but standard microbiology lab. D7 (selective reporting): low - prespecified outcomes reported. Overall moderate - confounding by donor type and conditioning is partially addressed.

EBMT CMWP registry, retrospective; significant baseline imbalances between PTCY and ATG groups (D1 confounding serious): PTCY group received MAC more often (55.8% vs 38.9%), HMA pre-HSCT more often (56.1% vs 42.3%), more MMUD donors (46.4% vs 25.4%), and younger (57 vs 60 years). Reason for choice of PTCY vs ATG not reported (selection bias D2 moderate). ATG dosing heterogeneous (Thymoglobulin 53.5%, Grafalon 46.4%, dose range 1-60 mg/kg) and missing in 24% of ATG patients (D3 missing data moderate). Multivariable adjustment performed with appropriate covariates and center frailty term; competing risks accounted for. Outcomes objective (death, GVHD, engraftment); minimal measurement bias (D5 moderate due to multi-center heterogeneity in GVHD grading). Selective reporting unlikely given pre-specified primary endpoints (D7 low).

Single-center retrospective cohort with homogeneous prophylaxis (MAP for all; PT-Cy for 81.6%) and standardized IFI definitions (EORTC 2020 + MSG-ERC 2019). D1 (confounding): moderate — donor type was the key exposure but PT-Cy use, MAP class, conditioning, and letermovir era covary; era of transplant (Jan 2015 - Dec 2022) spans introduction of letermovir (March 2019), and posaconazole was preferentially used in AML/MDS — donor-type comparison adjusted for some but not all confounders in Fine-Gray MV model. D2 (selection): low — consecutive patients. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate — donor type collapsed into MRD/MUD vs MMRD/MMUD for MV; haplo (30.7% of cohort) handling in donor-type MV model not transparent. D4 (deviations): low — homogeneous protocol. D5 (missing data): moderate — follow-up duration not reported; arm-specific outcomes (by donor) not reported separately. D6 (outcome measurement): low — standardized EORTC definitions, weekly azole TDM. D7 (reporting): low — pre-specified objectives. Overall: moderate. Small event count (10-11 b-PP-IFIs in PT-Cy subset) limits precision of donor-type comparison and may have led to type II error.

ROBINS-I assessment of retrospective non-randomized comparison. D1 (confounding): serious - retrospective design with substantial baseline imbalance (conditioning intensity differed markedly: 79% RIC in ATG vs 53% RIC in PTCy, p<0.001), donor type trend, and authors note PTCy vs ATG was largely center-specific, introducing institutional practice effects. IPTW propensity weighting and matched analysis partially mitigate but unmeasured confounders likely remain. D2 (selection): serious - center-level treatment assignment creates selection bias; no allocation procedure. D3 (interventions classification): moderate - ATG is a mixed category (Thymoglobulin 3.5x2 vs Grafalon 30 or 60 mg/kg), with brand-specific effects not disentangled. D4 (deviations): low - both arms received protocol prophylaxis. D5 (missing data): moderate - timing/intensity of immunosuppression tapering, chimerism, transfusion, and relapse-directed therapy data were not consistently available across centers and excluded from analysis. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - outcomes are clinical (engraftment, GVHD, relapse, NRM, OS) generally well-defined but ascertainment varied by center; molecular vs hematological relapse not distinguished. D7 (selective reporting): low - planned outcomes reported with both univariate and propensity-matched analyses. Overall: serious risk of bias.

Retrospective single-center cohort from prospective registry. D1 (confounding): moderate — observational allocation by donor type, although uniform GVHD prophylaxis and large multivariable models with GVHD as time-dependent covariate. D2 (selection): low — consecutive patients from prospective registry, exclusion of letermovir recipients applied uniformly. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate — donor type unambiguous, but excluded letermovir patients may have differed (selection by health policy). D4 (deviations): low — uniform PTCy/sirolimus/MMF irrespective of donor. D5 (missing data): low. D6 (measurement of outcome): low — CMV PCR with standardized cutoff identical across arms; ECIL-7 consensus criteria for CMV and EBMT-NIH-CIBMTR for GVHD. D7 (selection of reported result): low — pre-specified primary endpoint of CMV reactivation/disease, multivariable analyses pre-specified. Authors acknowledge reporting bias (more intensive haplo monitoring).

Retrospective single-center era comparison (SIP 2014-2016 vs PTCy 2016-2018) with substantial differential confounding: (D1) confounding serious — eras differ in supportive care, donor selection (more 7/8 MUD in SIP era because mismatched would now go to haplo), conditioning (more MAC in SIP), and ATG use (42.5% of SIP arm received ATG/alemtuzumab, none in PTCy arm) — and authors did not perform multivariable adjustment for these. (D2) selection bias serious — authors excluded 25 high-DRI patients from SIP cohort but retained all DRIs in PTCy cohort, an asymmetric exclusion that may bias OS/NRM/RFS comparisons in favor of PTCy. (D3) intervention classification moderate — era boundary is clear (April 2016). (D4) deviation from intended intervention low — uniform institutional protocols. (D5) missing data low. (D6) measurement of outcomes moderate — cGVHD definition is investigator-defined surrogate (tacrolimus continuation >1yr), not standard NIH grading; aGVHD grading system not specified; D+100 timepoints not reported. (D7) reporting low. Overall: serious risk of bias.

RoB2 assessment for ALLG BM12 CAST RCT (Curtis 2025). D1 (randomization): low - 1:1 randomization stratified by age and conditioning intensity; allocation concealment standard for ALLG trials. D2 (deviations from intended interventions): some_concerns - open-label design (authors note this as a limitation that could bias GVHD assessments which are subjective); 5/66 patients in experimental arm did not proceed to transplant; ITT analysis used. D3 (missing outcome data): low - censoring rules clearly specified; 43/129 transplanted patients had no event after >=13 mo follow-up; minimal loss to follow-up. D4 (measurement of outcome): some_concerns - composite primary endpoint includes GVHD components which are subjective and assessed unblinded; MAGIC and NIH 2014 criteria applied per protocol. D5 (selection of reported result): low - pre-registered (ACTRN12618000505202), prespecified analysis plan, full reporting of secondary endpoints. Overall: some_concerns due to open-label assessment of subjective GVHD endpoints.

Retrospective single-center historical control study (Institut Paoli-Calmettes, Marseille) comparing PT-Cy patients (2020-2021, n=30) vs ATG historical controls (2014-Mar 2020, n=64). D1 confounding=serious: substantial differences in conditioning regimens (PT-Cy=100% TBF with 70% NMAC; ATG=100% FB2 RIC), era effects (PT-Cy enrolled entirely in COVID/post-letermovir era while ATG spans 2014-2020), DLI use (43% vs 11%), and follow-up (19 vs 52 mo). D2 selection=moderate: consecutive patients in both periods. D3 classification of intervention=moderate: well-defined GVHD prophylaxis protocols but allocation tied to era. D4 deviations from intended interventions=low: standard institutional protocol. D5 missing data=moderate: minimal information on baseline characteristics in main text (Supplementary Table 1 not visible); CMV serostatus, disease subtypes by arm not reported. D6 measurement of outcomes=low: standard GVHD/NRM/OS endpoints. D7 selection of reported result=low: pre-specified comparison. Small PT-Cy arm (n=30) limits precision and confidence in multivariate adjustments. Overall: serious risk of bias due to era/conditioning confounding and limited statistical power.

Retrospective cohort comparing single-center ATG-PTCy-CNI arm (PMH) to a separately-collected CIBMTR comparator (P-5702). Major confounding domain (D1) judged serious due to non-contemporaneous geographic comparator with substantial baseline imbalances: conditioning intensity differs (RIC 69% PMH vs 52% CIBMTR), TBI use markedly higher in PMH (74% vs 17%), enrollment windows differ (2015-2023 PMH vs 2015-2018 CIBMTR), all of which were partially adjusted in MVA. Selection (D2) moderate: PMH cohort is consecutive single-center; CIBMTR a publicly available subset with unclear sampling. Classification of exposure (D3) moderate due to ATG dose heterogeneity within PMH (2 vs 4.5 mg/kg). Deviations (D4) moderate. Missing data (D5) moderate: CIBMTR limits granular cGVHD grading (NIH severity unavailable). Outcome measurement (D6) moderate due to differing centers/grading audits. Reporting (D7) low.

D1 confounding (moderate): collinearity between year of HSCT (era) and PTCy use because PTCy adopted as standard in 2015; authors acknowledge this limitation. MVA includes era variable but only 16 pre-2015 patients limits ability to disentangle. D2 selection (serious): PTCy and non-PTCy arms drawn from non-overlapping calendar periods (2010-2015 vs 2016-2023), with substantial differences in conditioning intensity (MAC 8% PTCy vs 40% no-PTCy), donor mix, and supportive care era. D3 missingness/classification (moderate): NGS available in 73%, cytogenetics in 71%. D4 deviations (low): retrospective observational, no protocol deviations relevant. D5 missing data (low): outcomes ascertained for all 75. D6 outcome measurement (moderate): GvHD/relapse adjudicated clinically without independent review. D7 reporting (low): outcomes pre-specified. Overall: serious risk due to era-PTCy collinearity and small sample.

Retrospective single-center cohort spanning 2010-2023 with temporal shift in standard-of-care prophylaxis (PTCy became default in October 2015). D1 (confounding): serious - PTCy/non-PTCy categorization is heavily confounded by calendar era (group I predominantly pre-2015, groups III/IV post-2015); conditioning intensity, TBI use, and cryopreservation differ markedly between arms (all p<0.01 in baseline table); letermovir era differs. Authors used multivariable Cox/Fine-Gray models adjusting for KPS, RIC vs MAC, cryopreservation, DRI, CMV serostatus but did not adjust for calendar year or letermovir era. D2 (selection): moderate - all consecutive MSD-HSCT PBSC included but only group with >=12 mo FU eligible. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - prophylaxis groups well-defined from records, though ATG dose varied during a 2-yr window (4.5 mg/kg vs 2 mg/kg) mixed within group II/III. D4 (deviations): low - prophylaxis is assigned per protocol of era. D5 (missing data): moderate - some baseline data missing (DRI not in all). D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - blinding not possible; routine clinical ascertainment for GVHD, CMV, BSI; competing-risk framework used. D7 (selection of reported result): low - prespecified primary outcomes (GRFS, NRM, OS). Overall: serious risk of bias mainly due to era confounding.

Retrospective registry-based analysis using publicly available CIBMTR P-5891 dataset restricted to young adults (18-39yr). Propensity score-matched analysis reduces but does not eliminate confounding. Strengths: large contemporary cohort (n=1387); MVA controlled for donor/recipient age, sex, diagnosis, DRI, HCT-CI, CMV serostatus, conditioning intensity; SMD <0.1 achieved post-PSM. Limitations: registry data with potential missing values and variable center-specific practices; PTCy era likely later than CNI-MTX era (era effect not formally adjusted); no granular data on PTCy dose, CNI agent/trough, MMF dose, infection prophylaxis (letermovir, antifungals); ATG agent/dose not reported. D1 (confounding): moderate (PSM mitigated). D3 (intervention classification): moderate (CNI agent and other details not reported). D5 (missing data): moderate (registry-typical). Overall ROBINS-I judgement moderate.

Retrospective EBMT ALWP registry analysis comparing CBT (no PTCy, transplanted earlier era 2010-2019 with median 2013) vs 9/10 MMUD with PTCy (later era, median 2017). D1 (confounding): serious — substantial era differences (2013 vs 2017), heterogeneity in conditioning, GVHD prophylaxis, in vivo TCD (40% CBT vs 26% MMUD), and supportive care; propensity score matching attempted but unmeasured confounders (MRD status, donor chimerism, recipient HLA antibodies, center expertise) remain. D2 (selection): moderate — registry-based selection by donor type with center-level practice variation. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — heterogeneity in PTCy schedule (+3+4 vs +3+5) and adjunct immunosuppression. D4 (deviation): low. D5 (missing): moderate — substantial missingness for cytogenetics (37.9% unknown in CBT), HCT-CI, donor CMV. D6 (measurement): moderate — different follow-up duration (19.1 vs 46.8 mo) may bias outcome ascertainment. D7 (reporting): low. Authors performed propensity score matching but acknowledged inability to adjust for unmeasured factors.

Retrospective matched-pair analysis from two LMU centers (Munich-Grosshadern + Augsburg) with high-quality matching on disease stage, ELN genetics, age. Two arms have inherently different GVHD prophylaxis (PTCy vs ATG) inseparable from donor type (confounding by indication). Some residual imbalances: cytoreductive chemotherapy (clofarabine vs FLAMSA) and graft source (BM 35% vs PBSC 100% in HLA-matched) differ; authors assessed and found no influence on outcomes. Small sample size (n=34 per arm). Standardized definitions (Glucksberg/Przepiorka for aGvHD, NIH 2005 for cGvHD, EORTC/MSG for IFI). Single-center supportive care and treatment protocols minimize center effects. Selection of matched pairs from larger pool of eligible patients (34/41 haplo and 34/166 HLA-matched) may introduce selection bias for HLA-matched arm in particular. Confounding domain moderate; selection moderate due to matched-pair design plus larger HLA-matched pool; classification of outcomes low.

Retrospective registry-based comparison of 4 non-randomized donor cohorts (haplo-PTCy vs MSD vs MUD TCD+ vs MUD TCD-). D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - haplo patients differed significantly from comparators in age (older), KPS (better), prior auto-HCT (less), and transplant procedure (more TBI, more BM grafts); Cox modeling with forward stepwise selection used but residual confounding likely (HCT-CI missing in 25-47% across arms, EBMT does not collect for MED-A; race missing 18-36%; CMV status missing 31-58%). Authors explicitly acknowledge confounding limitation in Discussion. D2 (selection): LOW - all consecutive eligible patients registered in EBMT/CIBMTR; CIBMTR limited to US/Canada to prevent EBMT duplicates. D3 (classification): MODERATE - donor groups well-defined but TCD+/TCD- pooled different agents (ATG + alemtuzumab); cGVHD severity not classified per NIH 2014 in registry data. D4 (deviations): LOW - GVHD prophylaxis platform fixed per arm by inclusion criteria. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - HCT-CI, race, CMV missingness varies substantially by registry; treated as 'missing' category in Cox models. Outcomes ascertainment standard for both registries with on-site audits. Overall judgement: SERIOUS due to baseline imbalances and registry heterogeneity.

Retrospective observational design across three Polish centers (Wroclaw, Gliwice, Poznan); GVHD prophylaxis assignment by center policy/donor type (PTCy haplo + MMUD vs ATG MMUD-only) creates strong confounding by indication (D1 serious). Arm sizes highly imbalanced (110 vs 35) and 100% of PTCy haplo are non-overlapping with ATG arm; only 17 PTCy-MMUD allow head-to-head comparison. Outcome definitions used standard Glucksberg/MAGIC for aGvHD and NIH 2014 for cGvHD but timepoints (D+100, 1yr, 2yr) not standardized; CMV reactivation reported as crude proportion without time-to-event. Loss to follow-up not described. No adjustment for multiple confounders presented in the primary tables. Heterogeneous ATG regimens (Grafalon 20 mg/kg or Thymoglobulin 4.5 mg/kg) within ATG arm. Pre-letermovir era (2015-2019) for both groups (Poland adoption).

Retrospective multicenter (3 Polish centers) cohort with strong arm imbalance: PTCy arm dominated by haplo-HSCT (84.5%) while ATG arm is exclusively MMUD-HSCT, so PTCy vs ATG comparison is confounded by donor type. Pooled PTCy arm reporting (haplo+MMUD together) for most outcomes prevents clean MMUD-PTCy vs MMUD-ATG analysis (only survival and HLA-mismatch distribution are reported within MMUD subset; aGVHD, cGVHD, CMV are not reported separately for MMUD-PTCy n=17). Domain 1 (confounding): serious due to non-random assignment of GVHD prophylaxis (donor type drives prophylaxis choice). Domain 3 (deviation from intended interventions): moderate. No adjusted hazard ratios reported. CMV timepoint not specified. Small MMUD-PTCy subset (n=17). No reporting of disease characteristics, conditioning intensity, HLA matching, or CMV serostatus by individual arm.

Retrospective multicenter PALG analysis with non-randomized 3-arm comparison (PTCy-haplo vs PTCy-MMUD vs ATG-MMUD). D1 (confounding): serious - substantial between-arm imbalance in conditioning intensity (PTCy-MMUD 100% MAC vs PTCy-haplo 53.5% MAC) and diagnoses (p=0.004); donor age also differs (p=0.027); no propensity-score or robust multivariable adjustment. D2 (selection): moderate - prophylaxis choice driven by center/era. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - heterogeneous ATG dosing (Grafalon 20 mg/kg vs Thymoglobuline 4.5 mg/kg combined). D4 (deviations): low - retrospective with defined protocols. D5 (missing data): moderate - short median follow-up (8.5 months for alive patients) limits longer-term outcome estimation; D+100/CIF-based metrics not formally reported (crude proportions only). D6 (measurement): moderate - aGvHD reported as overall %, not stratified D+100 cumulative incidence; cGvHD overall (no NIH severity grading). D7 (selective reporting): moderate - no protocol/registration; primary outcome composite of acute and chronic GvHD with multiple subgroup comparisons. Overall: serious.

Retrospective single-center comparison of historical UCBT cohort (predominantly 2005-2014) vs newer HaploHCT cohort (predominantly 2015-2017). Strong era confounding: 96% of UCBTs were performed before 2015, while 74% of HaploHCTs were performed from 2015 onwards. Substantial baseline imbalance: HaploHCT recipients older (median 48 vs 38), less likely in CR (53% vs 77%), higher EBMT risk score and HCT-CI. MVA adjusted only for age and disease status; era and HCT-CI not modeled. GVHD prophylaxis platforms also differ inherently (PTCy + tacrolimus alone vs CSA/prednisone/MMF + ATG). Small sample (n=77 total). Outcome ascertainment from institutional protocol. Outcome definitions reasonably standard (Glucksberg, NIH). Authors transparent about limitations.

Multicenter retrospective observational cohort (GETH 6 centers, 2013-2018). Single-arm descriptive infection epidemiology study with no comparator. D1 (confounding) moderate: heterogeneous conditioning (MAC/RIC), GVHD prophylaxis (CSA-MMF vs Tac alone), antifungal prophylaxis varies by center. D2 (selection) low: consecutive patients with broad eligibility. D3 (intervention classification) moderate: post-hoc landmark windowing may misclassify; severe infection definition standard but heterogeneous source ascertainment. D4 (deviations) low: standardized institutional protocols. D5 (missing data) moderate: retrospective chart review with potential underascertainment of late infections. D6 (measurement) moderate: ascertainment of severe infection uses standard EBMT definitions, but laboratory practices differ across centers. D7 (reporting) low: prespecified time windows, transparent. Overall moderate ROB for an observational study of this kind.

Retrospective multicenter cohort with substantial baseline imbalances (PTCy group: more MRD donors, shorter dx-to-HSCT time, more KPS>=90, higher DRI, more BM grafts, more TBF/TMF conditioning) and strong era confounding (96% of PTCy in 2016-2020 vs 72% of SIR/TAC in 2012-2015; median follow-up 23m vs 78m). D1 serious: confounding by indication, era, and donor type. D2 moderate: selection by center protocol but consecutive within strategy. D3 moderate: intervention classification clear but PTCy-arm itself heterogeneous (CNI+/-MMF vs Sirolimus+MMF). D5 moderate: missing data on some baseline variables. Authors mitigated with IPW analysis but D1 confounding remains substantial. Overall serious.

Multicenter retrospective GETH-TC/EBMT cohort (12 centers, 2012-2022) comparing HAPLO (n=330), MMUD-PTCy (n=49), MMUD-OTHERS (n=74) RIC alloHSCT. D1 confounding: moderate; multivariate Fine-Gray and Cox models with prespecified covariates (donor type, recipient/donor age, ECOG PS, diagnosis, disease status, TCI, CMV mismatch, ATG use) but residual confounding by indication likely (donor selection driven by center policy and clinical urgency). D2 selection: moderate; consecutive patients from PROMISE database across multiple centers, but era imbalance (73% MMUD-OTHERS transplanted 2012-2016 vs 89% MMUD-PTCy 2017+) may introduce era-related confounding. D3 intervention classification: moderate; GVHD prophylaxis is recorded but MMUD-OTHERS group is heterogeneous (Sir/Tac 78%, ATG 70%, varied combinations). D4 deviations from intended interventions: low. D5 missing data: low; cell counts of missing data reported per variable (e.g., DRI 17/4/23 missing across arms) and follow-up complete. D6 outcome measurement: moderate; outcome ascertainment not blinded; antifungal and CMV prophylaxis and monitoring not collected systematically (acknowledged limitation). D7 selective reporting: low; prespecified primary endpoint (GRFS) reported. Overall moderate risk of bias due to retrospective design, era effect, small MMUD-PTCy subgroup (n=49 limits power), and heterogeneity in MMUD-OTHERS prophylaxis.

RCT with 1:1 central randomization stratified by center via Emmes Corporation (D1 low). Open-label trial (donor source cannot be blinded) but objective and standardized endpoints with adjudication committee blinded to treatment assignment for >90% concordance check (D2/D4 low). Pre-specified primary endpoint (2-year PFS) and analysis plan (D5 low). Missing outcome data minimal at 2 years; ITT analysis with all randomized included (D3 low). Cross-overs from haplo arm to UCB (11/182) reflect clinical inability to obtain haplo donor; analyzed by ITT mitigating deviation bias. Overall low ROB.

Single-center retrospective cohort with non-randomized assignment to PTCy vs MTX. Era-confounded: PTCy was used uniformly from April 2019 onward while MTX was used predominantly before that date, creating substantial calendar-time/era confounding (D2 serious). Arm assignment was by center protocol rather than patient/disease characteristics, but confounders such as donor type, conditioning intensity, disease, age likely differ between eras (D1 moderate). Outcome ascertainment (HC) was based on clinical hematuria grading using accepted literature criteria with prospectively collected data, but ascertainment of aGVHD and NRM not stratified by arm. The paper does not report per-arm outcomes for aGVHD, NRM, OS, CMV, or BSI — only HC incidence is per-arm. Marked imbalance between arms (n=188 vs n=43) and PTCY-MTX comparison was not the primary research question (HC was). Risk of bias for any inference about PTCy vs MTX on outcomes other than HC is high. Selective reporting moderate (D5).

D1 confounding: serious - retrospective registry-based study with strong era imbalance (87% haplo transplanted 2016-2020 vs 28% of 9/10-MUD); MVA adjusted for year of allo-SCT but residual confounding from supportive care/conditioning evolution likely. Information on ATG dose/formulation, MRD status, molecular/genetic disease features, immune reconstitution and infection data NOT available in registry. D2 selection: moderate - consecutive registry patients; donor type determined by availability/center preference. D3 classification of intervention: moderate - heterogeneous ATG dose/formulation across centers. D4 deviations: low. D5 missing data: moderate - HCT-CI missing in 34.8% overall (42.8% in MUD arm); donor age missing in 43.1%; missing values treated as separate categories in MVA. D6 measurement of outcomes: low - standardized GVHD grading per consensus criteria. D7 selective reporting: low. Overall: serious risk of bias due to retrospective era-imbalanced registry design with substantial missingness.

Retrospective multicenter cohort design comparing haplo vs MSD HSCT in SAA. D1 (confounding): serious — donor type is non-randomized; significant baseline imbalance in conditioning regimen (p=0.040), GVHD prophylaxis distribution (p=0.008), time from diagnosis to HSCT (p=0.021), CD34+ cell dose (p=0.019); no multivariable adjustment for OS or GVHD comparisons. D2 (selection): serious — consecutive enrollment described but no randomization; donor type selection driven by availability; arms unbalanced 117 vs 39 with different prophylaxis mix (PT-CY 26.5% in haplo vs 10.3% in MSD; ATG-based 22.2% vs 46.2%). D3 (intervention classification): moderate — donor type and arm assignment clearly defined but heterogeneous GVHD prophylaxis within arms confounds donor-comparison interpretation. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): moderate — no flow diagram; 156 patients enrolled but completeness of outcome ascertainment across 4 centers not explicit. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — clinical/per-protocol GVHD grading (Fred Hutchinson criteria), CMV by weekly PCR; no blinded adjudication. D7 (selective reporting): low — pre-specified primary (2-yr OS) and secondary endpoints reported. Overall: serious due to confounding and selection bias inherent to a non-randomized observational comparison with substantial baseline imbalance.

Retrospective registry-based cohort. D1 (confounding): serious - ATG-PTCy was used exclusively at PMHCC (single-center) while PTCy-only was used at other Canadian centers, creating strong center-by-treatment confounding; multiple baseline imbalances (KPS, HCT-CI, DRI, recipient CMV). Authors performed multivariable Cox and PSM analysis but key unmeasured confounders (institutional supportive care, infection prophylaxis, CMV monitoring) remain. D2 (selection): serious - selection into prophylaxis regimen by center policy, not patient/disease characteristics; non-random allocation. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - clear regimen definitions but conditioning intensity definitions heterogeneous ('Other' vs MAC). D4 (deviations): low - registry data, no protocol deviations to consider. D5 (missing data): low-moderate - some missingness in DRI (18%) and ABO incompatibility (21.6%) handled with multivariable inclusion of 'unknown' category. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - GVHD grading and CMV monitoring not standardized across 11 centers; non-fatal infectious complications not captured. D7 (selective reporting): low - all pre-specified endpoints reported. Overall: serious risk of bias due to strong center-treatment confounding.

Single-centre retrospective observational study of 21 R/R HL patients with no comparator arm. D1 (confounding): serious - no adjustment for confounders, mixed conditioning (95% Flu/Cy/TBI200, 5% Flu/Mel) and GVHD prophylaxis (86% PTCy, 14% ATG) with no separate analysis. D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive patients meeting criteria, but selection of alloSCT candidates not described in detail. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate - intervention well documented but heterogeneous. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective. D5 (missing data): moderate - HCT-CI missing 1, GVHD prophylaxis missing 2, ABO mismatch missing 2. D6 (measurement): moderate - outcomes ascertained from CIBMTR-reporting database; CMV/EBV ascertainment method not specified. D7 (selection of reported result): moderate. Overall: serious due to small sample size, no comparator, heterogeneous treatment, and limited generalizability acknowledged by authors.

EBMT registry retrospective comparison; ATG and PTCy groups not randomized — choice of GVHD prophylaxis by center/era, large imbalance in group size (117 PTCy vs 779 ATG). D1 (confounding): serious — no MRD data, ATG brand/dose/timing not collected, calendar period imbalance (PTCy more recent). D2 (selection): moderate — both arms drawn from same registry by uniform inclusion criteria (CR1, 10/10 MUD, 2015-2020). D3 (intervention classification): moderate — broad classifier 'ATG' or 'PTCy' but no detailed regimen capture. D4 (deviations): low — registry data. D5 (missing data): moderate — KPS, HCT-CI, donor sex missing in 8-14% of records. D6/D7 (measurement, reporting): low — standard EBMT outcome definitions, all prespecified secondary endpoints reported.
Study excluded from PTCy contrast analysis as single-arm descriptive without PTCy vs comparator stratification; RoB not assessed per protocol exclusion.

Single-center retrospective study (138 haplo-HCT recipients with PBSC and PTCy at Washington University). The study stratifies by post-transplant CMV viremia (an outcome) and analyzes its impact on other outcomes - not a GVHD prophylaxis comparison. D1 (confounding): moderate - retrospective, baseline imbalance in age/race/CMV serostatus between groups. D2 (selection): moderate - convenience sample. D3 (classification): moderate - clinical/laboratory ascertainment. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - short median follow-up (220d) for time-to-event outcomes. D6 (measurement): moderate - clinical aGVHD/cGVHD grading. D7 (selective reporting): low. Letter to the Editor format limits methods detail.

Single-center retrospective registry cohort of 2-year survivors only (conditioning landmark survivor bias). Heterogeneous GVHD prophylaxis (CsA+MTX 77%, CsA+sirolimus 15%, PTCy 4%, other) and transplant era span (2005-2019 covers major practice changes). PTCy used only in n=17 haplo recipients - cannot be analyzed as comparator. Confounding by indication for prophylaxis platform, donor type, and era. No PTCy vs non-PTCy outcome stratification provided. For PTCy meta-analysis purposes, this study contributes background/context only (single_arm_descriptive_excluded).
Single-arm descriptive trial excluded per protocol (no comparator arm); RoB not assessed.

Single-center retrospective observational study (Luoyang Central Hospital) comparing two non-randomized GVHD prophylaxis platforms across the same enrollment window (2019-2024) at physician discretion. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - non-randomized allocation by treating physician discretion / evolving institutional practice; potential time-period confounding within 2019-2024 window; only baseline DRI/age/disease distribution adjusted in multivariable analyses. D2 (selection): MODERATE - consecutive eligibility, but selection mechanism between regimens not explicitly random and may reflect unmeasured prognostic factors. D3 (classification of interventions): MODERATE - ATG dose and PTCy administration well documented but no central audit. D4 (deviations): LOW - intent-based comparison, no major deviations. D5 (missing data): LOW - 100% follow-up. D6 (measurement of outcomes): LOW - cGVHD and aGVHD by standard NIH/Glucksberg criteria, blinded outcome assessment unlikely needed for these. D7 (reporting): LOW - all pre-specified outcomes reported. Sample size (n=61) extremely small with wide CIs limiting precision. Overall: SERIOUS due to small underpowered single-center retrospective design with non-randomized allocation.

Retrospective single-center matched-pair design at LMU Munich; D1 (confounding) serious because of marked era/calendar-time differences (median transplant year MRD 2006 / URD 2008 / Haplo 2012) and unbalanced graft source (Haplo predominantly BM, MRD/URD PBSC) that could not be matched; D2 (selection) moderate as matching used disease, age, ECOG/KPS but pool was 36 haplo from which 16 were matched; D3 (intervention classification) moderate due to GVHD prophylaxis platforms also differing in components (Sirolimus-MMF in some MRD/URD); D4 (deviations) low; D5 (missing data) low (long follow-up complete); D6 (measurement) moderate (GvHD grading clinical with potential observer variability); D7 (reporting) low; overall judgement serious due to confounding by era and graft source.

Retrospective EBMT+CIBMTR registry analysis with structural confounding: PTCy is structural to the haplo-HCT arm only; MSD and MUD comparator arms use CNI-based prophylaxis (MUD TCD+ adds ATG/alemtuzumab). Authors acknowledge important baseline differences (haplo arm has more KPS<90, more BM grafts, more RIC), and that application of PTCy to MUD transplants might question the equivalence. Multivariate Cox adjusted for donor source, disease status, age, sex, cell source, conditioning intensity, prior auto-HCT, KPS, histology, with stratification on data source. D1 (confounding): serious (donor-prophylaxis structural confounding, residual confounding by center practices and PTCy/CNI/ATG specifics not separable). D2 (selection): moderate (registry; selection of fitter patients able to undergo HCT). D3 (exposure measurement): moderate (registry classification with overlap exclusion vs prior studies). D4 (deviation from intervention): low (registry observational). D5 (missing data): moderate (substantial missing data on chemotherapy lines [61%] and HCT-CI; KPS missing in 86 patients). No central pathology review; ALK status missing for 27% of ALCL cases; no information on imaging modalities for response assessment or postrelapse therapies.

Large nationwide retrospective registry analysis (JDCHCT TRUMP2) with substantial cohort differences between arms. D1 (Confounding): serious - donor choice non-random, significant baseline imbalances (age, sex distribution by donor type, transplant era 2013-2016 vs 2017-2020 distributed asymmetrically, GVHD prophylaxis platform CNI+MMF vs CNI+MTX strongly correlated with donor type, conditioning intensity differences). Although multivariable Fine-Gray/Cox models adjust for multiple covariates, residual confounding from center-level practices, unmeasured factors (donor selection rationale, e.g., urgency for UCB-L group; functional status; CMV serostatus), and CD34+ cell count selection logic remains. D2 (Selection): moderate - 715/8506 cases (8.4%) excluded for missing data which authors note do not change results materially.
