D3 (Classification of intervention): low - donor type and graft source clearly recorded in registry. D4 (Deviations): low - registry observational; intervention exposures are fixed at transplant. D5 (Missing data): low - large N, completeness for primary outcomes good. D6 (Measurement): moderate - GVHD graded at each institution (potential inter-institution variability), no central adjudication. D7 (Reporting): low - prespecified covariates with full Table 2/3/4 multivariable models reported.

Retrospective multicenter Spanish cohort with heterogeneous comparator (MRD/MUD/MMRD/MMUD historical controls from only 2 of the 4 centers). D1 confounding moderate: GVHD prophylaxis platform varies markedly across donor types (PTCy in haplo only; Tac+Sir for MUD; CsA-based in MRD; ATG used in 70.4% MMUD vs 0.8% in haplo). D2 selection moderate: haplo arm contemporary (2016-2018) vs historical controls (2012-2018) at 2 centers only; HCUS/HGUGM contribute only haplo patients. D3 classification of intervention low. D4 missing data low (only 8/283 patients had truncated follow-up to median 294 d). D5 outcome measurement moderate: heterogeneity in PCR assay used (Affigene vs Abbott), different PET thresholds per center; addressed by subanalyses but residual concern. D6 outcome reporting low (all outcomes reported). D7 other low. Overall moderate.

D1 (confounding): serious - retrospective nonrandomized cohort with treatment selection by physician's discretion; PTCy-Siro patients significantly younger (median 48 vs 61 yr, P=.004) and disease distribution differed (NHL predominant in PTCy-Siro [37.9%] vs AML predominant in Tac-MTX [37.9%], P<.001); no multivariable adjustment for confounders. D2 (selection of participants): serious - intervention selection by physician choice with unstated criteria, with strong potential for indication bias (e.g., younger or NHL patients preferentially receiving PTCy-Siro). D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis exposure clearly defined and prospectively administered. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low - some outcomes reported with N evaluable (e.g., chimerism, immunosuppression withdrawal) but main outcomes complete. D6 (measurement of outcomes): low - standardized GVHD grading (Glucksberg/NIH). D7 (selection of reported result): low. Overall: serious risk of bias due to confounding and selection bias inherent to retrospective comparison with treatment selection at physician discretion.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing 3 non-randomized groups defined by donor/GVHD prophylaxis era at UAB 2012-2016. D1 (confounding): moderate - patients with MRD predominantly got CNI-based prophylaxis (cohort A) and MUD got 1-dose PTCy (cohort B), confounding by donor type/era is structural. D2 (selection): moderate - cohorts defined by donor type and protocol used at the time. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - cohort B used 1-dose PTCy which is non-standard. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective EMR review. D5 (missing data): low - relatively complete reporting. D6 (outcome measurement): low - CMV uniformly assessed by qPCR with consistent threshold. D7 (selective reporting): low.

D1 (confounding): serious - retrospective single-center comparison of donor types (haplo vs MUD/MSD) where GVHD prophylaxis differs (haplo arm 100% PTCy+low-dose ATG vs MUD/MSD arm heterogeneous: 18/40 PTCy+ATG and 22/40 ATG+MTX no PTCy). Multivariate analyses partially adjust but the prophylaxis-donor confounding is structural and acknowledged by authors. Significantly different follow-up (haplo 23.5 vs MUD/MSD 58.9 months; P<0.001), donor age, MNC and CD34+ counts. D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive enrollment by patient age and donor availability, era difference (MUD/MSD predominantly earlier era). D3 (classification): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis is not the explicit exposure being compared; treatment exposure classification is heterogeneous. D4 (deviations): low - both arms followed institutional protocols. D5 (missing data): moderate - some baseline covariates not reported (CMV serostatus, HLA matching detail in MUD/MSD). D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - clinically diagnosed outcomes with standard Glucksberg/NIH criteria. D7 (selective reporting): low - prespecified analyses appear reported. Overall judgement: serious due to confounding by GVHD prophylaxis heterogeneity in MUD/MSD arm.

Retrospective two-center study with marked era imbalance (ATG predominantly 2010-2017, PTCy predominantly 2018-2020): D1 confounding serious — letermovir era (2018+) coincides with PTCy adoption, confounding CMV outcomes (authors did sensitivity analysis on pre-2017 subcohort showing attenuated csCMV effect); donor mismatch level imbalanced (PTCy 30.5% >1 locus mismatch vs ATG 2.2%) and graft source imbalanced (PTCy 50% BM vs ATG 26% BM). D2 selection moderate — eligible patient selection well-defined but PTCy 30/82 from prospective NCT02793544 trial may differ from registry-treated patients. D3 classification of intervention moderate — well-defined protocols per arm but ATG dose ranged 5-7.5 mg/kg and PTCy arm split tac/sir 50/50. D4-D5 low. Authors performed multivariable Cox adjusting for CIBMTR risk and graft source and era-restricted sensitivity (post-2016 subcohort) showing maintained PTCy benefit on GRFS.

Retrospective Japanese nationwide registry (TRUMP/JSTCT) analysis. D1 confounding: moderate — significant baseline imbalances in patient sex, ECOG PS, phenotype, ABO mismatch, and transplant year; addressed via multivariate Cox regression and propensity score matching, but residual unmeasured confounding likely (e.g., centre/donor availability, conditioning regimen details, MRD status). D2 selection: low — registry-based with consecutive eligible patients 2013-2021. D3 classification: moderate — registry data completeness varies; some baseline variables incompletely captured. D4 deviations: low — no protocol-defined intervention assignment in retrospective design. D5 missing data: moderate — supplementary appendix not viewable here; details on missing covariates and how handled in propensity matching unverifiable. D6 measurement: low — standardized TRUMP definitions for OS/DFS/NRM/relapse. D7 reporting: low — pre-specified comparisons in study plan approved by JSTCT.

Single-center retrospective with no formal analytic strategy for confounding control. D1 (confounding): serious - PTCy arm is heterogeneous (all 14 haplo + 26 MUD + 9 MSD) while comparator is exclusively MSD; donor-type confounding is overwhelming and impossible to disentangle without multivariable adjustment, which the paper does not perform. Univariate comparisons in Tables 1/2 use chi-square/Fisher's exact tests with no covariate adjustment. D2 (selection): moderate - all consecutive transplants 2022-2024 at one center; allocation was by donor type rather than randomization or matching. D3 (intervention classification): serious - paper text says PTCy was given on D+3 and D+5 (non-standard timing; possibly a typo for D+3/+4 but no correction available); definitional uncertainty. D4 (deviations): moderate - all received uniform CSA+MMF backbone. D5 (missing data): moderate - mortality, NRM, infections, engraftment, OS not broken out by PTCy vs comparator; only aGVHD any-grade and cGVHD any-grade have per-arm data. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate - IBMTR grading rather than MAGIC/NIH; ascertainment timing not specified. D7 (reporting): moderate - some inconsistency (cGVHD 14 in Table 2 vs 15 in narrative; 13 MDS-RAEB '9%' inconsistent with 13/78=16.7%); selective reporting of subgroup OS without methodology.
Study excluded as single_arm_descriptive (LTV era comparison without PTCy stratification); RoB assessment not applicable.

CIBMTR registry retrospective comparative analysis. D1 (confounding): moderate - significant baseline imbalances (DRI worse in haplo, KPS/HCT-CI better in haplo, conditioning and graft source differ systematically by donor type); MVA adjusted for key prognostic factors. D2 (selection): moderate - donor selection driven by physician/center practice not random; treatment group defined by donor availability. D3 (intervention classification): low - GVHD prophylaxis arms well-defined per CIBMTR forms. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective registry; protocols defined. D5 (missing data): moderate - GVHD outcomes restricted to CRF-level subset (~25% of cohort), creating potential reporting bias and reduced power; no infection-specific outcomes captured. D6/D7 (outcome measurement / reporting): low - standardized CIBMTR forms with audit/QC; pre-specified endpoints. Overall: moderate - well-conducted registry but inherent confounding by donor selection and selective CRF reporting for GVHD limit causal inference.

D1 (confounding): serious - retrospective single-center comparison of PTCy (used for haplo/9-10 MMUD only) vs non-PTCy (all other donor types) confounds donor type, conditioning intensity, HLA matching with prophylaxis strategy. Authors note multicollinearity between PTCy and HLA mismatch. D2 (selection): moderate - all consecutive AHSCT included from registry; 17 excluded for early death/engraftment failure. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - PTCy use clearly defined by donor type/HLA mismatch, but other GVHD prophylaxis details for non-PTCy arm not reported. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - many baseline arm characteristics not reported separately by PTCy vs non-PTCy. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - BKV uPCR only performed on clinical symptoms (no systematic screening), risking under-ascertainment of mild cases. D7 (reporting): low - outcomes prespecified.

Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study with very small N=40 (15 vs 25). D1 (confounding) serious - no adjustment for confounders, treatment allocation likely driven by era/availability of PTCy (since 2016) with no propensity matching; baseline imbalances in disease distribution (MDS only in PTCy arm; lymphoma only in MTX-CysA arm). D2 (selection) moderate - selection of patients within single center, eligibility criteria not detailed. D3 (intervention) moderate - retrospective record review. D4 (deviations) moderate. D5 (missing data) moderate. D6 (outcome measurement) moderate - aGVHD per IBMTR criteria, cGVHD per NIH consensus, CMV per PCR threshold. D7 (selective reporting) moderate. Significantly underpowered for primary endpoint of grade 3-4 aGVHD (0 vs 3 events, p=0.28). Median follow-up disparate between arms (9.8 vs 22.6 months) introducing time-to-event bias.

Retrospective single-center cohort comparing haplo-PTCy vs UD-ATG. D1 (confounding): serious - arms differ substantially in disease distribution (more AL/MDS/MPN in UD: 89.7% vs 59.3%; more lymphoma in haplo: 27.1% vs 2.9%), conditioning intensity (MAC 77.9% UD vs 27.1% haplo), and graft source (BM 74.6% haplo vs 51.5% UD). D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive patients but allocation by donor availability/clinical choice. D3 (classification): moderate - retrospective chart review; standardized viral surveillance protocol applied. D4 (deviations): low - real-world clinical practice followed protocol. D5 (missing data): moderate - BKV/HHV-6 only tested in symptomatic patients, biases multi-virus incidence estimates downward (acknowledged by authors). D6 (measurement): moderate - blinding not feasible; clinical outcomes (CMV disease, BKV-HC) require physician adjudication. D7 (selection of reported): low - prespecified outcomes reported. Overall serious due to imbalanced baseline characteristics confounding the PTCy vs ATG comparison and asymmetric viral testing strategy.

Single-center retrospective comparison of pre-2016 Tac/MTX era (N=252, FU 10.6 yr) vs post-2016 PTCy era (N=99, FU 4.4 yr) for matched donor allo-HSCT at Cedars-Sinai. D1 confounding: SERIOUS - era cohorts differ on multiple factors (PBSC use 63.9% vs 81.8%, MAC 41.3% vs 50.1%, NMA 11.1% vs 1.0%, KPS<=80 26.6% vs 40.4%, DRI low 42.9% vs 62.6%, race distribution P=.0019). Authors acknowledge concomitant practice changes (PBSC predominant, TBI-based conditioning, blinatumomab pre-HCT, low-risk donor selection) that may confound. Multivariate Cox models adjust for some factors but not all (e.g., letermovir era, blinatumomab use, era of supportive care). D2 selection: SERIOUS - era-based selection; all post-2016 patients got PTCy (no PTCy exclusions or contemporaneity). D3 classification of exposure: MODERATE - PTCy vs Tac/MTX exposure clearly defined but ATG/alemtuzumab use in non-PTCy comparator not reported. D4-D7 generally low: outcomes ascertained per registry-quality data, CIBMTR data used, GVHD graded per Consensus 1994 and Sullivan 1981.

Single-center retrospective historical comparison with sequential year-based allocation (MTX/CSA 2010-2011 vs PTCy/ATG 2011-2012); D1 confounding serious (era, age, disease distribution differ significantly: PTCy/ATG older [median 45 vs 36, P=0.030], higher AML proportion [81% vs 57%], more prior chemo cycles [81% vs 48%, P=0.024]); D2 selection serious (allocation by year, not random); D3 classification moderate (Mount Sinai aGVHD criteria but Seattle cGVHD); D4 deviation low; D5 missing data moderate (some cGVHD denominators reduced for D+100 survivors); D6 measurement moderate (clinical ascertainment, no central adjudication); D7 reporting low. Overall: serious due to confounding and selection by era/year.

Retrospective non-randomized comparison of two cohorts treated in different eras (Haplo-Cord 1999-2012 vs PTCy-haplo 2012-2014). Significant baseline imbalances reported by authors (higher DRI in Haplo-Cord, higher HCT-CI in PTCy-haplo, TBI use 25% vs 0%). Different conditioning regimens, GvHD prophylaxis, donor types (UCB+TPD vs haplo PBSC), ATG use (100% vs 0%) — confounding by indication is substantial. No multivariable adjustment for confounding reported. Follow-up unbalanced (61 vs 26 months). Outcome ascertainment from multiple GETH centers, standardized definitions. No selective reporting evident.

D1 (confounding): Serious. Retrospective non-contemporaneous comparison; PTCy era 2014-2017 vs CsA-MTX era 2010-2015 with substantial overlap but inherent era confounding (supportive care, antimicrobial prophylaxis). Conditioning intensity also differs significantly between groups (RIC 60% PTCy vs 36% CsA-MTX, P=.015). Multivariate analysis included center, age, sex, comorbidity, diagnosis, DRI, stem cell source, conditioning. D2 (selection): Moderate. Consecutive patients from both centers (1 center contributing to both arms; 1 center contributing only PTCy). D3 (intervention classification): Moderate. Two different PTCy regimens combined (PTCy D+3,+5 + CsA D0 vs PTCy D+3,+4 + CsA + MMF D+5). D4 (deviations): Low. D5 (missing data): Moderate. Single-arm follow-up disparity (PTCy median 15 mo vs MTX-CsA median 60 mo) limits 2-year outcome reliability; some baseline variables (CMV serostatus, infection prophylaxis) not reported. D6 (outcome measurement): Low. Standardized GVHD criteria (Przepiorka 1994 aGVHD; NIH 2014 cGVHD). D7 (selective reporting): Low. Pre-specified endpoints reported.

Retrospective multicenter analysis stratifying outcomes by GvHD prophylaxis (Standard vs ATG vs PTCy) with no adjustment for confounders (donor type, conditioning, disease, age) that strongly influence prophylaxis selection (D1 confounding: serious - haplo patients almost universally PTCy; ATG predominantly for unrelated donors; standard predominantly for matched siblings). D2 selection: moderate - consecutive patients from 2017 transplants at six centers, but heterogeneous indication-by-center. D3 classification: moderate - cGvHD ascertained per 2014 NIH criteria (good), but laGvHD definition variable. D4 deviations: low. D5 missing data: moderate - no specific CMV/infection data and pediatric subgroup analysis limited. D6 measurement: moderate - cGvHD per NIH criteria but center-level variation in scoring. D7 reporting: low. No information on adjusted analyses; only crude proportions and chi-square p-values. Underpowered for severity stratification.

D1 (confounding): serious — retrospective non-randomized assignment to mPTCy vs G-CSF/ATG without protocol-specified allocation; significant baseline imbalance in disease classification (P=.002), HCT-CI (P=.001), donor sex (P=.003), donor type (P=.006), hemoglobin (P=.001), and follow-up duration (P<.001); multivariate Cox adjustment performed but propensity score matching not used. D2 (selection): moderate — multicenter retrospective cohort drawn from 7 Hubei centers without inclusion-criteria flowchart; differing center-level conditioning policies may bias selection. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — within-arm heterogeneity (PTCy D+3/+4 in 2018-2019 vs D+3/+5 in 2020-2021; porcine ALG 100 mg/kg or rabbit ATG 10 mg/kg); regimens are categorized but with internal variation. D4 (deviations): low — uniform GVHD prophylaxis protocols per arm. D5 (missing data): moderate — incomplete reporting of conditioning intensity classification, CMV/HLA serostatus, antifungal/antibacterial prophylaxis, letermovir use; follow-up imbalance (12.7 vs 31.5 months). Overall: serious.

EBMT registry retrospective comparison. D1 confounding: serious - ATG arm has substantially longer follow-up (66.8 vs 23.2 mo PTCy) suggesting era confounding, no PS matching, donor/center heterogeneity. D2 selection: moderate - inclusion well-defined but ATG arm small (n=35). D3 classification of intervention: moderate - GVHD prophylaxis category clear, but ATG agent/dose not granularly reported. D4 deviations: low - registry observational. D5 missing data: moderate - cytogenetics N/A in >50%, ATG dose/agent NR, comorbidity scores limited. D6 outcome measurement: moderate - registry-reported outcomes. D7 selection of reported result: moderate - aGVHD grade II-IV per arm not separately tabulated (only whole cohort), only HRs given for some comparisons. Overall serious.

ROBINS-I: D1 (confounding) serious — comparison entangles GVHD prophylaxis with donor type (PTCy arm 100% haplo; comparator arm 0% haplo / MSD-MUD only) and conditioning intensity (PTCy 90% NMAC/RIC; CsA+MTX 65% MAC) and age (PTCy median 56 vs CsA+MTX 42); no PS-matching or multivariable adjustment for comparison reported; authors acknowledge this limitation. D2 (selection) moderate — consecutive single-center 2003-2023 with 20-year era effects and unclear handling of antifungal-prophylaxis era shifts. D3 (classification of interventions) moderate — uniform institutional protocols. D4 (deviations) low. D5 (missing data) moderate — antifungal exposure heterogeneous (PTCy: 53.8% echinocandin vs CsA+MTX: 82.4% fluconazole) and may differentially classify IMI risk. Overall serious risk of bias for the PTCy-vs-CsA+MTX IFD contrast.

EBMT ALWP registry-based retrospective comparison; PTCy vs ATG groups differ substantially in baseline (conditioning intensity, stem cell source - PTCy more RIC/BM vs ATG more MAC/PBSC; both p<0.01), generating confounding. Heterogeneous ATG dosing (range 2.5-80 mg/kg). HLA typing imputation by in silico method for 66% of pairs based on German registry haplotype frequencies introduces potential measurement error. HLA-DPB1 and HLA-DQ not assessed. Outcome ascertainment via EBMT registry forms - dependence on local center reporting. Time-period heterogeneity (2007-2014). aGVHD and cGVHD endpoints likely reliably scored; relapse/TRM standard. No major issues with selection of reported result.

D1 (randomization process): Low risk. Permuted-block randomization with random block sizes, stratified by donor type and age, allocation concealed via central system; baseline characteristics balanced. D2 (deviations from intended interventions): Some concerns. Open-label trial (unblinded patients, providers); 14.4% noncompliance in CD34 arm (10 crossed to Tac/MTX), 8.2% in PTCy arm (6 crossed to Tac/MTX), 2.6% in control. ITT analysis primary; per-protocol as-treated sensitivity analysis showed similar results. The differential crossover rate raises some concerns even with ITT. D3 (missing outcome data): Low risk. Loss to follow-up minimal (2-3 patients per arm); end-point review committee blinded. D4 (measurement of outcome): Low risk. Independent endpoint review committee blinded to treatment allocation reviewed all CRFS components including cGVHD adjudication. D5 (selection of reported result): Low risk. Pre-specified primary endpoint (CRFS) and secondary endpoints; NCT02345850 registration; protocol available as supplement; gatekeeper hierarchy specified. Overall: Some concerns driven by open-label design and modest differential noncompliance/crossover; otherwise well-conducted phase III RCT.

Multicenter retrospective registry study with 1:2 matching on sex, conditioning intensity, disease stage, Ph-status, cytogenetic risk, plus multivariable Cox/Fine-Gray adjustment for age, KPS, stem cell source, era. D1 (confounding) moderate: key prognosticators matched but MRD status, prior treatment response, HCT-CI missing (77%), graft source not balanced (BM 49% Haplo vs 17% MUD), CMV serostatus and donor age differ markedly between arms. D2 (selection): moderate -- HaploHCT pts and MUD pts drawn from partly different registries (TCT-RC + EBMT for Haplo; EBMT-only for MUD), introducing potential geographic/center selection bias. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate -- GVHD prophylaxis heterogeneous in MUD arm (CNI+MTX 68%, CNI+MMF 29%, sirolimus 2%, ATG in 64%). D4 (deviations): low -- prophylaxis platforms internally consistent. D5 (missing data): moderate -- HCT-CI missing 77%, donor age missing 38%, KPS NA 7%. D6 (outcome measurement): low -- standardized GVHD criteria and clinical endpoints. D7 (selective reporting): low -- pre-specified analysis plan, all endpoints reported.

Retrospective single-center cohort 2005-2019 spanning very long calendar era; PTCy and ATLG groups differ significantly in disease distribution (more ALL/MM and fewer AML/MDS in PTCy), donor type (more MRD/MMRD in PTCy), median year of transplant (2015 vs 2013), conditioning intensity (less busulfan, more TBI in PTCy), and immune suppression backbone. D1 (confounding) serious: NRM univariate difference attenuated on multivariate analysis, indicating substantial confounding. D2 (selection) moderate: consecutive series but groups defined by physician choice over different eras. D3 (intervention classification) moderate: ATLG dose varied (30 vs 60 mg/kg) by donor and over time. D6 (outcome) moderate: infections defined as any positive microbiology requiring therapy - not standardized definition; cGVHD timepoint not explicit.

Single-center retrospective cohort with allocation to PTCy vs TAC by transplant physician discretion. D1 (confounding): serious - PTCy was preferentially used for HLA-mismatched (7/8) transplants (53.3% vs 5.8% in TAC group, P<.0001) and the era of transplantation overlapped with TAC use. D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive patients included. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - 3 different TAC-based regimens pooled. D4-D7: low (deviations from intervention, missing data, outcome measurement, selection of reported result all appear adequately handled with multivariable adjustment for HLA match, conditioning intensity, DRI, etc.).

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing PTCY vs non-PTCY GVHD prophylaxis. D1 (confounding) moderate: substantial baseline imbalance in donor type (49% haplo + 32% MMUD in PTCY vs 73% MUD + 20% MRD in non-PTCY) and conditioning intensity (P=.04), with conditioning regimen assignment by physician choice and changing era. Authors performed multivariable analysis but did not appear to formally adjust for donor type when comparing PTCY effects. D2 (selection) low: consecutive identification from institutional database. D3 (intervention classification) low: well-defined PTCY 50 mg/kg D+3,+4 vs MTX+tacrolimus+/-sirolimus regimens. D4 (deviations) low: standard institutional protocols. D5 (missing data) moderate: 11% cytogenetics missing; comorbidities prospectively validated by 2 reviewers. D6 (outcome measurement) low: NRM/OS objective endpoints. D7 (reporting) moderate: arm-level NRM/OS at standard timepoints not separately reported in main paper; outcomes primarily reported stratified by HCT-CI score.

Single-center retrospective comparison with non-randomized allocation (insurance/trial enrollment driving PTCy vs conventional). Significant baseline imbalances: graft source (BM 83% PTCy vs 63% conv, p=0.02), HLA class-I mismatch (88% PTCy vs 57% conv, p<0.001), and age (median 50 vs 54, p=0.05). Confounding (D1) serious as conditioning regimens differed by arm (Flu/Mel-based for PTCy vs heterogeneous including Bu/Flu for conventional) and ATG/in-vivo TCD exposure differs by design. Selection (D2) moderate given the contemporaneous controls. Classification of interventions (D3) clear and unambiguous but with multiple co-interventions changing across era. Deviations (D4) low - both groups had defined protocols. Missing data (D5) moderate - 1 patient missing aGVHD data. Outcome measurement (D6) moderate as GVHD requires clinical judgment but standardized criteria used. Selection of reported result (D7) low - prespecified primary endpoint reported in full. Overall serious risk of bias.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing 3 donor types under uniform PTCy backbone, with multivariable Cox/Fine-Gray adjustment. D1 (confounding): moderate - non-randomized donor assignment; major confounders adjusted (age, HCT-CI, DRI, conditioning intensity) but unmeasured confounders likely (center practice variation by year, donor selection bias, MMF use distribution differs by arm 96% vs 47% vs 26%). D2 (selection): moderate - all eligible patients receiving PTCy 2015-2020 included; MMUD (n=19) and ex vivo/in vivo T-cell depleted grafts excluded explicitly. D3 (classification of intervention): low - donor type unambiguous, PTCy dosing uniform. D4 (deviation from intended): low - retrospective; intent-to-treat not applicable. D5 (missing data): low - small proportions missing for sex match, cGVHD severity (8-13%). D6 (measurement of outcome): low - aGVHD/cGVHD by Mount Sinai/NIH 2014, NRM/OS standard. D7 (reporting): low - all prespecified secondary outcomes reported.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing PTCy vs Tac/MTX (+/-ATG) GVHD prophylaxis. D1 (confounding): serious - PTCy and Tac/MTX cohorts differ substantially in age, race/ethnicity distribution, disease type (more myeloid in PTCy), graft source, and conditioning intensity; era effect (PTCy adopted later, median HCT year 2018 vs 2016); MV adjustment performed but residual confounding likely. D2 (selection): moderate - retrospective consecutive inclusion, but allocation between PTCy vs Tac/MTX was based on era/protocol availability. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - heterogeneous MMF use within PTCy arm (per protocol enrollment). D4 (deviations from intended): low - uniform institutional protocols. D5 (missing data): moderate - some baseline covariates with missing values (DRI 4% missing). D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - clinical ascertainment without independent adjudication. D7 (selective reporting): low - prespecified outcomes reported.

CIBMTR registry retrospective cohort sub-analysis. D1 (confounding): moderate - significant baseline imbalances (graft source, conditioning intensity, T-cell vs B-cell immunophenotype) addressed by multivariate Cox/Fine-Gray adjustment with backward stepwise selection. Treatment selection era-confounded (haplo more in later years 2016 vs 2015 MUD). D2 (classification of intervention): low - donor type unambiguous. D3 (deviations): moderate - residual donor selection bias; missing data on HLA-DPB1, donor parity, KIR; no chimerism, CRS, or graft composition data. D4 (missing data): low - registry-level. D5 (measurement): low - outcomes standardized via CIBMTR data collection. D6/D7 (selection/reporting): low - pre-specified outcomes per CIBMTR protocol; no clinically reported infectious outcomes (BSI/IFI/CMV) reducing applicability to PTCy MA infection mediator framework.

Retrospective registry analysis using publicly available CIBMTR deidentified dataset (same as Shaffer 2024). Strengths: large N=10025, predefined cohorts, comprehensive multivariable adjustment (IPTW, overlap weighting, LASSO, XGBoost machine learning), false discovery rate correction, multiple sensitivity analyses including ATG exclusion. Weaknesses: D1 (confounding) moderate due to inherent registry selection bias and residual confounding by indication (cohort assignment based on physician/center preference); D5 (missing data) moderate as some variables in publicly available CIBMTR dataset have limited granularity (race/ethnicity categorization, ATG dose); MMUD-CNI small group (n=459) showed poor covariate overlap producing volatile estimates. Concordance index 0.63-0.64 indicates moderate discriminatory ability. Outcomes for combined PTCy cohort (not separately by MUD-PTCy vs MMUD-PTCy in main Table 2).

Retrospective two-center observational study with strong confounding between donor type, GVHD prophylaxis, and graft source (HAPLO is 100% BM from Genoa; UD includes PBSC/BM/CB across both centers). All UD recipients had ATG and all HAPLO had PT-CY by design - donor and prophylaxis platform cannot be separated. Study population is a selected subset (CMV-viremic patients receiving foscarnet), limiting generalizability and creating selection bias for downstream outcomes (OS, NRM). D1 (confounding) serious: centers, donor, prophylaxis, and graft source confounded. D2 (selection) serious: only foscarnet-treated CMV patients included; ganciclovir-treated and CMV-non-reactivators excluded. D3 (classification of intervention) moderate: clear definitions but no detail on individual patient regimens beyond schema. D4 (deviations) low: protocol-defined approach. D5 (missing data) moderate: 6 patients missing CMV serostatus; no missing-data handling described. Outcomes reflect foscarnet-treated CMV-viremic subgroup, not the full transplant population - severely limits use for primary outcomes of interest.

Single-center retrospective Italian cohort, San Martino Genoa 2010-2016. D1 (confounding) moderate: multivariable Cox adjusts for age, diagnosis, disease phase, year, donor; but unmeasured confounders (mucosal injury severity, CMV serostatus, gut decontamination practices) not addressed. D2 (selection of participants) serious: donor selection strongly confounded with era (CBT 93% in 2010-2012 declining to 7% in 2013-2016; haplo 33% rising to 67%); MAC vs RIC distribution and active-disease distribution differ markedly across arms. D3 (intervention classification) moderate: PTCy is donor-confounded (used only in haplo arm), so the donor-type comparison is also a PTCy-vs-no-PTCy comparison; cannot disentangle PTCy effect from haplo donor effect. D4 (deviations) low: standard protocols. D5 (missing data) low: cross-checked microbiology database. D6 (outcome measurement) low: blood culture-based, microbiology-confirmed. D7 (selection of reported result) moderate: focused on pre-engraftment BSI only; aGVHD/cGVHD/OS/1yr NRM not reported (no D+100 GVHD or 1yr survival data). Overall: serious risk of bias for any inference about PTCy effect.

Single-center retrospective cohort with conditioning assignment by physician discretion (strong selection bias by age, fitness). PSCA used to adjust for measured confounders but residual confounding likely (D1=serious). D2 classification of interventions: clearly defined. D3 deviations: clinical practice may have varied across the 7+ year span. D4 missing data: 6/89 missing KPS, 1 missing ABO, 4 missing CD34, otherwise complete. D5 measurement: outcomes are objective. D6 reporting: limited correspondence format reporting; key infection endpoints not reported. Overall serious due to small MAC group (n=24), wide CIs, and lack of D+100 timepoint reporting for several key endpoints.

Retrospective single-center cohort with substantial era confounding (PTcy group transplanted predominantly 2014-2020, thymoglobulin predominantly 2008-2018; median year PTcy 2018 vs thymoglobulin 2013, P<.001). Baseline imbalances in age (62 vs 53, P=.04), conditioning intensity (MAC 20% vs 59%, P=.002), and follow-up (1.13 vs 5.27 years for survivors). D1 confounding serious. D2 selection of participants serious - intervention assignment by era and physician discretion, not random. PSCA used as mitigation but could not adjust for unmeasured era effects (peritransplantation supportive care improvements). D3 classification of interventions moderate - GVHD prophylaxis strategies well documented. D4 deviation low. D5 missing data moderate. D6/D7 reporting low. Subgroup analysis restricted to post-2014 patients showed loss of all significant findings (aGVHD, cGVHD, NRM HRs all NS), reinforcing era confounding as primary concern.

Single-arm descriptive Letter to Editor from a single US center (KUMC). No comparator arm and no PTCy contrast: outcomes are stratified only post-hoc by EBV+ vs EBV- status, which is not a treatment contrast. D1 (confounding) serious due to lack of any comparator. Enrollment dates and follow-up duration not stated, limiting D3 (classification of intervention) and D4 (deviations). EBV ascertainment was prospective protocol-based weekly PCR monitoring (low bias for D5). PTLD ascertainment described qualitatively without standardized criteria stated; absence of PTLD across N=63 could reflect short follow-up or reporting incompleteness. Overall serious risk of bias. Paper excluded from quantitative synthesis per single_arm_descriptive_excluded rule.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis. D1 (confounding): moderate - multivariate Cox adjustment for age, sex, KPS, graft source, DRI, transplant year, TBI, conditioning intensity, CMV combination, plus center frailty random effect; sensitivity matching analyses supported conclusions; however unmeasured confounders likely (era effect since PTCy arm transplanted more recently; centers used predominantly one or the other regimen; biology of malignancies, infection covariates not collected). D2 (selection): moderate - selection by data completeness for HLA-match/DRI/GVHD prophylaxis introduces possible bias; 5-7/10 MMUD excluded (n=24). D3 (intervention classification): low - GVHD prophylaxis well-defined by ATG vs PTCy. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low - prophylaxis fixed by protocol/era. D5 (missing data): moderate - ATG dosing missing for 120/318 patients (38%); follow-up censored at 2y to ensure comparable FU between arms (PTCy median FU 2.1y vs ATG 3.8y). D6 (measurement of outcome): moderate - acute/chronic GVHD grading per EBMT registry but no detailed quality audit for outcomes; NRM/OS robust. D7 (selection of reported result): low - all prespecified outcomes reported. Overall: moderate.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing prospectively treated PTCy patients (2014-2016) with a historical control of CNI-treated patients (2006-2014). D1 (confounding): serious — significant temporal confounding (year of transplant differed substantially, p<0.001); diagnostics, supportive care, and treatment paradigms likely changed over 10-year span. Differential salvage status (CNI 36% vs PTCy 14%, p=0.0008) and ALL distribution. Multivariate adjustment performed but residual confounding likely. D2 (selection): moderate — consecutive PTCy patients vs historical control may not be fully comparable. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate — clear PTCy vs CNI assignment but heterogeneous CNI regimen (mixed tacrolimus/cyclosporine and MMF/MTX). D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low. D6 (outcome measurement): low — standard cumulative incidence with competing risks. D7 (selection of reported result): moderate — multiple outcome subgroup analyses reported without pre-specification.

Retrospective single-center cohort with non-randomized GVHD prophylaxis assignment by era/institutional protocol (switch during 2023 MTX shortage). D1 (confounding): moderate - era effect confounded (PTCy received post-2023, TAC/MTX includes 2018-2025 patients), unbalanced follow-up time (PTCy median 1.1 yr vs TAC/MTX 3.3 yr), unbalanced graft source (PBSC 96% vs 77%), TBI use (43% vs 22%); authors used propensity score adjustment. D2 (selection of participants): moderate - real-world cohort, some MRD-unknown patients excluded from subgroup analysis. D3 (classification of interventions): low - GVHD prophylaxis well-defined per institutional protocol. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing outcome data): low - only 16% MRD-unknown in TAC/MTX arm. D6 (measurement of outcomes): low - MAGIC and NIH 2014 criteria; outcomes adjudicated by 2 clinicians. D7 (selection of reported result): moderate - extensive supplementary subgroup analyses suggest possible selective emphasis.

Retrospective non-randomized comparison with strong center effect: TCD performed exclusively at Vall d'Hebron Barcelona (1 center) and PTCy-Sir-MMF exclusively at 2 Valencia centers (HUPLF + HCU) — confounding by center is inseparable from intervention. Different conditioning regimens used in each arm (TBI-based or Bu-Mel-Flu for TCD; TT-Bu-Flu/Bu-Flu/reduced TT-Bu-Flu for PTCy). Different CMV preemptive treatment thresholds between arms (100 copies/mL TCD vs 1500 IU/mL PTCy) biases CMV outcome comparison. Different ATG use, different graft manipulation, different stem cell dose (median 5.4 vs 7.3 x10^6 CD34+/kg, P<.001). Donor type imbalance (TCD: 31% MMUD; PTCy: 0% MMUD; P<.001). DRI imbalance (PTCy higher risk; P=.03). Follow-up imbalance (PTCy 16 mo vs TCD 24 mo). Multivariable Cox model adjusts for major covariates but cannot adjust for center, conditioning, and CMV threshold simultaneously. Outcome ascertainment standardized but at different institutions. D1 (confounding) and D2 (selection/intervention assignment by center) judged serious; D3-D7 moderate.

ROBINS-I for retrospective registry study. D1 (confounding): serious - significant baseline imbalance in donor type (MSD 74% vs 50%) and prior autologous HSCT (77% vs 67%), with limited adjustment available in registry data (no data on PD-1 inhibitors for 80% of cohort). D2 (selection): moderate - center- and physician-level selection of GVHD platform; PTCy uptake increased over enrollment window. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate - heterogeneous PTCy regimens (PTCy+2 drugs 72%, +1 drug 23%, alone 5%) and conventional regimens (CsA+MTX 51%, CsA+MMF 27%, CsA alone 8%, other 14%); PTCy dose/schedule not reported. D4 (deviations): low - intent-to-treat registry follow-up. D5 (missing data): low - core outcomes complete for almost all patients. D6 (measurement): low - GVHD and survival outcomes assessed using standard EBMT registry case-report forms. D7 (reporting): low - all prespecified outcomes reported. Overall serious due to confounding by indication and substantial intervention heterogeneity.

Retrospective JSTCT/TRUMP nationwide registry analysis. D1 (confounding): moderate - significant baseline imbalances between groups in disease status at HCT (more CR in ATG-MUD), conditioning intensity (more MAC in MUD arms), TBI use, donor age, and sex compatibility; multivariable Cox model adjusts for major confounders but residual confounding likely (pre-transplant chemotherapy, genomic data, center effects, donor selection by physician preference). D2 (selection): low - consecutive AML-PBSC patients in nationwide registry. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - heterogeneous PTCy dosing (50+50, 40+40, others) and heterogeneous ATG regimens (dose not captured). D4-D7: low - end-points and reporting well-defined, no missing primary outcome data, complete reporting of pre-specified endpoints. Letermovir era not separable; CMV/BSI/IFI infection outcomes not reported individually (only cause-of-death tabulation).

Single-arm descriptive cohort with no comparator; protocol-excluded per spec (single_arm_descriptive_excluded). RoB assessment not applicable since the paper does not contribute to PTCy vs non-PTCy contrasts. Tracked for PRISMA only.

CIBMTR registry retrospective cohort comparing HaploCy (haplo+PTCy), SibCy (MSD+PTCy), and SibCNI (MSD+CNI). D1 (confounding): moderate — adjusted for major confounders via stepwise Cox model and centre effects, but unmeasured confounding likely given retrospective registry design (no info on antifungal/antibacterial/CMV prophylaxis, no immune reconstitution data, no severity grading). D2 (selection): moderate — centres without any haplo HCT excluded which may introduce selection bias; otherwise consecutive registry capture. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — GVHD prophylaxis groups well-defined but specific PTCy schedule, doses, and concurrent IS not standardised. D4 (deviations): low — observational, no protocol deviations relevant. D5 (missing data): moderate — CRVI ascertainment relies on centre reporting; no standardised testing protocol; outpatient CRVIs likely under-reported per authors' own discussion; no LRTI vs URI differentiation; no severity data. D6 (measurement of outcome): moderate — CRVI definition based on organism reported per CIBMTR forms manual; no central confirmation or standardised methodology. D7 (selective reporting): low — pre-specified outcomes consistent with discussion. Overall moderate.

ROBINS-I assessment: D1 (confounding) serious - retrospective registry with non-randomized GVHD prophylaxis assignment heavily confounded by era (PTCy use more common in later years), donor type (PTCy predominant in haplo/MMUD), and conditioning intensity. Multivariable adjustment partial. D2 (selection of participants) moderate - registry inclusion required complete reporting; selection by center reporting patterns. D3 (classification of interventions) moderate - GVHD prophylaxis classified into composite categories (CNI+MMF, CNI+MTX, CNI+other, PTCy+other) without granular dosing detail. D4 (deviations from intended interventions) low - registry observational. D5 (missing data) moderate - KPS missing in 4%, HCT-CI not reported in 6%, GVHD prophylaxis subgroups vary (n=33-37 across analyses suggesting some missing data). D6 (outcome measurement) moderate - registry-reported outcomes; uniform competing risks framework but no central adjudication of GVHD grade or relapse. D7 (selection of reported result) low - prespecified endpoints with adjusted models. Overall serious risk of bias due to confounding inherent to non-randomized registry comparisons.

Single-center retrospective cohort study comparing MUD vs haplo at KUMC 2016-2021. D1 (confounding) moderate: significant baseline imbalances between arms (age, sex, ethnicity, donor age/sex, TBI use, graft type, GVHD prophylaxis) but multivariate adjustment performed for key confounders. D2 (selection) moderate: retrospective, but inclusion of all consecutive HCT recipients with >=1 year follow-up requirement may exclude early deaths. D3 (intervention classification) low: well-defined donor types and uniform haplo prophylaxis. D4 (deviations) low. D5 (missing data) low. D6 (outcome measurement) low: standardized MAGIC and NIH 2014 criteria. D7 (selective reporting) moderate: no infection-specific outcomes (BSI, CMV, IFI) reported in detail; cause-of-death breakdown reported but no D+100/D+180 timepoints for infection. Heterogeneity in MUD arm GVHD prophylaxis (87% Tac/MTX, 13% PT-Cy) is a limitation for the MUD-vs-haplo comparison interpretation.

Joint EBMT+CIBMTR registry retrospective comparison of haplo vs MUD with PTCy in lymphoma 2010-2019. D1 (confounding): serious - non-randomized donor selection with heterogeneity in disease subtype (HL 44% haplo vs 28% MUD), GVHD prophylaxis (PTCy+CNI+MMF 90% haplo vs 54% MUD), graft source (40% BM haplo vs 9% MUD), donor age (median 37 vs 28 yr), patient age (46 vs 53 yr); authors mitigated via multivariable Cox + 2 propensity score sensitivity analyses (IPTW and matched pairs). D2 (selection): moderate - donor selection at center discretion may introduce institutional bias. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - heterogeneous GVHD prophylaxis classified together as PTCy-based. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low - small missingness in HCT-CI 23% haplo / 19% MUD. D6 (measurement): low - registry-defined standard outcomes. D7 (selective reporting): moderate - GVHD severity grading system not explicitly stated. Overall serious due to D1.

Retrospective JSTCT/JDCHCT registry cohort; donor selection (haplo vs CBT, and donor age) influenced by physician judgment and institutional factors (D1 confounding moderate). Patients aged 16-70 with AML/ALL/MDS/CML undergoing first HSCT 2016-2021; ATG/alemtuzumab recipients excluded by design (D2 selection moderate due to retrospective selection of donor groups for comparison). Standardized data collection through TRUMP (D3 low). GVHD graded per 1994 Consensus and Shulman 1980 Seattle criteria; clinically diagnosed at each contributing center (D4/D5 low). Outcomes ascertained from registry follow-up (D6/D7 low). Multivariate Cox adjustments for disease risk, disease type, HCT-CI, PS, conditioning intensity, sex mismatch. Short median follow-up (443 days) limits long-term assessment.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis comparing HaploSCT (92.7% PTCy) vs MSD (4.2% PTCy, mostly CsA/MTX +/- ATG). D1 (confounding): serious - large imbalances in conditioning intensity (MAC 68% vs 83.2%), TBI use (42.6% vs 64.9%), CR2 status (33.4% vs 16.7%), BM graft use (46.2% vs 18.6%), GVHD prophylaxis (PTCy vs CsA/MTX), and ATG; MVA + PS adjustment performed which partially mitigates but unmeasured confounders (HCT-CI not collected, MRD missing in ~45%, no TKI data for Ph+ ALL) remain. D2 (selection): moderate - registry-reported cohort with center-driven donor selection. D3 (exposure classification): moderate - donor type is well-defined but PTCy vs ATG vs CsA/MTX heterogeneity within MSD arm. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low - actual treatments captured. D5 (missing data): moderate - 45% MRD missing, KPS 7%, engraftment 51 missing. D6/D7 NA for ROBINS-I (last two columns repurposed). cGVHD graded by Seattle criteria, not NIH 2014.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis. Imbalanced baseline characteristics: ATG arm had more relapsed/refractory disease (30.6% vs 16.4%, P=0.008), less TBI use (26.5% vs 45.2%, P<0.001), more PBSC (68.4% vs 47.9%), and earlier transplant era (median 2011 vs 2015). Patients receiving both ATG and PTCy (n=37) excluded; treatment allocation by center practice/era introduces strong confounding (D1, D2 serious). Multivariate Cox adjustment for measured confounders but unmeasured (MRD status, ATG product type, ATG dose - documented in only 81 subjects) limits causal inference. No center effect detected except chronic GvHD. Outcome ascertainment by EBMT registry routine reporting with audit.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective cohort study (n=127 AML CR2 PTCy URD). D1 (confounding): moderate - no comparator arm, era spans 2010-2019, missing cytogenetics in 23%, no MRD/molecular data, no HCT-CI. D2 (selection): low - consecutive eligible registry patients. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - heterogeneous PTCy adjuncts (10+ IS combinations), ATG dose/agent unreported. D4 (deviations): low - registry-based observational. D5 (missing data): moderate - 22.8% missing cytogenetics, missing pre-transplant therapy data. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - registry-reported, no central adjudication. D7 (reported result selection): low - prespecified outcomes per ALWP-EBMT standard.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective comparison of haploSCT+PTCy in sAML vs de novo AML, both PTCy arms (no PTCy-vs-non-PTCy contrast). D1 confounding: moderate - propensity-matched 2:1 analysis performed (exact match on cytogenetics, conditioning, graft source, sex match; nearest neighbor on age, KPS); HCT-CI not in PS due to missing data, frailty term for center heterogeneity in MV. D2 selection: moderate - clear inclusion criteria (haplo, PTCy, CR1, 2010-2021), exclusion of T-depletion. D3 classification: low - PTCy vs non-PTCy not the contrast; sAML vs de novo well-defined. D4 deviations: low - registry observational. D5 missing data: moderate - HCT-CI missing 265/1711 (~15%), MRD missing 868/1711 (~51%); cytogenetics complete. D6 outcome measurement: moderate - registry-reported outcomes, no central adjudication. D7 selection of reported result: low - both arm-specific and HR results reported per Tables 3, 4, 6. Overall moderate.

Large EBMT ALWP registry comparing PTCy (n=707) vs no-PTCy (n=6342) URD HSCT for AML in CR1. D1 (confounding): serious - significant baseline imbalances (age, HLA match, MAC, CMV serostatus, year of HSCT, in vivo TCD use); addressed by multivariate Cox with random center effect and pair-matched propensity analysis but residual confounding likely (no HCT-CI, no measurable residual disease, no front-line treatment data). D2 (selection): moderate - registry-based with all consecutive transplants reported; possible center-level selection of PTCy vs ATG strategy. D3 (intervention classification): low - clearly defined GVHD prophylaxis arms. D4 (deviations): low - registry observational design. D5 (missing data): moderate - molecular remission data missing in 51.6% (3638/7049); cytogenetics missing in 17%. D6 (outcome measurement): low - EBMT standard data forms with established criteria. D7 (selection of reported result): low - all key transplant outcomes pre-specified and reported. Overall serious due to D1 confounding despite analytic mitigation.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective study. D1 (confounding): moderate - propensity score matching and MVA used; standardized mean differences <10% in matched cohort. Significant baseline differences (year of transplant, conditioning intensity, donor type distribution, CMV) addressed by MVA + matched pair. Unmeasured confounders (ATG dose/agent, PTCy dose/schedule, MRD ~50% missing, frontline therapy, mutation profiling) acknowledged by authors. D2 (selection): moderate - registry-based with potential selection bias by center practice. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - intervention defined by recorded GVHD prophylaxis but heterogeneity in CNI choice (TAC vs CSA) and ATG agent/dose. D4-D5 (deviations from intended/missing data): low. D6-D7 (outcome measurement/selection of reported result): low - standardized EBMT outcome definitions and registry quality control.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective study. D1 (confounding): serious - donor selection is non-random; physician/center preference for haplo vs MMUD likely correlated with patient factors and era; pre-HSCT MRD missing for ~50%, mutation profiling missing for ~50%. D2 (selection): low - consecutive registry reporting required. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - donor type/age clearly defined but PTCy platform heterogeneity not characterized in main text. D4 (deviation from intended): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - significant missingness for MRD, FLT3, NPM1; donor characteristics complete. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate - GVHD and infection outcomes ascertained per center reporting without central adjudication. D7 (reported result): low. Overall: serious risk of confounding by selection bias and missing baseline data.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis. D1 (confounding): serious - heterogeneous PTCy regimens (9 different combinations) and substantial baseline imbalance (age, KPS, conditioning intensity, year of HCT) between arms; propensity-matched analysis mitigates but cannot fully address residual confounding from unmeasured factors (MRD status, supportive care). D2 (selection): moderate - registry inclusion limited to patients reported between 2010-2019 with sufficient data. D3 (classification of intervention): moderate - PTCy intervention heterogeneous across multiple adjunct IS combinations. D4 (deviation): low - registry follow-up. D5 (missing data): moderate - missing KPS in 81 cases, missing FLT3-ITD/NPM1 in ~30%, MRD not available. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate - GVHD reporting varies across EBMT centers, no central adjudication. D7 (selective reporting): low - all standard EBMT outcomes reported. Overall serious due to confounding and intervention heterogeneity.

Registry-based retrospective cohort using JSTCT TRUMP2 dataset. D1 (confounding): moderate - multivariable Cox/cause-specific hazard models adjusted for patient age, sex, PS, HCT-CI, disease risk, cytogenetic risk, prior azacytidine, conditioning intensity, donor age, time from diagnosis, and transplantation period, but genetic mutational profile (acknowledged limitation) and center effect not adjusted. Treatment assignment driven by donor availability and physician/institutional policies (selection bias acknowledged). D2 (selection): moderate - donor selection bias and center effects acknowledged by authors; haplo-PBSCT cohort had shorter follow-up (median 399 days vs 1118 MUD-BMT, 786 MUD-PBSCT) and more recent transplantation (70.6% in 2018-2020 vs 39.8% MUD-BMT, 57.3% MUD-PBSCT). D3 (intervention classification): low - GVHD prophylaxis well-characterized via TRUMP2. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective registry, intent-to-treat structure. D5 (missing data): low - all key baseline covariates available; minor missing for cytogenetics (~1%). D6 (measurement): low - GVHD graded by MAGIC/NIH consensus; engraftment objectively defined. D7 (reporting): low - prespecified endpoints per Methods. Overall moderate.

Large nationwide JSTCT TRUMP registry of adult ALL patients (n=1999) comparing PTCy-haplo vs single-unit UCB transplantation 2013-2021. Strengths: nationwide coverage, propensity-matched sensitivity analysis, multivariate adjustment for OS/DFS/relapse/NRM. Limitations: retrospective with substantial baseline imbalance (ABO mismatch, era - 76.7% PTCy-haplo in 2018-2021 vs 48.5% UCB; phenotype, sex, age). Significant confounding by indication (donor selection driven by clinical/logistical factors); pre-letermovir vs letermovir era spans both groups; missing detailed prophylaxis platform data (PTCy dose, CNI, MMF, ATG use not specified in main text). Outcome ascertainment standardized via TRUMP. Short report format limits methodological detail.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing RIC vs NMA conditioning in NHL. D1 (confounding) serious: significant baseline imbalance — RIC arm younger (median 56 vs 60 yr, P<.001), enriched for aggressive histology (DLBCL 28% vs 18%; T-cell lymphoma 30% vs 17%); NMA arm enriched for ATG (45% vs 6%) and rituximab (49% vs 2.7%) reflecting enrollment on parallel phase 2 trial; clinician selection of conditioning regimen could not be fully accounted for. D2 (selection) moderate: consecutive patients meeting eligibility but conditioning choice not randomized. D3 (intervention classification) moderate: heterogeneous RIC regimens (Flu-Mel, Flu-Cy-TT-4Gy-TBI, Flu-Bu-4, Flu-Cy-4Gy-TBI) grouped. D4 (deviations from intended interventions) low. D5 (missing data) moderate: 27% missing ethnicity. D6 (outcome measurement) low: standard transplant outcomes with established definitions; competing-risk methods used. D7 (selective reporting) low: pre-specified primary/secondary outcomes reported. Not relevant for PTCy MA Comparison 3 because PTCy-stratified outcomes are not reported.

Retrospective sequential cohort comparing ER-SCT program era (Oct 2017-Sep 2018) vs pre-program historical controls (Jan 2015-Sep 2017) at MD Anderson. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - concurrent practice changes including a shift to F-Bu/PTCy regimens occurred between eras and act as time-varying confounders not fully separable from the ER-SCT intervention (acknowledged by authors). D2 (selection): SERIOUS - no concurrent controls feasible because all age >=65 patients were enrolled in ER-SCT after program initiation; historical-control design introduces selection by era. D3 (classification of interventions): MODERATE - ER-SCT enrollment well-defined but in-hospital elements applied as standard practice to all age >=65 patients including non-enrollees. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): LOW - all 64 eligible patients analyzed. D5 (missing data): LOW. D6 (measurement of outcomes): LOW (objective outcomes NRM/OS/relapse from departmental database). D7 (selective reporting): LOW.

D1 (confounding): moderate - retrospective single-center cohort; PTCy use (27%) not analyzed as separate variable for BSI outcomes; PTCy collinear with haplo/MMUD donor type. D2 (selection of participants/deviations from interventions): serious - this paper does NOT contrast PTCy vs non-PTCy; outcomes reported for full mixed-prophylaxis cohort, severely limiting its utility for the PTCy meta-analysis. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - PTCy use is documented but not granular (dose, schedule, agent specifics not reported). D4 (missing data): low - whole cohort included; complete BSI ascertainment via active blood culture surveillance. D5 (measurement of outcomes): low - standardized ECDC/CDC bacteremia definitions; weekly surveillance blood cultures; standardized empirical antibiotic protocol. D6 (selection of reported result): moderate - paper reports BSI outcomes only; no IFI or CMV outcomes reported despite available data. D7 (other): low. Overall serious risk of bias for the PTCy MA question because the paper does not stratify BSI outcomes by PTCy receipt.

Registry-based retrospective cohort using JSTCT TRUMP2 data. D1 (confounding): moderate - donor choice driven by attending physician preference/institutional policy; adjusted Cox models include 8 prespecified confounders but residual confounding likely (no DLI use, no specific PTCy/CNI doses, no GVHD prophylaxis details for uCBT MMF vs MTX subgroups). D2 (selection): moderate - PTCY-haplo skewed to later era (79% in 2018-2021) and CMV-positive recipients/donors; selection bias acknowledged by authors. D3 (classification): low - registry-coded donor/graft. D4 (deviations): low - both arms received uniform per-protocol GVHD prophylaxis (PTCy with CNI+MMF for haplo; mixed CNI-based for uCBT). D5 (missing data): low - <5% missing for key covariates; minor missingness for PS, HCT-CI, CMV status. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standardized TRUMP2 registry outcome capture. D7 (selective reporting): low - all prespecified primary/secondary endpoints reported with HRs and figures. Overall moderate ROBINS-I due to confounding and selection bias inherent in retrospective registry comparison.

Prospective single-center observational cohort with non-randomized GVHD prophylaxis allocation (PT-Cy vs ATG vs none) driven by donor type (haplo->PT-Cy historically) and era/protocol; confounding by donor type is the main concern (D1 moderate). Selection (D2) moderate because the PT-Cy and ATG arms were not contemporaneous in a randomized sense though all patients in 2013-2015 were included consecutively. Classification of HHV-6 (D3) low - prospective weekly PCR with prospective ECIL-based EOD adjudication. Deviations (D4) low - non-interventional design. Missing data (D5) low - 90% evaluable for immunology subset, full clinical data on 208. Outcome measurement (D6) low - blinded virology lab. Selection of reported result (D7) low - prespecified outcomes. Overall moderate due to confounding-by-indication on donor type/era and lack of arm-stratified outcome reporting.

Single-center retrospective historical comparison with substantial confounding from temporal era differences (ATG 2010-2014 vs PT-Cy 2015-2018) - D1 serious. Selection: consecutive patients with consistent inclusion criteria - D2 moderate (era selection inherent in design). Classification of interventions: PT-Cy vs ATG well-defined - D3 moderate (heterogeneous conditioning regimens between eras: ATG group received predominantly FB2 RIC vs PT-Cy group received predominantly TBF or Flu-Cy-TBI which the authors acknowledge as a confounder). Deviations from intended interventions: standard protocols - D4 low. Missing data: infection data only available for 28/40 ATG patients - D5 low (acknowledged). Measurement: standard MAGIC/Glucksberg and NIH cGVHD criteria, blinded outcome ascertainment unlikely required - D6 low. Reporting: complete outcomes reported - D7 low. Authors performed multivariate Cox adjustment for age, conditioning, HCT-CI, DRI but residual confounding from era and conditioning heterogeneity remains substantial. Overall serious.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis with three non-randomized donor/prophylaxis groups (non-PTCy UD n=1094, PTCy UD n=113, PTCy MMRD n=134). D1 (confounding): serious - substantial imbalance in donor type, TCD use (83% in non-PTCy UD vs 19%/9% in PTCy arms), conditioning intensity, TKI exposure, and CMV serostatus across arms; multivariable adjustment performed but residual confounding likely with such heterogeneous prophylaxis platforms. D2 (selection): moderate - registry-based selection of CML patients 2012-2019; some centers may report selectively. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - PTCy arms heterogeneous (different CNI agents, +/- MMF, +/- MTX, +/- sirolimus); non-PTCy arm heterogeneous (CsA-based 88%, with TCD in 83%). D4 (deviations): low - registry reports actual treatments delivered. D5 (missing data): moderate - HCT-CI missing in 28%, TKI data missing in 26%, treatment after allo-HCT missing in 70%; multiple imputation used for OS sensitivity analysis with similar results. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate - GVHD graded by 2 different criteria depending on year; outcomes ascertained from registry-reported data without independent adjudication; explicit statement that infection data inadequate. D7 (selection of reported result): moderate - main outcomes pre-specified but post-hoc subgroup analyses possible. Overall: serious due to severe baseline confounding and heterogeneous prophylaxis composition within arms.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing two donor/conditioning/GVHD-prophylaxis packages. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - donor matching status assigned the package, so donor type/conditioning/GVHD prophylaxis are confounded together; baseline differences in CR1 proportion (82% vs 70%) and HCT-CI (HCT-CI 0: 37% vs 11%) favor the ETOP arm. D2 (selection): MODERATE - all consecutive patients meeting inclusion criteria, but ETOP arm spans 2010-2020 while FLU arm is entirely 2015-2020, introducing era effects. D3 (intervention classification): MODERATE - package definitions clear but two-step assignment by donor match. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): LOW. D5 (missing data): LOW for survival outcomes, but pre-HCT MRD data missing in 29% (78/269). D6 (outcome measurement): MODERATE - retrospective abstraction; engraftment/GVHD outcomes objectively assessed. D7 (selective reporting): LOW. Infection-specific outcomes (BSI, CMV, IFI) NOT reported despite likely being collected.

Single-center retrospective cohort. D1 (confounding): serious - non-randomized donor allocation by IPC guideline (UD preferred if available, HRD if UD unavailable); HRD arm initially enriched for higher-risk/advanced disease per authors; significant baseline imbalances in disease type (myeloid 37 vs 49%), lymphoid distribution (HL 22 vs 6%, NHL 28 vs 13%, ALL 3 vs 18%), conditioning intensity (66% NMAC in HRD vs 0% in UD), and graft source (BM 27 vs 5%); multivariate Cox adjustment and match-paired analysis partly mitigate but residual confounding by indication remains substantial. D2 (selection): moderate - all consecutive patients <60 yr undergoing haplo or UD allo-HSCT in same period included; no missing cases reported but historical period dating boundaries not specified in text. D3 (intervention classification): low - donor type/regimen unambiguous. D4 (deviations): low - per-protocol intent. D5 (missing data): low - 209 patients with outcomes reported. D6 (measurement of outcomes): low - standardized definitions (Glucksberg, NIH, EBMT criteria) with competing-risk analysis. D7 (selection of reported result): low - all primary endpoints reported. Overall judgement serious driven by D1 confounding by indication and treatment-platform heterogeneity (PT-Cy+CSA+MMF vs ATG+CSA+/-MMF) confounded with donor type.

D1 (Confounding) serious: retrospective single-center cohort with marked imbalance between arms - donor distribution (19% HID in ATG-PTCY vs 0% in Other, P=6.15e-7), disease distribution (P=4.12e-3), in vivo TCD use (100% vs 58%, P=2.04e-8), and arm composition (ATG-PTCY arm uniform vs heterogeneous comparator). MVA limited to age, HCTCI, gender, disease, donor, CMV, conditioning (7 covariates). D2 (Selection) moderate: consecutive patients age >=60 transplanted Dec 2013-Jul 2017, but arm allocation determined by era/donor type rather than randomization. D3 (Classification of interventions): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis allocation per institutional protocol; clearly recorded. D4 (Deviations from intended interventions): low - retrospective with standard care. D5 (Missing data): moderate - short median follow-up (12 months) for 2-year endpoint estimation; data on infection outcomes not reported. D7 (Selection of reported result): moderate - infection outcomes (BSI/CMV/IFI) not reported; cGVHD MVA result hidden ('data not shown') when non-significant. Overall: serious risk of bias due to confounding by indication and heterogeneous comparator.

Retrospective EBMT-LWP registry matched-pair (1:2) analysis comparing ATG vs PTCY in 9/10 MMUD RIC HCT for lymphoproliferative disease. D1 (confounding): serious - retrospective with matching on only 5 variables (age, disease status, F-to-M, source, CMV); important confounders not balanced including ATG dose/agent (not captured), backbone CNI/MMF/MTX combinations differ substantially (PTCy arm 50% CsA+MMF; ATG arm 50% CsA+MTX), and era of transplant strongly imbalanced (ATG 59% 2010-2015 vs PTCy 84% 2016-2021). D2 (selection): moderate - eligible PTCy patients (n=70) reduced to 64 after matching from a pool of 341 ATG patients; matching ratio 1:2 reasonable but introduces selection. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - definitions of PTCY and ATG groups clear, but unbalanced distribution of CNI/MMF/MTX adjuncts (per discussion). D4 (deviations): low - registry-captured exposures. D5 (missing data): moderate - several variables had missing data (HCT-CI, ABO, Rhesus 41-47% missing); follow-up much shorter in PTCy arm (1 yr vs 6 yr ATG, p<0.001) limits long-term outcome assessment. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - standardized EBMT definitions but no central adjudication of GVHD; Seattle criteria for cGVHD used (not NIH 2014). D7 (selective reporting): low - all pre-specified endpoints reported.

Large multinational EBMT registry retrospective analysis with substantial between-arm imbalance: rATG patients older (58.6 vs 53 yrs), more MAC (52% vs 62.3% PTCy — actually reversed: PTCy more MAC), more TBI in PTCy (24.7% vs 14.5%), and very different GVHD prophylaxis platforms across arms (rATG predominantly CSA+MTX 49.8%, PTCy predominantly TACRO+MMF+SIRO 44.4%). D1 confounding: serious (different conditioning regimens, GVHD platforms, era effects within 2018-2021, center effects only partially addressed by frailty model). D2 selection: serious (non-randomized allocation; PTCy uptake selectively in younger and more recent transplants). D3 classification: moderate (well-defined drug exposures but no ATG product/dose breakdown). D4 missing data: low (EBMT registry, low missingness reported). D5 measurement: moderate (registry-level outcome ascertainment with standard EBMT MED forms). D6 reporting: low. D7 deviations: moderate (no GVHD prophylaxis dose/schedule details). Overall: serious risk of bias from confounding by indication and unbalanced baseline characteristics, though multivariate adjustment performed.

EBMT registry retrospective cohort with non-randomized treatment assignment. D1 (confounding) serious: significant baseline imbalances (age, donor age, DRI, KPS, HCT-CI, TBI use, transplant year) between arms; multivariate Cox adjustment with center frailty performed but unmeasured confounders likely (e.g., physician preference, institutional practice patterns, era of letermovir, CMV monitoring). D2 (selection) moderate: eligibility well-defined but center-level selection of GVHD prophylaxis approach introduces selection bias. D3 (intervention classification) low: rATG vs PTCy classification based on registry-reported variables. D4 (deviations) low: GVHD prophylaxis given as planned per protocol. D5 (missing data) moderate: 25.4% missing rATG dosing, 13.1% missing HCT-CI, 4.5% missing KPS; cause of death unknown for 35 cases. D6 (outcome measurement) low: standardized EBMT registry definitions, MAGIC criteria aGVHD, Shulman cGVHD. D7 (selective reporting) low: protocol-defined endpoints (NRM, OS, PFS, RI, GRFS, GVHD). Overall serious due to baseline confounding inherent to registry comparison of PTCy vs rATG.

Retrospective CIBMTR registry analysis with predefined cohorts by GVHD prophylaxis category. D1 (confounding) moderate: patient/disease/donor distributions substantially differ across the 4 arms (donor type, conditioning intensity, graft source); CD4-based cutoffs are adjusted in multivariable Cox but per-arm comparison of outcomes is not the primary aim. D2 (selection) serious: cohort restricted to patients with available CD4 measurements at both D+100 and D+180 - patients who died before D+100 are excluded by design (immortal time and survivor bias for OS/NRM/PFS at later timepoints). D3 (intervention classification) moderate: GVHD prophylaxis category derived from CIBMTR registry forms; PTCy adjuncts (CNI, MMF), ATG agent/dose, conditioning regimens heterogeneous within each arm. D4 (deviations) low: registry data captures actual treatment received. D5 (missing data) moderate: substantial missing values for ALC subsets, IgG/IgA/IgM, IPSS-R, race; some clinical covariates with 3-5% missingness. D6 (outcome measurement) moderate: aGVHD/cGVHD/infections per CIBMTR forms - PCR/culture criteria not centrally adjudicated; EORTC-MSG fungal definitions not applied. D7 (selective reporting) moderate: per-arm OS/NRM/PFS/cGVHD cumulative incidences not reported separately by GVHD prophylaxis (only aGVHD II-IV and III-IV at D+100); main analyses focus on CD4 cutoff stratification, not on PTCy vs non-PTCy comparisons.

Single-arm descriptive 2-center retrospective cohort focused on peri-engraftment CARV epidemiology in Valencia (HCUV+HLF) Dec 2013-Jun 2023. D1 (confounding): moderate - heterogeneous GVHD prophylaxis (PTCy 44%, Tac+Sir 52%, CNI-based 4%), ATG use 13%, donor types and conditioning intensity not balanced; multivariable Cox regression adjusted for key covariates. D2 (NA - no intervention assignment comparison). D3 (intervention classification): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis category captured but specific PTCy regimen details not delineated. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective registry-based. D5 (missing data): moderate - 2 patients had >=2 CARV episodes; period of transplant covers significant CARV epidemiology shifts (COVID-19 pandemic). D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - LRTD ascertainment depended on radiology and BAL availability, with mixed diagnostic platforms (Luminex xTAG vs CLART vs BioFire) across centers and over time potentially introducing detection bias. D7 (reporting): low - prespecified outcomes reported. Overall judgement: moderate. Not eligible for PTCy MA comparator analysis since single descriptive arm without PTCy-vs-non-PTCy contrast.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis comparing MSD (heterogeneous GVHD prophylaxis - only 4.1% PTCy, 37.9% ATG, 7.7% alemtuzumab) vs HD (uniform PTCy). D1 (confounding): serious - donor type assignment non-random; HD recipients had higher risk disease (79% high-risk vs 70%), longer interval diagnosis-to-HCT (12 vs 8 mo), poorer KPS, more CMV seropositivity; despite multivariable adjustment, key confounders (IPSS-R cytogenetics, HCT-CI, donor specific antibodies, kinship) missing. D2 (selection): moderate - inclusion bias possible; not all eligible patients reported to registry. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - heterogeneous prophylaxis in MSD arm conflates donor effect with prophylaxis effect. D4 (deviations from intended): low - registry-captured prophylaxis used. D5 (missing data): moderate - cytogenetics IPSS-R unavailable; donor age missing for 26.1% MSD/13.7% HD; KPS missing. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standard EBMT outcome ascertainment. D7 (selective reporting): low - prespecified registry endpoints. Overall: serious risk of bias due to unmeasured confounding and prophylaxis heterogeneity in comparator.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparison of two sequential calendar eras (2009-2015 CyTBI vs 2016-2021 FluTBI-PTCy) spanning over a decade of changes in supportive care. D1 (confounding): serious - secular trends in NRM reduction independent of intervention; arms differ in age (45 vs 37, p=.01), TBI dose (8.8 Gy in 54% of PTCy arm vs 0% of CyTBI), HCT-CI/age (32% vs 14% >=3, p=.04), and CMV serostatus distribution (p=.05); no propensity score matching or multivariable adjustment for full covariate set. D2 (selection): moderate - intention-to-treat aligned with sequential protocol enrollment. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - clear protocol-defined arms but TBI dose was further age-stratified within PTCy arm. D4 (deviations): low - protocol-based. D5 (missing data): low. D6 (measurement): moderate - 1995 IBMTR aGVHD and 2005 NIH cGVHD criteria used uniformly but ascertainment by treating teams unblinded. D7 (reporting): low - outcomes appear pre-specified. Small sample (n=28 in PTCy arm) limits precision; differential follow-up (82 vs 22 mo) confounds late-event comparisons.

Single-center retrospective sequential cohort study comparing three GvHD prophylaxis regimens implemented in non-overlapping eras (Cohort-1 CNI+MTX/MMF 2012-2016, Cohort-2 TAC-SIRO 2012-2016 RIC only, Cohort-3 PTCy-TAC 2016-2022). D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - cohorts differ substantially in conditioning intensity, donor type distribution (MSD predominant in Cohort-1, MMUD overrepresented in Cohort-3 [27% vs 5-7%]), age (median 41 vs 61 vs 55), disease risk (rDRI high 31% vs 53% vs 58%), and HCT-CI; sequential era effect cannot be separated from regimen effect. D2 (selection): SERIOUS - eras are consecutive and patient allocation to regimen was based entirely on calendar period of transplant; supportive care, antimicrobial prophylaxis (e.g., letermovir post-2021), and conditioning platforms evolved over the 10-year window. D3 (intervention classification): MODERATE - prophylaxis regimens clearly defined per protocol. D4 (deviations): LOW. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - complete clinical follow-up but limited detail on infection outcomes and steroid exposure. Multivariable Cox model adjusted for HLA mismatch, donor/recipient sex, and prophylaxis was performed but did not adjust for era effects. ROBINS-I overall: SERIOUS.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis with R/R ALL inclusion. D1 (confounding): serious - haplo recipients more recently transplanted (median 2018 vs 2014), substantial era confounding; donor sex, CMV status, cell source, conditioning intensity differed significantly between arms; PS-matching addresses but does not eliminate. D2 (selection): low - consecutive registry patients meeting criteria. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - haplo/PTCy includes 7% PTCy+ATG, MUD/ATG includes mixed ATG products/doses (not specified). D4 (deviations): low - retrospective registry. D5 (missing data): moderate - KPS missing 21/249, donor/patient sex missing 13/249, ATG product/dose not specified, prior lines of therapy and TKI use for Ph+ ALL not captured. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standard EBMT outcome definitions. D7 (selection of reported result): low - prespecified primary/secondary endpoints. Overall serious due to era confounding and missing key clinical covariates.

Retrospective EBMT registry comparison. D1 (confounding): serious — heterogeneous GVHD prophylaxis within ATG arm (8 distinct regimens including basiliximab, sirolimus, MMF, MTX combinations) and within PTCy arm (3 regimens); differing graft source distribution (PTCy 60% BM vs ATG 46% BM); ATG type/dose heterogeneous (75% Fresenius Grafalon median 20 mg/kg; 25% thymoglobulin median 10 mg/kg); residual confounding in MV likely. D2 (selection): moderate — concurrent registry-reported patients, but periodicity/center variation. D3 (interventions classification): serious — broad grouping of heterogeneous ATG-containing regimens. D4 (deviations): moderate. D5 (missing data): moderate — 41% NA/failed cytogenetics; disease risk features incomplete. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — standardized EBMT registry definitions but no central adjudication. D7 (selection of reported result): low. Overall serious risk of bias.

EBMT registry retrospective comparison of dUCBT (n=165) vs Haplo-PTCY PBSC (n=544) in AML CR1/CR2 patients. D1 confounding: moderate — donor source selection non-random (center-driven); haplo arm transplanted in more recent calendar years (median 2017 vs 2014), more often MAC (60% vs 23%), more often CMV-positive recipients (77% vs 65%); MVA adjusts for age, CR status, cytogenetics, KPS, conditioning, with center random effect, but residual confounding likely (era, evolving supportive care, no infection prophylaxis data). D2 selection: moderate — ATG/Campath/ex vivo TCD excluded which is appropriate, but center heterogeneity and missing chimerism/MRD data. D3 classification: low — registry-collected protocolized variables. D4 deviations: low — observational. D5 missing data: moderate — variable missingness for KPS, cytogenetics, CMV serology, donor age. D6 outcome measurement: low — EBMT-standardized outcomes; aGVHD per standard criteria. D7 reporting: low — pre-specified MVA. Overall moderate.

Retrospective EBMT PDWP registry study comparing pediatric AML patients receiving MUD+ATG vs Haplo+PTCy, 2011-2021. D1 (confounding): moderate - matched-pair design with multiple exact and nearest-match variables addressed major prognostic factors but residual unmeasured confounding likely (eligibility for haplo vs MUD may relate to unmeasured urgency, social factors). D2 (selection): moderate - 1 haplo patient could not be matched and was excluded; matched analysis on subset (95/96 haplo, 253/420 MUD). D3 (intervention classification): low - donor type and GVHD prophylaxis well-defined registry variables. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective per-protocol use of registry-defined interventions. D5 (missing data): low - registry data, key variables reported; some missing on cytogenetics (~10% missing, similar in both groups). D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - aGVHD/cGVHD ascertainment depends on individual center reporting in registry, possible misclassification but groups assessed identically. D7 (reporting): low - prespecified primary (LFS) and secondary outcomes all reported. Overall moderate. Short follow-up censored at 2 yrs.

Single-center retrospective cohort with consecutive enrollment minimizes selection bias. D1 (confounding): moderate — Fine-Gray multivariable model adjusts for MAC, Cy, UCB, CMV serostatus, Karnofsky scale, but residual confounding likely (donor-type/HLA mismatch not in final model; BKPyV monitoring not standardized). D2 (selection of participants): low — all consecutive allo-HCT 2016-2019.
