D3 (classification of interventions): moderate — PTCy use clearly recorded; GvHD prophylaxis well documented; but PTCy vs non-PTCy not the design contrast (PTCy is one of many covariates). D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): moderate — BKPyV viremia performed in only 27/41 BKHC cases and 83 non-BKHC; CMV donor serostatus and other covariates well captured. D6 (measurement of outcome): low — BKHC defined per ECIL criteria, prospective clinical surveillance with daily urinary stick. D7 (selection of reported result): low — pre-specified primary/secondary objectives, Fine-Gray with planned forcing of MAC/Cy/UCB. Overall: moderate.

Retrospective single-center cohort spanning 2001-2021 (20 years) with substantial era effects (pre-PET vs PET vs LET). Confounding (D1): moderate — PT-Cy use was non-randomized and concentrated in later years (>=2008), so PTCy patients differ systematically from CNI-only patients in transplant era, conditioning, donor type, and CMV monitoring practice; multivariable Cox models adjust for major confounders but residual confounding by indication likely. Selection (D2): moderate — only day 100 survivors included; pre-day-100 deaths excluded which may differentially affect PTCy arm (haplo-heavy). Classification of intervention (D3): low — GVHD prophylaxis regimen documented per medical record. Deviations from intended intervention (D4): low — observational design with standardized FHCC protocols. Missing data (D5): moderate — only patients with late CMV disease had detailed PCR surveillance adherence data; ~80% followed outside FHCC after day 100, leading to potential underestimation of late CMV disease. Outcome measurement (D6): low — CMV disease defined per standard Ljungman international criteria; biopsy-proven. Selection of reported result (D7): low — pre-specified multivariable analyses and sensitivity analyses reported. Overall moderate due to confounding by era and missing surveillance data for ~80% of cohort.

Retrospective registry analysis combining EBMT/CIBMTR cohorts (heterogeneous data sources, definitions, conditioning, GVHD prophylaxis). D1 (confounding): serious - non-randomized comparison of PT-Cy vs non-PT-Cy with substantial baseline imbalance (n=73 vs 17); univariate analysis only with no multivariable adjustment for stem cell source (BM vs PB) which was also significantly associated with outcomes. D2 (selection): moderate - registry-based selection, only patients reported to EBMT/CIBMTR included. D3 (classification): moderate - PT-Cy use clearly classified but conditioning intensity and ATG use have substantial missing data. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - 16/96 missing ISS, 33/96 missing donor relationship, 30/96 missing CMV status, 61/96 missing pre-transplant therapy details. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - heterogeneous ascertainment across registries; no specified GVHD grading system. D7 (selective reporting): moderate.

ROBINS-I assessment: D1 (confounding) moderate — era comparison (Period 1 vs Period 2) with simultaneous changes in conditioning intensity (MAC use increased from 0.9% to 38.1%), ATG dose (4.5 to 2 mg/kg), CsA target, supportive care, and multiple other co-interventions; confounding by changing case mix (high/very high DRI 27.0% vs 14.7%) and improvements in care over time hard to fully adjust for. D2 (selection of participants) serious — non-randomized retrospective era comparison; selection into period is fully time-dependent; competing interventions vary between periods. D3 (classification of interventions) low — periods clearly defined by calendar date. D4 (deviations from intended interventions) low — observational. D5 (missing data) moderate — some missing baseline KPS/HCT-CI/DRI values (1-7% per variable); no clarity on whether outcome assessment was complete. D6 (measurement of outcomes) moderate — clinical/standardized outcomes; CMV/EBV monitored weekly; graft failure definition unclear. D7 (selective reporting) low — pre-specified outcomes reported. Overall serious risk of bias due to bundled simultaneous interventions and confounding by indication/era.

Single-center retrospective cohort with progressive institutional adoption of PTCY-TK over the enrollment window (2014-2021), confounded by era (median 18.8 mo follow-up PTCY-TK vs 37.1 mo Other; 63.6% PTCY-TK transplants performed in 2018-2021 vs 24.7% in Other). Donor distribution markedly imbalanced (PTCY-TK 93.4% UD with 46.5% MMUD vs Other 56.0% MSD, only 4.0% MMUD). Multivariate Cox regression adjusts for time period, age, HCT-CI, KPS, DRI, and donor; partially mitigates confounding for GVHD/GRFS endpoints, but residual confounding is plausible (D2). Outcome measurement standardized per institutional protocols (D4-D5). Reporting appears complete with figures, tables, and primary outcomes pre-specified. Selection bias risk moderate-serious because of historical comparator. Overall: serious.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis of 404 MDS pts (PTCy n=66 vs heterogeneous 'other' n=338 including 162 ATG-containing). D1 confounding: Moderate - MVA adjusted for age, IPSS-R, TP53, year, conditioning intensity, HCT-CI, KPS, disease status. PTCy group had higher MAC use (52.3% vs 38.2%, p=0.047) and were more recently transplanted (65.2% in 2018-2020 vs 36.1%); residual era confounding likely. Letermovir use not captured. D2 selection: Moderate - inclusion required completed MED-C follow-up forms returned 2023; only 52/many EBMT centers participated; potential selection bias toward better-quality centers. D3 classification of intervention: Moderate - PTCy/other prophylaxis well-defined by registry but adjunct IS heterogeneous (PTCy+1 vs +2 IS agents, varying CNI/MMF); 'Other' arm collapsed across CNI-MTX/MMF (52%) and ATG-containing (48%). D4 deviations: Low. D5 missing data: Moderate - TP53 missing in 281/404 (use of missing indicator); molecular markers missing in 79; cGVHD denominator 65/66 and 336/338; bacterial infection and detailed CMV/EBV timepoint data not captured; ATG dosing/schedule heterogeneity not detailed. D6 outcome measurement: Low - standardized EBMT registry definitions, Glucksberg/MAGIC for aGVHD, Seattle for cGVHD. D7 selective reporting: Low - prespecified outcomes reported with CIs; multivariable Cox models for OS, PFS, NRM, CIR shown in Tables 3-4. Overall moderate.

Retrospective single-center sequential-era cohort (ATG-based 2011-2015; ATG4.5/PTCy Oct 2015-May 2018; ATG2/PTCy May 2018-2021). D1 (confounding): moderate-to-serious — supportive care evolved over decade (no letermovir initially; antifungal practice may have shifted; CMV preemptive practice). MVA controlled for age, DRI, conditioning intensity, HCT-CI, KPS but did not adjust for era-specific supportive care. D2 (selection): serious — different time periods select different patients; baseline characteristics differed (older age and lower HCT-CI in ATG2/PTCy era). D3 (intervention classification): low — GVHD prophylaxis is well-defined. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low — small numbers missing in DRI, KPS, HCT-CI. D6 (measurement of outcomes): low — standardized criteria (Keystone for aGVHD, NIH for cGVHD). D7 (reporting): low. Overall: serious due to era effect confounding and selection.

Retrospective single-center cohort comparing consecutive PTCy/Tac patients (2016-2021 era) with historical controls receiving conventional non-PTCy CNI/MTX or CNI/MMF prophylaxis (2011-2016 era). D1 (confounding): moderate - era effect strongly confounds prophylaxis comparison (supportive care, infection management, donor sourcing all changed between eras); statistical adjustment included time period and known confounders (age, sex, HCT-CI, KPS, DRI, donor type, conditioning intensity). D2 (selection): serious - non-randomized allocation determined solely by transplant date relative to 2016 (MUD) and 2019 (MSD) practice changes; no concurrent controls. D3 (exposure classification): low - prophylaxis regimens unambiguously documented. D4 (deviations): low - protocolized post-transplant management with homogeneous GVHD treatment per institutional pathway. D5 (missing data): low - follow-up censored uniformly at 2 years, near-complete data for primary outcomes. D6 (measurement): moderate - GVHD ascertained by treating physicians (MAGIC and 2014 NIH) without blinded adjudication; CMV PCR threshold-based; BSI documented by blood cultures. D7 (selection of reported result): low - main outcomes prespecified in methods. Overall judgement: serious risk of bias driven primarily by era-based allocation (D2) and residual unmeasured confounding (D1).

Retrospective CIBMTR registry analysis 2013-2017. D1 Confounding: serious — Haplo/PTCy vs MUD/conventional confounded by donor type (impossible to separate PTCy effect from haplo donor effect); paper acknowledges this is fundamental limitation. Significant baseline differences (age, DRI, graft source, AML predominance). D2 Selection: serious — primary analytic cohorts conditioned on developing grade 2-4 aGVHD or cGVHD (collider stratification creates selection bias for downstream outcomes); parent-population CIs OK. D3 Classification of intervention: moderate — GVHD prophylaxis well-defined but ATG dose/agent not detailed. D4 Deviations: low — registry, standard care. D5 Missing data: moderate — small amounts missing for HCT-CI/sex/DRI; cGVHD severity grading not standardized (predates NIH 2014). D6 Outcome measurement: moderate — GVHD assessed clinically; consensus criteria but no central adjudication. D7 Selection of reported result: low — pre-specified hypotheses on GVHD organ patterns/NRM/OS.

D1 (confounding) serious: RIC choice non-randomized, varied by era and physician preference, with documented time bias (Flu-Mel uptake increased after 2018 due to busulfan shortage). Donor type also differs significantly across RIC arms (haplo predominant in TBI and Mel but more balanced in Bu, p=0.001), confounding intensity effect with donor effect. D2 (selection) serious: post-hoc subset selection of 52/450 RIC AML/MDS patients with no documented sampling frame. D7 (reporting) serious: incomplete outcome reporting (no D+100 GVHD, no NRM, no infections, no engraftment data; only crude proportions for adverse events, KM for OS/PFS only). Mixed within-arm PTCy use makes the comparison ambiguous for our PTCy analytic framework. Small sample (especially Bu arm n=7) limits inference.

EBMT ALWP retrospective registry analysis of 208 adults with ALL undergoing haplo-SCT 2007-2014. D1 (confounding): moderate - retrospective registry; choice of GVHD prophylaxis non-randomized; MV Cox adjusted for major confounders but no PSM. D2 (selection): moderate - centers chose PTCy vs ATG by policy, possible center-level confounding (frailty term tested NS p=0.30). D3 (intervention classification): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis assignment well-defined though ATG type/dose varied (Thymo vs Fresenius). D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - cytogenetics 142/208; MRD 91/149; ATG type only 66/90; key prognostic data missing. D6 (measurement of outcome): low - standard EBMT-defined outcomes with audited data. D7 (reporting): low - all pre-specified outcomes reported. Overall moderate.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective analysis comparing Haplo (n=250) vs MUD 10/10 (n=2589) in older AML. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS — significant baseline differences in disease status (CR1 38% vs 53%), KPS, time to Tx, donor sex mismatch; propensity score with caliper 0.2 used to mitigate, but residual confounding by indication likely (Haplo arm more recent and used preferentially for active disease). D2 (selection): MODERATE — registry inclusion criteria broad but center-level reporting heterogeneity possible. D3 (intervention classification): MODERATE — Haplo arm itself heterogeneous (65% PT-Cy, 26% ATG); MUD arm 75% ATG. D4 (deviations): LOW — observational, no protocol deviations applicable. D5 (missing data): MODERATE — cytogenetics missing in 33% Haplo and 46% MUD; secondary AML status missing extensively. D6 (outcome measurement): LOW — central reporting with EBMT audits, standard GVHD criteria. D7 (selection of reported result): LOW — outcomes pre-specified. Overall: SERIOUS.

EBMT ALWP registry retrospective comparison of MAC vs RIC haplo-SCT for AML >=45y. D1 (confounding): moderate - propensity score weighting and Cox multivariate adjustment used, but key confounders (Karnofsky, age, disease status, secondary AML) differed at baseline; Sorror HCT-CI not available in registry; molecular markers missing. D2 (selection): serious - RIC patients were older (61.3 vs 55.2y) and had different graft sources (60% PBSC RIC vs 47% MAC); strong indication bias for conditioning intensity choice. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - MAC/RIC defined by EBMT Bacigalupo 2009 criteria but center variability in regimen composition (TBF, BF, TBI-based) and PTCy vs ATG vs combination prophylaxis introduces classification heterogeneity. D4 (deviations): low - registry-based outcome ascertainment. D5 (missing data): moderate - molecular markers missing, Sorror HCT-CI absent. Note: this paper's primary comparison is MAC vs RIC; PTCy is a subgroup/covariate. Outcomes for PTCy-only patients within each conditioning arm are NOT separately reported. Strong center effect acknowledged by authors.

Single-center retrospective cohort, 960 consecutive patients. D1 (confounding): moderate - era effects (2015-2021 spans introduction of PTCy-ATG-CsA Oct 2015 and ATG dose reduction May 2018); composite 4-group analysis with multivariate adjustment for donor and ABO, but residual confounding by indication (HD Bu used preferentially for younger/fitter patients with adverse-risk disease) likely. D2 (selection): low - consecutive enrollment. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - PTCy use confounded with ATG, CsA, calendar era, and conditioning intensity (PTCY-ATG-CsA cohort overlaps strongly with HD Bu MAC group). D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low - 98.6% urine BK PCR coverage in HC patients, but 40.4% BK-NEG cases lacked adenovirus/CMV viral testing. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standardized Bedi grading; charts reviewed. D7 (selection of reported result): low. Paper appropriately acknowledges that only 60 patients received PTCy without ATG, limiting isolation of PTCy effect from ATG. Overall moderate ROB due to inability to disentangle PTCy from concurrent HD Bu use and from ATG/CsA in this institutional cohort.

ROBINS-I retrospective non-randomized: D1 Confounding SERIOUS - PTCy arm is 9/10 MMUD whereas control is matched related donor; HLA mismatch and donor relation are major effect modifiers for infection/GVHD outcomes, making the PTCy vs no-PTCy contrast deeply confounded with donor type; no adjustment beyond descriptive comparison. D2 Selection MODERATE - all consecutive eligible patients per registry but allocation determined by donor availability/era. D3 Classification of intervention MODERATE - prophylaxis regimens well-described. D4 Deviations LOW - intervention adherence not a concern in retrospective infection ascertainment. D5 Missing data MODERATE - small n (45+45), no patient flow diagram; Table 1 contains a denominator inconsistency (gender row sums to 79 not 90). D6 Outcome measurement LOW - standardized definitions (EORTC/MSG, ECIL, NIH) and twice-weekly CMV PCR / galactomannan monitoring; outcome ascertainment same in both arms. D7 Selection of reported result MODERATE - chi-square p-values reported only; no multivariable adjustment; competing risks not handled. Overall SERIOUS due to baseline confounding between donor type and intervention.

Retrospective registry analysis of three non-randomized donor strata (MSD, Haplo+PTCy, MUD+ATG) with substantial baseline imbalance: median age 12-37 yrs across donor/CR strata, marked imbalance in conditioning intensity (Haplo CR1 only 53.3% MAC vs MSD CR1 85.4%), in pediatric proportion (Haplo CR2+ 66% children, MSD CR2+ 40%), in sex-match distribution, and in CMV serostatus distribution. ATG/PTCy exposure perfectly confounded with donor type and explicitly excluded from multivariable modeling. Authors acknowledge survival bias in CR2+ MUD comparisons due to longer time-to-transplant. Acute GVHD data unavailable (selection/data missingness concern for d4). Multivariable adjustment for age, sex match, HCT-CI, KPS, diagnosis, disease status, donor type, graft source, conditioning is reasonable but limited by missing variables: MRD pre-HCT, time-from-diagnosis-to-HCT, DSA, prophylactic DLI. Outcome ascertainment is registry-based (standard for CIBMTR/Brazilian Registry; reasonable but cGVHD criteria stated only as 'standard criteria' without grading specification). No deviation-from-intended-intervention data. Reporting bias unlikely given comprehensive Table 2 and 3 presentation.

Retrospective real-life observational study with small N (40), substantial baseline imbalance between arms (donor type significantly differed p=0.001, conditioning regimen p=0.001, stem cell source p=0.05), heterogeneous era spanning 2009-2021 (era confounding likely between PTCy and ATG arms); no propensity score matching or multivariable adjustment for arm assignment beyond univariate/multivariate regression on relapse and GvHD; outcomes reported as crude proportions without competing-risk handling; no formal HR for OS by arm; high missingness on infection outcomes (no CMV/BSI/IFI specifically reported); no information on letermovir era or antifungal regimen. D1 confounding serious due to differential donor/conditioning between arms and era effect; D2 selection moderate (consecutive enrollment but selection by physician choice of prophylaxis); D5 missing data moderate (substantial outcome categories not reported); overall serious.

Non-randomized observational cohort study with PT-CY/CSA arm enrolled prospectively from Sept 2017 and MTX/CSA arm largely retrospective from 2015-2017. D1 confounding: moderate, multiple baseline imbalances (age PT-CY older 34 vs 29 yr p<0.001; conditioning regimens differ dramatically with PT-CY arm 100% Flu/Bu vs MTX arm 81% Bu/Cy; CMV donor IgG status differs 75.3% vs 91.1%) partially addressed via multivariate Cox. D2 selection: moderate, sequential calendar-era based assignment creates risk. D3 intervention classification: low, regimens well-defined. D4 deviations: low, single-center protocol-driven care. D5 missing data: moderate, no statement of loss to follow-up or completeness. D6 measurement: low, standard Glucksberg + NIH 2014 criteria. D7 selective reporting: low, all pre-specified outcomes appear reported.

Comparative analysis of two independently-conducted prospective phase II single-arm studies (JSCT-ATG15 enrolled 2016-2018; JSCT-PTCY19 enrolled 2020-2021) with non-overlapping enrollment windows and structurally different eligibility (JSCT-ATG15 restricted to MAC + HLA-matched only; JSCT-PTCY19 allowed MAC or RIC and HLA-matched or 1-2 allele mismatched). Confounding by indication / era / protocol design is severe (D1). Outcome ascertainment and statistical methods comparable across protocols (D3 moderate). Despite prospective phase II origin of each component, the head-to-head comparison is essentially a retrospective non-randomized cross-protocol analysis; small sample size limits adjusted analyses.

Non-randomized prospective vs historical-control retrospective comparison with substantial confounding by era (PTCy 2017-2019 vs MTX 2015-2019 with overlap), age (median 34 vs 28 yrs, P=.017), conditioning (uniform Flu/Bu in PTCy arm vs heterogeneous BuCy/BuFlu/TBI-Cy in MTX arm), and disease distribution (more AML in PTCy 70.7% vs MTX 57.3%, more ALL in MTX 13.4% vs PTCy 1.3%). D1 (confounding) and D2 (selection - historical control with retrospective ascertainment) are serious. Small single-country two-center sample. No CMV/letermovir era information. Short median follow-up (12.5 mo PTCy). Outcome ascertainment by clinical criteria appears consistent. Missing creatinine clearance data in 33/75 MTX patients. No documentation of competing risk methodology though CIs reported for aGVHD and cGVHD suggesting CIF used.

CIBMTR registry retrospective design; D1: confounding present (donor selection, era, center practice) but multivariable Cox adjusted for center effects via score test; D2: selection of participants reasonable, exclusions explicit (UCB, single-mismatch, CD34-selected, ATG/alemtuzumab); D3: intervention classification based on registry GVHD prophylaxis categories — reliable; D4: deviations minimal in observational registry; D5: missing data limited (5% ALC at D+100, 20% at D+180); D6: outcome measurement — infection ascertainment passive (clinical only), institutional viral monitoring NOT collected — risk of differential ascertainment between HaploCy (more aggressive screening expected) vs SibCNI, acknowledged by authors; D7: selection of reported result — pre-specified analysis, low concern. Overall moderate due to ascertainment bias and unmeasured confounders (immunosuppression burden, antiviral prophylaxis).

Single-center retrospective non-randomized cohort. D1 (confounding): serious - PTCy and ATG cohorts treated in different eras (2016-2018 vs 2010-2017), age and conditioning intensity differ significantly; only partial multivariable adjustment. D2 (selection): serious - eras differ; era effects and improvements in supportive care over time could bias PTCy cohort favorably. D3 (classification): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis protocols clearly defined. D4 (deviations): low - retrospective routine care. D5 (missing data): moderate - some chimerism data missing. D6 (measurement): moderate - clinical diagnosis with biopsy confirmation, but ascertainment for infections not blinded. D7 (selective reporting): low - all pre-specified outcomes reported. Limited PTCy sample (n=22) reduces precision.

Multicenter retrospective single-arm observational study of 109 ALL pts receiving haplo PTCy across 5 centers (2005-2015). D1 (confounding): moderate - no comparator arm; heterogeneous disease status (CR1/CR2/beyond CR2/PIF) and conditioning (MAC/NMA); univariate/multivariate Cox done but only conditioning intensity significant. D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive pts (good) but 5 centers with potential variation in practice; pediatric and 2nd HSCT pts excluded but 2nd HSCT analyzed separately within paper. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - PTCy uniform but CNI varied (tacrolimus 79% vs cyclosporine 21%); no detailed infection prophylaxis reporting. D4 (deviations from protocol): low - retrospective so no protocol deviations per se. D5 (missing data): moderate - acknowledged missing data for some covariates (denominators don't add to 109 for several variables); GVHD severity not assessed accurately for all per authors' own limitations statement. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate - GVHD ascertainment retrospective and authors acknowledge could not accurately assess GVHD severity for all; infection ascertainment unclear. D7 (selection of reported result): low - DFS prespecified primary endpoint; multiple secondary endpoints reported transparently with HRs. Overall: moderate.

Retrospective single-center analysis spanning 1993-2023 with strong confounding by era: ATLG group transplanted predominantly pre-2014 (median 2003), PTCy group post-2014 (median 2020). Substantial differences in age (29 vs 42), donor type distribution, graft source (38% BM ATLG vs 11% PTCy), and conditioning regimen (TBI+Cy/Vp16 vs TBI/Flu). Authors performed PSM (only 31 matched pairs) and multivariate analysis to address confounding. Multicollinearity acknowledged among ATLG-vs-PTCy, conditioning, and year of transplant variables. Outcome definitions standard (NIH cGvHD, Glucksberg-IBMTR aGvHD). Missing data on MRD status and inconsistent MRD assessment over time noted by authors.

Retrospective matched-pair analysis of JSHCT/JDCHCT TRUMP registry with 1:3 optimal matching on year of transplant, age, sex, refined DRI, HCT-CI, and conditioning intensity. D1 (confounding): moderate - matched on key variables but unmeasured confounders remain (e.g., MTX dose, center-level practice differences as PTCy was done at 31 trial centers vs 127 UCBT centers - 'trial effect' acknowledged). D2 (selection): moderate - PTCy-haplo group was assembled via separate AMED survey, then matched to TRUMP controls; potential selection bias for fitter/larger male recipients in PTCy. D3 (classification): low - intervention defined by donor type. D4 (deviations): low - registry data. D5 (missing): moderate - infections (BSI/CMV/IFI) not reported; only HLA antibody testing in 94-98%. D6/D7 (measurement, reporting): low - standard outcome definitions, comprehensive reporting of OS/RFS/relapse/NRM/GVHD/engraftment.

Retrospective multicenter Chinese CBMTRG registry study comparing G-CSF/ATG (n=176) vs PTCy (n=44) with nested case-pair 1:4 matching on diagnosis, refined DRI, age (+/-5yr), year of HSCT (+/-2yr). D1 (confounding): serious - unbalanced conditioning regimens (BU/Cy vs BU/FLU/Cy variants), graft source (BM+PB vs PB-only), and GVHD prophylaxis backbones differ systematically by arm; residual confounding from era, CMV/EBV monitoring, antifungal/antibacterial prophylaxis not reported. D2 (selection): moderate - case-pair matching addresses some selection bias but PTCy arm is small (n=44) and selected from registry. D3 (classification): moderate - retrospective registry coding. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing): low - complete outcomes for engraftment, GVHD, NRM, OS, relapse. D6 (measurement): moderate - GVHD criteria modified Keystone/NIH; no central review. D7 (reporting): low. Authors acknowledge limitations including retrospective nature, small PTCy n, heterogeneous conditioning and GVHD prophylaxis, and lack of CMV/EBV/immune reconstitution data.

Retrospective multicenter cohort 2000-2020 covering 20-yr era spanning major changes in donor selection, conditioning, GVHD prophylaxis, supportive care, and lymphoma therapeutics. D1 confounding (moderate): multivariable Cox adjusts for histology, status at allo-HSCT, but era, donor type, HCT-CI not retained; PTCy use confounded with later era and haploidentical donor (haplo received PTCy preferentially). D2 selection (serious): PTCy use almost entirely in haploidentical donor subset; very high baseline imbalance not adjusted for in PTCy vs non-PTCy comparison. D3 classification (moderate): standard GVHD/disease definitions, but composite endpoints (early vs late NRM) defined post-hoc. D4 deviations (low): retrospective registry-style data; no protocol deviations to manage. D5 missing data (low): complete follow-up for survival outcomes, modest missingness on KPS/HCT-CI. D6 measurement (low): standard outcome ascertainment. D7 selective reporting (moderate): no protocol/registration cited; PFS pre-specified primary endpoint per Methods. Overall: serious risk of bias for PTCy vs non-PTCy comparison primarily driven by D2 confounded indication.

Retrospective single-center comparison of two non-contemporaneous transplant cohorts (cTCR/TCD 2006-2007 vs TCR/PTCY 2009-2011). Major confounding by era and patient selection: TCR/PTCY group had higher proportion of second transplants (44% vs 0%) and older age, suggesting differential indication. No statistical adjustment in primary OS/NRM comparisons (univariate only). Outcome ascertainment standardized via institutional protocol with routine PCR-based viral monitoring, reducing detection bias. Small sample size (n=55) limits statistical power. Authors acknowledge low patient numbers and different observational periods as study limitations.

Retrospective single-center cohort 2007-2018; confounding by indication for GVHD prophylaxis choice (PTCy used more often for unrelated donors, MMF used preferentially with NMA conditioning, MTX with MAC). Multivariate adjustment performed for key covariates (donor age, conditioning, donor relationship, CMV serostatus). Uniform CMV monitoring per institutional protocol; outcome ascertainment robust. PTCy arm small (n=44) limiting precision. No missing data described.

Phase II open-label RCT (NCT03246906). D1: low - randomization 1:1 stratified by HLA-match. D2: some concerns - open-label design (patients and physicians not blinded). D3: low - 5/150 (3%) randomized but not treated; primary analysis on 145 protocol-adherent patients. D4: low - blinded adjudication by Fred Hutch Long-Term Follow-Up service verified by PI. D5: low - prespecified primary endpoint (CRFS) and secondary endpoints in protocol; trial closed early at 145 of target 160 per DSMB due to declining accrual. Overall: some concerns due to open-label design.

Large CIBMTR registry (n=2765, 102 centers, 2012-2017). Strengths: uniform CIBMTR data forms, central auditing, broad geographic representation, comparator group available (SibCNI), <5% missing data on pertinent variables. Weaknesses (D1 confounding): retrospective registry; reason for choosing PTCy in MRD vs CNI not captured, with potential indication bias (e.g. center preference, donor preference). D2 (selection): centers without patients in both SibCNI and HaploCy excluded to reduce ascertainment bias; reasonable. D5 (missing data): infection prophylaxis info limited prior to 2017 - cannot adjust for antimicrobial prophylaxis era differences; no MDR data captured. Cox MVA adjusted for multiple confounders incl age, disease risk, neutrophil engraftment, aGVHD as time-dep variable.

Retrospective EBMT registry study of adverse-risk AML in CR1, 2017-2022. D1 (confounding): moderate - multivariable Cox with random center effect adjusts for key confounders (age, donor age, conditioning, CMV, gender mismatch) but pre-HCT MRD was missing in 59% and not in model. D2 (selection): low - consecutive registry reporting. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - donor type and GVHD prophylaxis (ATG/PTCy/other) recorded per protocol but PTCy regimen details (dose, schedule, companion IS) not standardized. D4 (deviations): low - registry observational. D5 (missing data): moderate - MRD missing in 1779/3006 (59%), CMV in 55, donor age in 34. D6 (measurement): low - GVHD/relapse standardly captured. D7 (selection of reported result): low - pre-specified endpoints. Overall moderate.

EBMT registry-based retrospective matched-pair analysis with propensity score matching on key covariates (age, year of HCT, donor type, Karnofsky, TCI, FtoM, AML cytogenetics). D1 (confounding): moderate - propensity matching addresses measured covariates but residual confounding likely (no data on early cardiac events, lipids, smoking, hypertension, exact ptCy dosing/timing, antifungal prophylaxis, letermovir use, CMV serostatus). D2 (selection): low - all consecutive ptCy retained; ATG matched 3:1. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - exact ATG agent/dose and ptCy schedule not captured. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low - small missing in HCT-CI and cytogenetics. D6/D7 (outcome measurement & reporting): low - standardized EBMT endpoints. Overall moderate.

Single-center retrospective case series of only 5 patients with no comparator group. D1 (confounding): serious - heterogeneous donor types, conditioning regimens, and GVHD prophylaxis across only 5 patients with no adjustment possible. D2 (selection): serious - retrospective convenience sample at one tertiary center in India, eligibility based on physician judgement. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - regimens clearly described. D4 (deviations): moderate - case-by-case management. D5 (missing data): moderate - small N with complete data per Table 1. D6 (measurement of outcome): serious - outcomes clinically ascertained without blinding, no standardized infection surveillance protocol described, GVHD per NIH criteria. D7 (reporting): moderate - all 5 cases tabulated. Overall serious risk of bias; underpowered for any inference about PTCy effect.

Single-center retrospective cohort comparing two conditioning regimens. D1 (confounding) serious: regimens chosen non-randomly across 2014-2020 enrollment period, with PTCy arm enrolled later (median follow-up 284d vs 729d), introducing era effect/secular trend confounding; no adjustment for confounders. D2 (selection): patients selected based on regimen received with some imbalances (CR/CR2 distribution, age 46 vs 34 yr median, donor type p=0.023). D3 (classification): regimens clearly defined. D4 (deviations): per-protocol approach. D5 (missing data): low missingness for primary outcomes. D6 (outcome measurement): GVHD assessment unclear if blinded; investigators uniform. D7 (reporting): no protocol referenced. NRM values (75-77% at 1yr) appear inconsistent with OS (62-65%) figures suggesting potential reporting/figure-labeling concerns.

Prospective non-randomized comparison with contemporaneous external (across-institution) control. Authors acknowledge limitations: non-randomized design, comparison across three institutions (though all use identical Beijing protocol), residual differences in donor age, HLA matching, ABO matching, and cell doses despite matched-pair sensitivity. Outcomes systematically captured with blinded expert panel for GVHD adjudication (low for measurement). Disease type / DRI distribution comparable. No selective reporting suspected. Confounding by indication is the primary risk (D2-D3).

Large CIBMTR registry retrospective comparison with multivariable adjustment for major prognostic factors (age, remission status, MRD, cytogenetics, conditioning, donor/recipient sex/CMV match). D1 (confounding): moderate - multiple adjusted covariates and stepwise selection but residual confounding from non-random donor selection (e.g., center preference, donor availability, ethnicity-driven donor mix). D3 (intervention classification): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis modality heterogeneous within non-haplo arms, ATG use differs substantially (1% haplo vs 5-50% comparators). D5 (missing data): moderate - MRD missing in ~4-9% per arm, race partly unreported. Infection-specific outcomes not captured by registry (only cause-of-death categories), limiting infection inference. Outcome ascertainment via CIBMTR follow-up forms is standardized.

Comparative study pooling prospective mPTCy arm (registered ChiCTR2000038297) with retrospective historical G-CSF/ATG controls from a different era (2012-2021 vs 2019-2023). D1 (confounding): moderate - multivariable adjustment performed but era differences (PBSC graft, supportive care, letermovir availability) only partially controlled. D2 (selection of participants): serious - non-concurrent comparison with potential selection bias from differing eligibility/treatment-era criteria. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - protocols well-defined but era-bound. D4-D7: low - outcomes ascertained uniformly, single-center follow-up, complete data except 4 missing CD34. Follow-up imbalance (866 vs 2511 days) limits long-term outcome (cGVHD/GRFS) interpretation in mPTCy arm.

Retrospective multicenter registry analysis with propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics. D1 (confounding) moderate: PSM used for 4 of 13 measurable covariates but HLA mismatch, MNC, CD34+ cells, and graft resource remained imbalanced after PSM; residual confounding by center, conditioning regimen heterogeneity, and unmeasured variables. D2 (selection): moderate; non-random assignment to treatment groups based on physician/center preference. D3 (classification): low; protocol assignments were prospective. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): low (only patients with complete records included). D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate; some outcomes ascertained heterogeneously across centers; no central adjudication described. D7 (selection of reported result): low. Overall: moderate ROB.

D1 (randomization): low — central interactive response technology system used; 2:1 allocation specified; baseline characteristics balanced. D2 (deviations from intended interventions): some_concerns — open-label design without blinding of participants/providers; aGVHD/cGVHD assessment by treating clinicians not blinded (MAGIC/NIH 2014 criteria are clinical). D3 (missing outcome data): low — all 66 randomized patients analyzed; median follow-up 264/257 days, no LTFU reported. D4 (measurement of outcome): some_concerns — GVHD outcomes are subjective clinical assessments; open-label design with unblinded clinicians grading aGVHD/cGVHD. D5 (selection of reported result): some_concerns — trial stopped early at first interim analysis for futility (after 66/196 planned, conditional power 0.025); pre-specified protocol via NCT06108739 but interim stopping affects interpretation. Overall: some_concerns due to open-label design, subjective GVHD endpoints, and early stopping.

Registry-based retrospective cohort (TRUMP/JDCHCT). D1 (confounding): moderate - multivariate Cox/Fine-Gray adjusted for age, sex, PS, HCT-CI, cytogenetic risk, conditioning, year, but MRD status and molecular profiles not captured. D2 (selection): low - consecutive registry enrollment with prospective registration covering >99% of Japanese centers. D3 (intervention classification): low - donor source clearly defined. D4 (deviations from intended): low - standard clinical practice; ATG/TCD excluded. D5 (missing data): moderate - cytogenetic risk had 3-5% unevaluable; MRD/molecular profiles missing. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - GVHD and engraftment subject to ascertainment; standard criteria used; centers report at D+100 and annual follow-up. D7 (selection of reported result): low - pre-specified primary outcome (OS) and secondary outcomes.
Single-arm descriptive paper protocol-excluded; no PTCy vs comparator contrast for RoB assessment. Tracked for PRISMA only.

Retrospective nationwide JSTCT TRUMP registry analysis. D1 confounding: moderate — significant baseline imbalance across arms (age, conditioning intensity, donor-recipient sex, donor HTLV-1 status); authors adjusted for major prognostic factors in multivariable Cox/Fine-Gray models and conducted propensity-score-matched PTCY vs CBT comparison. D2 selection: moderate — limited reporting of donor selection rationale within institutions; PTCY vs MRD/MUD/CBT choice driven by donor availability/protocol selection. D3 classification: low — outcomes defined by standard criteria. D4 deviation: low — observational, no protocol deviations. D5 missing data: low — registry capture, complete follow-up. D6 measurement: low — outcomes standardized via TRUMP. D7 reporting: low — comprehensive outcome reporting per JSTCT working group. Overall moderate.

Retrospective multicenter (3 Ankara centers) registry-based comparison of 9/10 MMUD PTCy vs 10/10 MRD MTX/CsA. D1 (confounding): serious — fundamental differences between arms (donor type, prophylaxis, conditioning regimens differ substantively: TBI/Flu in PTCy vs Cy/Bu in 56.7% of control), no multivariable adjustment, no propensity matching. D2 (selection): moderate — both groups enrolled consecutively but different intrinsic indication (MMUD vs MRD). D3 (classification of interventions): moderate — interventions well-defined. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): moderate — heterogeneous prophylaxis combinations within PTCy arm (Tac or CsA, +/- MTX). D5 (missing data): moderate — no CMV, infection, IFI data reported. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate — GvHD scored by 2 clinicians per modified Keystone/NIH; objective survival outcomes. D7 (reported result selection): moderate — primary endpoint defined a priori but multiple statistical tests reported. Overall: serious due to confounding and lack of adjustment for major imbalances (donor type, disease risk distribution, conditioning regimen).

Prospective PTCy cohort vs historical ATG control at single Russian center. D1 (confounding): serious — historical comparison spans 2010-2013 (ATG) vs 2013-2015 (PTCy), with possible temporal changes in supportive care, donor selection, and HLA-matching distribution (10/10 frequency differs significantly p=0.012). D2 (selection): moderate — both groups derived from same single-center URD population but allocation by era. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — PTCy/tacrolimus/MMF vs ATG/CNI/MTX-or-MMF clear, but ATG dose details and agent (rabbit vs other) not explicitly specified. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing outcomes data): low — outcomes appear comprehensively reported. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — clinical-only ascertainment for IFI, no systematic CMV pre-emptive monitoring threshold reported, follow-up unequal between arms (PTCy 322 d vs ATG 1146 d). D7 (selective reporting): low — primary and secondary endpoints clearly pre-specified per NCT02294552. Multivariable adjustment performed but residual confounding likely.

Prospective pilot of PTCy70 (n=41) compared with contemporary (Jan 2021-Jun 2024) non-randomized PTCy100 cohort (n=132) at same single center. D1 (confounding): moderate - groups not balanced for conditioning intensity (PTCy70 had more RIC, p=0.01) and follow-up duration differs substantially (7.1 vs 24.1 mo); multivariable analysis adjusted only for conditioning intensity. D2 (selection): moderate - consecutive AML MUD patients in pilot; comparator drawn from contemporary historical cohort. D3 (intervention classification): low - clear PTCy70 vs PTCy100 dose distinction. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low - prospective protocol. D5 (missing data): moderate - short follow-up of PTCy70 cohort precludes assessment of chronic GVHD, 2-yr outcomes. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standardized outcome definitions, blinded ascertainment not described but objective endpoints. D7 (selection of reported result): low - prespecified pilot endpoints reported. Overall: moderate ROBINS-I.

Retrospective single-center cohort 2013-2018 at Saint-Antoine Paris. Substantial baseline imbalance: PT-Cy group has 86% haplo donors vs 0.5% in no-PT-Cy arm; conditioning intensity differs (more sequential in PT-Cy); higher DRI in PT-Cy. Donor type and PT-Cy use are tightly confounded - authors explicitly note inability to adjust for donor type in multivariable analysis. ATG used in both arms (87% PT-Cy, 99.5% no-PT-Cy) further complicates interpretation. Outcome ascertainment (cardiac events) appears robust with systematic monitoring, but GVHD/survival outcomes assessed by clinical care only. No selection or missing data issues described.

ROBINS-I retrospective single-center cohort. D1 (confounding): SERIOUS - the two dose groups are temporally non-overlapping (100 mg/kg 2014-2019; 70 mg/kg 2020-2022), and letermovir prophylaxis was given to 85% of the 70 mg/kg arm but 0% of the 100 mg/kg arm. Era-confounded changes in supportive care (letermovir, CMV monitoring, evolving cardiac monitoring intensity) cannot be disentangled from PT-Cy dose. Authors acknowledge this. D2 (selection of participants): SERIOUS - selection criterion (age >=65 OR cardiac comorbidity) was applied only in the reduced-dose era; the standard-dose arm includes patients who would have qualified for reduced dose if the policy had existed earlier, but no propensity matching or formal adjustment performed. D3 (classification of interventions): LOW - PT-Cy total dose is unambiguously documented and contemporaneously coded as part of GVHD prophylaxis protocol. D4 (deviation from intended interventions): LOW - the study reports per-protocol regimens; deviations are not reported. D5 (missing data): MODERATE - HCT-CI missing in 1/33 patient (3%) of 70 mg/kg arm; follow-up duration markedly different (median 17 vs 59 months) - analyses censored at 2 years which partly mitigates differential follow-up but cannot fully address right-censoring bias for late events. D6 (measurement of outcome): MODERATE - GVHD grading is clinical and unblinded; cardiac events were ascertained by routine cardiac monitoring in BOTH arms per authors but the monitoring policy may have evolved. Infection ascertainment by twice-weekly qPCR is uniform. D7 (selection of reported result): LOW - all pre-specified endpoints in Tables 2-4 appear reported. Overall judgement = SERIOUS, driven by D1 (era confounding with letermovir) and D2 (non-temporally-overlapping comparison).

Single-center phase II prospective trial with historical control comparator (CSA/MTX 2005-2018 vs PTCy 2018-2022). D1 (confounding): serious - era effect (13-year span vs 4-year span), changes in supportive care, donor type imbalance (PTCy cohort has many more MMUD), and acknowledged by authors. D2 (selection): moderate - both cohorts from prospective phase II trials at same institution; eligibility criteria similar but PTCy allowed age up to 60 vs 55 for CSA/MTX. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - prophylaxis regimens clearly defined. D4 (deviations): low - prospective protocol adherence. D5 (missing data): moderate - some missing comorbidity and performance status data in CSA/MTX cohort. D7 (outcome reporting): moderate - GVHD grading system not explicitly stated; cGVHD endpoint operationally defined as 'requiring IST' rather than NIH consensus. Overall: serious risk due to confounding by era and donor-type imbalance, despite multivariable adjustment for some confounders. medRxiv preprint not peer-reviewed.

Single-center retrospective sequential cohort study spanning 1999-2020 with three different consecutive GVHD prophylaxis eras. Confounding (D1) serious: sequential eras differ substantially in patient mix (HCT-CI-age, EBMT score, DRI, donor type, conditioning) with the PTCy-Tac group enriched for high-risk DRI (43%) and mismatched donors (43%); also differ in supportive care and CMV prophylaxis era. Selection (D2) serious: era effect confounded with prophylaxis allocation. Classification of interventions (D3) moderate: prophylaxis regimens well-defined. Deviations from intended (D4) low. Missing data (D5) moderate: limited per-arm reporting of D+100 GVHD outcomes (only overall reported at D+100; per-arm at 200 days). Outcome measurement (D6) low: standard endpoints. Selective reporting (D7) moderate: per-arm CI reporting incomplete for some primary timepoints. Overall risk SERIOUS due to era confounding and incomplete per-timepoint per-arm reporting.

Prospective phase 2 non-randomized trial (NCT01010217). Two parallel arms assigned based on donor availability + physician preference (not randomized) creating potential confounding (D1 moderate). Selection: enrolled prospectively per protocol; D2 moderate due to non-random arm assignment. Intervention classification clear (D3 low). Deviations from intended interventions minimal: prespecified protocol amendment for MMF extension after 11 patients showed early aGVHD; reported transparently (D4 low). Missing data: standard transplant cohort follow-up; D5 low. Outcome ascertainment by separate research team using CIBMTR criteria (D6 low). Reported outcomes pre-specified per protocol (D7 low). Overall moderate due to non-randomization and donor-source assignment confounding.

Single-center retrospective cohort (n=107) drawn from 552 alloHCTs. D1 (confounding) serious: substantial baseline imbalance — PTCy arm includes 33% haplo (vs 0% in TAC/MTX) and shorter follow-up (19 vs 46 mo); donor type strongly confounds GVHD prophylaxis assignment. D2 (selection): moderate — patient selection criteria are clear but consecutive eligibility within institutional protocol-driven era effect. D3 (classification): moderate — GVHD prophylaxis assignment likely era-driven (PTCy adoption); short follow-up in PTCy may underestimate cGVHD/NRM. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate — MRD assessed in 45/45+ AML patients but not all; HCT-CI, KPS partly missing. D6/D7 not applicable for ROBINS-I (overall judgement reflected in d6/d7 marked low as placeholder per template). Overall: SERIOUS due to confounding.

Single-institutional prospective phase 1/2 trial with planned 3+3 dose deescalation and Simon two-stage phase 2 design; pilot DL1 cohort (n=5) provides directly comparative HD-PTCy data but was not randomized and is small. Confounding (D1) is moderate as the dose-level groups differ in enrollment timing and were sequentially enrolled. Selection (D2) and intervention classification (D3) are low. Deviations (D4) low (per-protocol). Missing data (D5) moderate given small n and per-protocol replacement of patients not evaluable for primary endpoint. Outcome measurement (D6) moderate as some endpoints (BK virus monitoring, immune reconstitution) were unblinded. Selection of reported result (D7) low (registered trial, primary endpoint pre-specified).

Retrospective single-center cohort, n=117. D1 confounding: moderate - donor-type comparison is unmatched and unadjusted for important confounders (age, conditioning intensity, era - haplo enrolled 2013 onward while non-haplo enrolled later). D2 selection: moderate - consecutive enrollment but variable follow-up and different median follow-up by group (851 vs 526 days). D3 classification of interventions: low - well-documented uniform PTCy/tacrolimus regimen across all donor types. D4 deviations: low - protocol-driven supportive care. D5 missing data: moderate - some outcomes (CMV subgroups by serostatus) reported but denominators not always specified. D6 measurement of outcomes: low - infection definitions are clear and microbiologically/clinically defined; CMV by routine PCR screening; aGvHD/cGvHD by published consensus criteria. D7 selection of reported result: low - prespecified primary objective (IRM by donor type). Overall moderate risk of bias.

Prospective single-center cohort study (n=36) comparing PTCy vs ATG in unrelated donor HSCT, with treatment allocation determined either by randomization within concurrent RCT (NCT03818334) OR clinician choice - leading to serious risk of confounding (d1). Selection bias (d2) is serious because allocation mechanism is mixed (RCT + clinical preference) and not all consecutive patients randomly assigned. Classification of intervention (d3): moderate since PTCy/ATG protocols are clearly defined. Deviations from intended interventions (d4): low. Missing data (d5): moderate (small N, possible loss to follow-up not described). Measurement of outcomes (d6): moderate (immune reconstitution outcomes by flow cytometry, clinical endpoints by chart review with no blinding). Reporting bias (d7): low (predefined outcomes). Primary focus is on immune reconstitution, with limited clinical outcome data; small sample size (16 vs 20) limits inferential statistics for clinical endpoints.

Retrospective single-center cohort with non-randomized assignment to ATG vs ATG/PTCy based on staff physician preference (some implemented ATG/PTCy for research purposes, others adhered to conventional ATG practice) - serious concern for confounding (D1). Significant temporal imbalance: ATG/PTCy concentrated in 2017-2020 (68.8%) while ATG concentrated in 2020-2023 (71.7%, P=0.001), creating era-confounded comparison. Conditioning intensity (MAC 28.1% vs 10.9%, P=0.098) and other characteristics generally well-balanced. Multivariate Cox adjusted for age, diagnosis, mEBMT, conditioning, CD34, HSCT timing. Disease ascertainment standardized using uniform conditioning and prophylaxis platforms. GVHD graded by MAGIC criteria. Outcomes complete with 38-mo median FU.

RoB2 assessment for this RCT (NCT03680092). D1 (randomization): computer-generated 1:1 randomization with stratification by donor type and conditioning intensity (RANDI2 software); allocation concealment not explicitly described - some concerns. D2 (deviations from intended interventions): open-label, single-center trial; trial was amended midway after FDA approval of Aba in Dec 2021 with only PTCy+Aba arm enrolling thereafter, leading to imbalanced final n (25 vs 15) and very different cohort composition (more advanced disease in PTCy+Aba arm); 2 SOC patients excluded due to insurance issues - HIGH risk of bias for assignment effects given midstudy change. D3 (missing outcome data): minimal loss to follow-up, all patients followed 1 year - low. D4 (measurement of outcome): GVHD graded by NIH consensus and Glucksberg criteria; primary endpoint clinical but open-label assessment - low (objective endpoints). D5 (selection of reported result): trial registered prospectively (NCT03680092) and met its prespecified primary endpoint; protocol amendment was transparent - some concerns due to small sample and amendment. Overall HIGH risk of bias driven by midstudy amendment causing imbalanced arms and inability to fully account for unbalanced disease risk; randomization was not preserved for the entire enrolled cohort.

Single-center prospective study with non-randomized historical control (2015-2019) vs prospective PTCy arms (2019-2024). Bias due to confounding (D1) is serious because control group has significantly different baseline (younger, more lymphoma, more MAC; no letermovir prophylaxis in control group whereas 30/63 in study). Selection (D2) moderate (consecutive treated patients but non-contemporary groups). Classification of interventions (D3) moderate as 2 PTCy doses were sequentially escalated (15 then 25 mg/kg). Missing data (D5) moderate (D+100 chimerism only in 41/63 study, 23/31 control). Measurement (D6) moderate; reporting (D7) low (all primary endpoints reported). Overall judgement serious due to historical comparator confounding.

Retrospective single-center study with sequential cohorts: PTCY arm enrolled 08/2014-05/2017, PTCY+ATG arm enrolled 05/2017-03/2019 with concomitant change of conditioning regimen (Baltimore-based vs CloB2A1). D2 (deviations from intended interventions) and bias due to time-period confounding are serious because the PTCY arm received Baltimore-based RIC (mostly clo-Baltimore) while PTCY+ATG received CloB2A1, making it impossible to disentangle the effect of ATG addition from the effect of the changed conditioning. Outcome ascertainment is clinical with standard definitions but follow-up duration differs by 19 months between arms. Small sample size (n=58 total), no multivariable adjustment for outcomes. Disease risk index and most baseline characteristics were balanced but CD3+ T cell graft dose differed significantly between arms (higher in PTCY+ATG).

Single-center retrospective cohort, n=33 total (very small). D1 (confounding): serious - regimen choice based on era/clinical judgement and groups differ in median follow-up (15 vs 26 mo) and disease composition (AML 43.8% vs 76.5%, ALL 31.3% vs 5.9%). No multivariable adjustment for confounders. D2 (selection): moderate - all eligible patients in time window enrolled. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - regimen well-defined. D4 (deviations): moderate. D5 (missing data): moderate - excluded patients with missing outcome documentation. D6 (measurement of outcomes): moderate - aGVHD/cGVHD adjudication subjective, no blinding. D7 (selection of reported result): moderate. Overall: serious risk of bias due to small sample, confounding by indication, and lack of adjustment.

Prospective non-randomized equivalence trial (NCT02294552), single center (Pavlov St Petersburg). Assignment to arms based on available donor type/HLA match, not random — confounding by indication is intrinsic (D1 moderate). Selection (D2) and intervention classification (D3) low. Outcomes assessed per pre-specified protocol with standardized criteria (D4 low). Some deviations: salvage prevalence differs by arm (16/23/29%), conditioning intensity also differs across arms (D5 moderate). Missing data unlikely (D6 low). Outcome measurement standardized across arms. Reporting follows protocol; some discrepancy between figure 13.1% NRM and text 17% for MMG (D7 moderate).

Single-center prospective observational study from Osaka City University. D1 (confounding): serious - allocation to graft type driven by donor availability and patient/clinician choice; substantial baseline imbalances in disease risk (PTCy-haplo arm had 49% high + 21% very high DRI vs 18% high + 6% very high in MRD), conditioning intensity (97% RIC in PTCy-haplo vs 41% RIC in MRD), and graft source (100% PBSC vs 76% PBSC+24% BM in MRD); no adjustment for confounding in primary group comparisons. D2 (selection): moderate - patients excluded post-enrollment for early relapse/graft failure/withdrawal (11/121) but this is uniform across groups. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - regimens well-described but reduced-dose PTCy 25 mg/kg x 2 is non-standard. D4 (deviations): low - prospective consent and uniform supportive care manual. D5 (missing data): moderate - small subgroups (especially MRD n=17) limit power. D6 (measurement): moderate - GVHD diagnosed clinically with histology when possible (standard). D7 (selective reporting): low - all pre-specified outcomes reported. Overall: serious.

ROBINS-I applied (no concurrent comparator arm; single-arm phase 2 trial PHYLOS). D1 (confounding): moderate - no comparator arm so unmeasured confounding cannot be assessed against an internal control; pre-specified eligibility criteria (AML CR1/CR2 or MDS, 18-65y, no MSD/MUD available) provide some standardization but selection by absence of suitable matched donor introduces structural confounding for indirect comparisons. D2 (selection): low - prospective consecutive enrollment across 26 GITMO centers (81 screened, 77 evaluable), eligibility well-defined, EUROCT registered. D3 (intervention classification): low - PTCy + CSA/Tac + MMF protocol uniformly delivered to all enrolled patients per protocol. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low - uniform MAC (Bu4Flu) conditioning and PTCy 50 mg/kg D+3/+4; CSA vs Tac choice institutional but both CNI. D5 (missing data): low - 77/77 evaluable for primary endpoint; CMV serostatus missing in 9 (11.7%) - minor. D6 (measurement of outcomes): low - Glucksberg criteria for aGVHD, NIH consensus for cGVHD, EBMT/standard definitions; safety per CTCAE 4.03; protocol pre-specified primary endpoint. D7 (selection of the reported result): low - primary endpoint and secondary endpoints reported as pre-specified per protocol; CONSORT-like figure with all enrolled patients tracked. Overall judgement: moderate (driven by single-arm design preventing internal causal comparison and inherent selection of patients lacking matched donors). This study is excluded from PTCy MA outcome pooling per single-arm exclusion rule but ROBINS-I is recorded for completeness.

Retrospective single-center sequential cohort comparison of standard-dose PTCy (n=59, 2017 onwards) vs reduced-dose PTCy (n=48, after March 2018 selectively, all from September 2023). D1 (confounding): serious - allocation was non-random based on clinical criteria (cardiac comorbidity, low CD34, MF) until Sep 2023, leading to substantial baseline imbalance (reduced-dose arm older, more MF, more advanced disease, more MUDs). No multivariable adjustment shown for treatment effect estimates. D2 (selection): moderate - sequential consecutive enrollment, but selection criteria for reduced-dose arm shifted mid-study. D3 (measurement of intervention): low - both regimens clearly defined. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): low - 107 consecutive patients. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - retrospective ascertainment, no blinding, but standardized definitions used. D7 (selective reporting): low. Overall: serious due to confounding by indication.

Retrospective registry-based study from EBMT ALWP. D1 (confounding): moderate - significant imbalance between groups in donor type, age, conditioning intensity, graft source, ATG use; multivariate adjustment attempts to handle key confounders but residual confounding likely. D2 (selection): serious - patients selected from registry; allocation to PT-Cy alone vs +1IS vs +2IS strongly center-driven and confounded with donor type (group 1 dominated by MSD/BM/no ATG; group 3 dominated by UD/PBSC/ATG). D3 (intervention classification): moderate - GVHD prophylaxis well-defined as 3 categories but ATG dose/agent heterogeneous and unbalanced. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - some KPS/CMV missing; outcomes reasonably complete. D6 (measurement of outcome): moderate - registry-reported GVHD grading subject to interobserver variability across 150 centers. D7 (selective reporting): moderate. Overall serious risk of bias for the within-PTCy comparison primarily due to severe confounding by donor type, graft source, and ATG use.

Retrospective EBMT registry analysis. D1 confounding: moderate - significant baseline imbalances by donor type (age, secondary AML, conditioning, BM/PB, in vivo TCD, GVHD prophylaxis composition); MVA performed and frailty (center) effect included but residual confounding likely (PTCy combination drugs and TCD strongly correlated with donor type and could not be evaluated). D2 selection bias: moderate - registry-based, voluntary EBMT reporting. D3 classification of intervention: low - all received PTCy. D4 deviations: low. D5 missing data: moderate - cytogenetic risk missing in 410/1239 (33%), CMV missing 48, PerformanceStatus missing 59. D6/D7: low.

EBMT ALWP retrospective registry study. D1 (confounding): moderate - groups not randomized, important difference in calendar year/era (2017 vs 2015) and follow-up; conditioning intensity and CIS combinations differ at trend level; Cox model with center frailty adjusts for major variables but unmeasured confounders include ATG pharmacokinetics, MRD status, time of CIS withdrawal. D2 (selection): moderate - inclusion based on registry availability of detailed GvHD prophylaxis data which may not be at random. D3 (intervention classification): low - PTCy vs PTCy+ATG is objective. D4 (deviations from intended interventions): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - some variables (HCT-CI 78/62 missing; ATG formulation 41 missing) but key outcomes available. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standard EBMT criteria. D7 (selection of reported result): low - prespecified outcomes. Overall moderate.

Small case series (n=11) compared to a historical control cohort (n=57) from the same center receiving standard-dose PTCy. Selection of intermediate-dose for vulnerable patients (advanced age, splenomegaly, cardiac comorbidity, fungal infection, prior HSCT, MSD) introduces confounding by indication (D1: serious). Time period 2023-2024 differs from historical cohort with attendant differences in supportive care/letermovir era (D3: serious). Outcomes ascertained by chart review; engraftment definitions standard. Few outcomes reported and very small N produce wide uncertainty.

Prospective single-center cohort with two comparator groups (contemporary matched-pair and historical). D1 (confounding): serious — historical control cohort (C) introduces calendar-time confounding (2014-2015 vs 2015-2016); matched-pair cohort (B) controlled for 5 variables (age, sex, disease, disease status, HLA disparity) but residual confounding likely (e.g., donor type within haplo, conditioning details). Cohort A uses maternal/collateral donors which are themselves high-GVHD-risk donors, while Cohort B uses other haplo relatives — donor type itself differs systematically. D2 (selection): moderate — Cohort A was prospectively enrolled; Cohorts B and C selected retrospectively. D3 (intervention classification): moderate — PTCy administration well-defined but timing/dose unusual (14.5 mg/kg x 2, not standard 50 mg/kg). D4 (deviations): low — all 40 study patients completed prescribed therapy. D5 (missing data): moderate — short follow-up in Cohorts A and B (303, 342 days median) limits assessment of long-term outcomes. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate — aGVHD diagnosis adjudicated by 5 blinded experts (strength); cGVHD per NIH 2014 criteria. D7 (selective reporting): low — predefined endpoints (NCT02412423). Overall: serious risk of bias due to non-randomized comparisons with potential donor-type and era confounding.

Single-arm prospective phase II trial with historical control group from same institution. D1 (confounding): serious - PTCy and historical groups differ substantially in conditioning regimen (Flu-Bu4 vs Bu-Cy, P<0.001), donor distribution (more MSD/haplo in PTCy, more MUD in historical, P<0.001), and time period (post-2013 vs pre-2013); no propensity matching or multivariable adjustment. D2 (selection): moderate - patients selected sequentially based on eligibility criteria, but historical control selection unclear. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - protocolized GVHD prophylaxis but historical group received mixed regimens (CsA+MTX+MMF for MSD; CsA+MTX+MMF+ATG for MUD). D4 (deviations): low - prospective protocol-driven trial. D5 (missing data): moderate - 31 patients with median follow-up only 18 months (historical 39 months), some outcomes immature. D6 (outcome measurement): moderate - standard GVHD/CMV definitions but unblinded. D7 (selective reporting): moderate - primary endpoint reported but limited infection outcome reporting (no IFI/BSI). Overall: serious risk of bias due to historical comparator, small sample, era effects.

Single-center retrospective non-randomized comparison with historical controls (2015-2020 vs 2020-2021). D1 (confounding) serious: era differences (introduction of newer conditioning Flu-Bu-Mel vs Flu-Bu, post-HSCT maintenance with low-dose decitabine only in PTCy-ATG group), age difference (PTCy-ATG older, P=0.024), disease distribution differences. D2 (selection): serious - landmark analysis from D+100 excludes early NRM (4/77) and PGF (2/77) from PTCy-ATG but landmark also applied to controls; selection of historical comparator from different time era introduces selection bias. D3 (classification of interventions): moderate - regimens well defined per protocol. D4 (deviations): moderate - no detail on protocol adherence. D5 (missing data): low - all enrolled patients reported. D6 (measurement of outcome): low - NIH 2014 cGVHD criteria applied. D7 (selection of reported result): low - primary endpoints clearly defined.

Single-center retrospective cohort with non-contemporaneous arms (standard ATG enrolled 2014-2018; low dose ATG/PTCy enrolled June 2017 onward). Disease risk differences (more AML-CR1 in PTCy group, more MDS-MLD in ATG group). Follow-up imbalance (12.5 vs 23 months). Limited covariate adjustment described. Outcomes objectively assessed but selective reporting concern given some outcomes only narratively described. PBSC+UCB co-infusion adds complexity.

Single-center retrospective matched-pair pilot. D1 (confounding): serious - propensity-score matched on disease type/status, HLA matching, donor age, conditioning intensity, CD3+ count but key unmeasured confounders include letermovir use (15/21 vs 0/42), prophylactic G-CSF (10/21 vs 0/42), and substantial era effect (study group 2019-2021 vs control 2015-2018). D2 (selection): moderate - all consecutive eligible patients receiving PT-Cy+ATLG enrolled prospectively; controls drawn from prior era with same inclusion criterion. D3 (intervention classification): moderate - protocol clearly defined per institutional practice. D4 (deviations): low. D5 (missing data): moderate - shorter median FU in study group (538d vs 1450d) limits long-term outcomes. D6 (outcome measurement): low - standard NIH/IBMTR criteria. D7 (selective reporting): moderate - no pre-registered SAP visible. Overall serious due to era confounding and letermovir/G-CSF imbalance.

RCT (ChiCTR2200058591) with simple 1:1 randomization across 4 centers; allocation concealment and blinding not specified. D2 (deviations from intended intervention): some concerns because the two arms differ in multiple co-interventions beyond GVHD prophylaxis (conditioning regimen: FBA vs modified BuCy/ATG; graft source: PBSC alone vs G-BM+PBSC mixture; rituximab on d+5 in PTCy/ATG arm only; MTX in standard arm only). Authors acknowledge these as 'confounding factors'. D1 (randomization): low. D3 (missing data): low (no loss to follow-up). D4 (outcome measurement): low. D5 (selection of reported result): low for primary endpoint, defined a priori in protocol.

D1 (randomization): centralized 24-hour internet-based randomization with allocation concealment described - low risk. D2 (deviations from intended interventions): masking described as research staff, clinical teams, and patients were masked to randomization and treatment allocation, but given the markedly different protocols (PTCy + low-dose ATG + CsA/MMF vs ATG + CsA/MMF/MTX) full masking of clinical teams is implausible - some concerns. D3 (missing outcome data): no loss to follow-up, complete analysis of all 104 - low risk. D4 (measurement of outcome): aGVHD/cGVHD per Glucksberg/NIH 2014; outcomes assessor blinding not stated and asymmetric rituximab use confounds EBV reactivation - some concerns. D5 (selection of reported result): primary endpoint pre-specified, sample size justified, trial registered (ChiCTR2200056979) - low risk. Overall: some concerns, primarily from implausibility of blinding given highly different regimens (PTCy and MTX administration) and asymmetric rituximab prophylaxis between arms acknowledged as limitation by authors.

RoB2 assessment for the Zu 2023 multicenter RCT (ChiCTR2200056979): D1 (randomization process) some_concerns — patients randomized 1:1 but allocation concealment, sequence generation method, and baseline imbalance handling not described (notably HLA allele-mismatch imbalance 48.8% vs 30.0%, P=0.047, was not addressed by stratification). D2 (deviations from intended interventions) some_concerns — open-label design; PTCy-ATG arm received prophylactic rituximab while quadruplet ATG arm did not, introducing a co-intervention imbalance that confounds EBV outcomes. D3 (missing outcome data) low — 160/162 enrolled with completeness suggested by CONSORT-like reporting in supplementary figure. D4 (measurement of outcome) some_concerns — outcomes mostly objective (engraftment, viral reactivation by PCR), but GVHD grading and adjudication blinding not specified. D5 (selection of reported result) some_concerns — pre-specified outcomes not fully described in the manuscript (correspondence format limits Methods detail); ChiCTR registry referenced but pre-specified primary endpoint not stated in main text. Overall: some_concerns.
